billions:S01E01.title: Pilot
billions:S01E01.summary: Ari Spyros of the SEC brings US Attorney Chuck Rhoades a suspicious trading pattern in Pepsum Pharmaceuticals that links three small funds to billionaire Bobby 'Axe' Axelrod. Chuck, who is 81 and 0 on financial prosecutions, refuses to move until he is sure he can win, partly because his wife Wendy is the in-house performance coach at Axe Capital. Chuck and his father set a trap: they warn Axe off buying an $83 million beach house next to Chuck Sr.'s place and plant a rival bidder, betting a guilty man will buy it out of pride. Axe, tipped by his fixer Hall that a former employee has flipped, feeds a reporter a story about rival fund manager Steven Birch to redirect attention. Axe buys the house anyway, the Post puts it on the front page, and Hall reports that a case file has likely been opened on him.

billions:S01E02.title: Naming Rights
billions:S01E02.summary: The Birch story Axe fed to the press breaks, and Chuck's office is pulled into chasing Birch until Chuck works out that the story is a decoy and settles fast to get back to Axe. Axe stages a fake SEC raid on his own firm, fires trader Victor publicly to show investors he is clean, and then needs Wendy to stop Victor from taking revenge. Hall blackmails Tara Mohr, a Justice Department staffer, into spying on Chuck's office. Axe's lawyer Orrin Bach sets out the defensive strategy: posture as someone who would never settle in order to win a better settlement. Axe ends the episode buying the naming rights to a concert hall from the financially desperate Eads family, and cuts their payment at the last minute to settle a childhood grudge.

billions:S01E03.title: YumTime
billions:S01E03.summary: Axe takes a 4.9% stake in the snack company YumTime and launches an activist campaign, wins over the board chairman Jerome Purkheiser, ousts CEO Hutch Bailey III and removes board member Evelyn Benson, who is Chuck Sr.'s mistress, as a message to the Rhoades family. Chuck trades one of his deputy Lonnie's biggest cases to the Eastern District to take back control of the Pete Decker investigation, and has to accept Spyros embedded with his team as part of the price. His bluff to Decker fails, so Connerty finds a pressure point: Decker trades his elderly parents' accounts, and Chuck threatens to arrest them at their grandson's Little League game. Lara Axelrod quietly squeezes June, a 9/11 widow, into cutting a damaging chapter from her memoir. Wags keeps a portfolio manager, Maria Saldana, who used an outside offer as leverage, but plans to punish her slowly.

billions:S01E04.title: Short Squeeze
billions:S01E04.summary: Axe has an Axe Capital manager short Cross-Co Trucking and then uses his new YumTime board seat as YumTime prepares to drop Cross-Co's contract. Chuck Sr., working with a prime broker executive, learns of the short from the stock loan desk and engineers a squeeze: the broker recalls the shares, an analyst upgrades the stock and a rumoured takeover pushes the price up. Axe identifies who is behind it, pays his rival Ken Malverne a 25% premium to borrow shares, and holds until YumTime announces it is dropping Cross-Co. Chuck, warned by Spyros, forces his father to sit on the position until it is worthless so there is no profit to prosecute, and extracts concessions from Spyros in return. Chuck catches Tara Mohr and turns her against Hall, while Decker's proffer gives the prosecutors 'Dollar' Bill Stearn instead of Axe. A friend at Mundia-Tel tips Axe that the company is a fraud, and Axe orders his team to sell everything.

billions:S01E05.title: The Good Life
billions:S01E05.summary: Axe liquidates the fund slowly, tells Wags to warn investors he is shutting down and disappears to watch films and plan a yacht trip, so the market and his own traders think he is having a breakdown. Wags and Wendy manage the restless floor and make Axe face his oldest investors, and a meeting with police pension chief Raul Gomez reignites him. Connerty places Bill Stearn in Iowa through hotel reward points, and Chuck extracts a signed statement from the Pepsum researcher Stearn bribed. Reporter Mike Dimonda uses a threatened story to turn Lonnie into a source, and publishes an article saying Chuck is going easy on Axe because of Wendy. Chuck responds by speeding up the arrest, and Mundia-Tel collapses just as the FBI walks onto the Axe Capital floor and arrests Stearn.

billions:S01E06.title: The Deal
billions:S01E06.summary: Axe answers Stearn's arrest with a war speech, a $300 million legal war chest and quiet financial support for Stearn's family, and Stearn refuses to cooperate even after Connerty discovers his secret second family. Investors start to leave, the prime broker Axe courts snubs him in public, and Justice Department official Adam DeGiulio presses Chuck to recuse himself because of Wendy. Wendy, now caught between the two men, briefs Chuck on how Axe thinks and then persuades Axe to negotiate. The settlement collapses at the signing when Chuck adds a lifetime trading ban after Axe mocks the $1.9 billion fine, and Axe tears up the check. Chuck then officially recuses himself to save his marriage while privately telling Connerty to keep him informed with no paper trail.

billions:S01E07.title: The Punch
billions:S01E07.summary: After the settlement collapses, Axe punches neighbour Bruce Layner at a Hamptons barbecue for driving his sons home drunk, and a clipped phone video of the punch threatens him with an assault charge, a hostile press cycle and a pension-fund exodus. Axe's fixer Hall works out which teenager filmed it, buys the full uncut video (which shows Layner admitting he drove drunk) and feeds it to reporter Mike Dimonda after Axe buys a one-day hold on the story; Axe becomes a folk hero overnight. Chuck, officially recused, confronts SEC chief Ari Spyros with the woman Spyros once assaulted to force him back into a subordinate role. Donnie Caan, apparently turned by the government, plays the reluctant informant for Connerty, who is appalled that Chuck is still steering the case. Chuck keeps Connerty from quitting with a speech about the people the case is really for, and Wendy starts quietly looking at jobs outside Axe Capital.

billions:S01E08.title: Boasts and Rails
billions:S01E08.summary: Chuck's team raids Donnie at night to squeeze him for evidence on a coming Kemlot trade, while Axe learns from his source that there is an informant inside Axe Capital and launches a very public mole hunt. On Chuck Sr.'s advice the government side fabricates an SEC inquiry file on an innocent trader, Butch 'the Pouch' Probert, and Axe fires him. Kate Sacker obtains a redacted chapter of a biography showing Axe was being fired on the morning of 9/11 and shorted airline stocks as the towers burned; Chuck feeds it to Dimonda, who breaks the story. Chuck tries to move Connerty off the case, is blocked by Adam DeGiulio, then courts and rejects a lucrative offer from a white-shoe firm. The final scene reveals that Donnie is working for Axe: the whole informant arrangement is a show to set the government up on Kemlot.

billions:S01E09.title: Where the F*ck Is Donnie?
billions:S01E09.summary: The 9/11 story turns public opinion against Axe: protesters picket Axe Capital, a symphony hall tries to strip his name off its building, the police pension fund withdraws, and Lara's restaurant is shut down by firefighters. Donnie places the huge Kemlot order on Axe's instructions, but the key conversation about the source happens in a room that blocks the government's wire, and then Donnie vanishes. Chuck lets his informant's progress leak to DeGiulio to keep the case in his office and starts an off-book investigation into Judge Whit Wilcox, who is hostile to his cases. Axe goes to a firehouse and confesses more than the papers printed, while his top traders defect to start a rival fund. Donnie finally resurfaces, names an FDA official as Axe's source, promises to testify and collapses on the floor of the FBI office.

billions:S01E10.title: Quality of Life
billions:S01E10.summary: Donnie has terminal pancreatic cancer, and Chuck realises Axe used a dying man to plant false evidence that could never be tested in court; the Attorney General hands the Axe case to the Eastern District. A flashback shows Axe offering Donnie a guaranteed 40 million dollars for his family in exchange for playing the double agent. Judge Wilcox dismisses the Dollar Bill case, Chuck confronts him with evidence that he profits from a private prison company, trades a quiet resignation for a promise that the Southern District will not prosecute, then has the Eastern District arrest him at his farewell party. Axe stages a public brawl with Dollar Bill to plant him inside the defectors' new fund Ionosphere, feeds them a false tip that costs them 28 percent, then rescues them on brutal terms. At the end Axe quietly decides not to tell Donnie about a drug trial that could have extended his life long enough to testify.

billions:S01E11.title: The Conversation
billions:S01E11.summary: Axe ignores his analysts and his trader Mafee on BioLance, holds the position through a failed FDA decision and loses more than 400 million dollars. He asks Wendy for a real session, and over a long night she takes him through his guilt over Donnie until he admits he blocked Donnie's treatment and felt relief at his death; Axe in turn guesses she is shopping herself to a rival fund. Chuck trades DeGiulio a federal judgeship for the right to pick DeGiulio's successor, then has to swallow his pride and ask Chuck Sr. to deliver the Senator who can push the nomination through. Chuck's marriage is fraying, he goes to a dominatrix, and a man photographing him is caught outside. Lara, feeling sidelined, reconnects with her sister and her old recklessness.

billions:S01E12.title: Magical Thinking
billions:S01E12.summary: Chuck reads Wendy's session notes on her computer, learns that Axe paid off Greenwich police to bury an automatic weapons incident involving trader Mick Danzig, and routes the tip through returning prosecutor Lonnie Watley so it cannot be traced to him. Axe is warned by a police union ally, deduces the leak came from his session with Wendy, and threatens her with compromising photographs and browsing history; Wendy proves her innocence by playing him a recording of her fight with Chuck, then quits Axe Capital and throws Chuck out. Chuck kills the tainted case, Axe closes a key allocator and restarts his capital raise, and Axe tries to recruit Connerty by telling him how Chuck got the tip. Chuck feeds a fake bugging story to Axe's janitor source, and Axe tears his office to the rivets. The season ends with the two men in the gutted office, each declaring total war.

billions:S02E01.title: Risk Management
billions:S02E01.summary: Axe Capital reopens after Chuck's flooding of the office, and Axe announces a lockdown: no electronics, ID bracelets, and every pitch to him must happen in front of his new chief of staff, Stephanie Reed. Oliver Dake of the Office of Professional Responsibility arrives to investigate Chuck's conduct on the aborted Axelrod case and quickly finds the $5 million payment Axe made to Wendy on the day Chuck dropped the case. Chuck uses a chess parable at a farewell dinner to signal to his ambitious AUSAs that loyalty will be rewarded with the vacant Head of Crim job. Wendy, now separated from Chuck and out of Axe Capital, is courted by Todd Krakow and refuses Axe's plea to come back. Axe, inspired by a cop story about numbers, buys up the claims of everyone Chuck has wronged and serves him with 127 lawsuits at once, while the Attorney General summons Chuck to Washington to fire him and Dake reveals to Connerty that he knows Connerty made the tip call.

billions:S02E02.title: Dead Cat Bounce
billions:S02E02.summary: Axe humiliates Krakow on a Spartan-Ives panel for trying to poach Wendy, then intern Taylor Mason reverse-engineers Krakow's satellite research to find that a Chinese chip factory is a fake built to fool the satellites, leading Axe to short Anata-Tek and drive it down by half. Chuck, three days from being fired, orders his office to find a case too big and bold to fire him over; when the Attorney General rejects the GoodStop case as a gift for his successor, he reverses course and lets it leak that he is investigating Spartan-Ives, a friend of the administration, so firing him would look like obstruction. Dake questions Wendy about the payment and offers Axe immunity if he will testify the $5 million was a bribe. Axe keeps Taylor with a flexible, prorated million-dollar deal, and starts Wags looking for a way to change Axe's standing, starting with an NFL franchise. Boyd, now Chuck's target, asks Axe to teach him how to beat Rhoades.

billions:S02E03.title: Optimal Play
billions:S02E03.summary: Chuck's team uses a Spartan-Ives flight attendant's small, legal trade to frighten her into recording Boyd on the corporate jet, catching him with the wife of managing director Tom McKinnon, and Chuck then turns the humiliated McKinnon into an informant on Treasury bid-rigging. Axe helps Boyd find a lawyer and explains to Lara that Boyd is a scout whose fight will teach Axe how to beat Chuck. At the Alpha Cup charity poker tournament, Axe drops Dollar Bill for Taylor, bets Krakow a million that Taylor will outlast him, and Taylor wins with a ten-high call after Krakow goes on tilt; Krakow's attempt to use Wendy as his coach backfires. Axe is told the NFL does not want him to bid and responds by raising his bid, while he quietly buys every signed Churchill first edition, including the set Chuck has had to sell.

billions:S02E04.title: The Oath
billions:S02E04.summary: Axe pursues the NFL team by staging a Giving Oath pledge with billionaire Sanford Bensinger for the headlines, while a rival bidder's legal problems are leaked to the league. Chuck, whose informant McKinnon reports that Boyd has stopped rigging bids, sends Connerty to execute a search warrant and then meets Boyd to ask a favor, offering him an easy way out; Boyd sacrifices a few mid-level staff and, feeling safe, restarts the bid-rigging. Dake presses Connerty to turn on Chuck and is rebuffed. Lara destroys a competing IV-drip business by planting a worker in it who gets it busted for pimping, Wendy assesses an astronaut candidate for billionaire Craig Heidecker, and Marc from Sandicot pitches Axe a distressed muni-bond deal tied to a casino. In the deposition for Axe's civil suit, Chuck's lawyer Ira nearly corners Axe, and Axe learns mid-break that Bensinger has exposed the Oath stunt and the NFL has rejected him.

billions:S02E05.title: Currency
billions:S02E05.summary: Facing his first down quarter after a supplier failure hits Sansomic, Axe bets big on a devaluation of the Nigerian naira, recruiting rivals Krakow, Malverne and Steven Birch to reach a $5 billion threshold; Birch, who has worked out that Axe used him as a stalking horse, betrays the group and warns the banks. Axe refuses to back down, keeps Krakow and Malverne in by offering to buy their positions, and gets Lawrence Boyd to endorse the trade on television even though Axe knows Boyd is about to be arrested. Chuck waits for McKinnon to produce, and a drunken dinner at Ai Fiori ends with Boyd confessing on the wire that he ordered the bid-rigging restarted, leading to his arrest. Axe secures the casino location from Donald Thayer by giving him a car and a risk-free stake in the muni deal, Wendy pulls Wags out of a spiral, and Axe fires his chief of staff and refuses Wags's resignation.

billions:S02E06.title: Indian Four
billions:S02E06.summary: Boyd, out on bail, lets Hall buy back the cooperating witness Michael Arendt with quarterly payments and an implied threat, and Chuck's case suddenly rests on a single recording. Connerty uses jury selection to show Boyd what a jury of ordinary New Yorkers thinks of banker bonuses, Boyd folds, and Chuck refuses the plea until the Attorney General calls, at which point he trades acceptance for her promise never to meddle in his office, which kills Dake's investigation mid-interview. Wendy, having learned from Ira how badly the lawsuits are hurting Chuck, returns to Axe Capital on her own terms and makes Axe drop the suits, which Axe admits he had planned for. Axe personally closes a holdout landowner, Hank Flagg, for $5 million and a motorcycle, then leases the land to Thayer, only to learn the gaming license has gone to the Catskills after Chuck's father, who had investigators trail Axe's lieutenants to Sandicot, called in a political favor. Chuck learns Wendy went back to Axe and calls it a deal breaker.

billions:S02E07.title: Victory Lap
billions:S02E07.summary: Sandicot loses its gaming license at the last minute, leaving Axe exposed to a default that could cost him half a billion dollars. Axe convenes a war room, traces the switch from state senator Joe Scolari to the Governor and then to the Albany power broker Black Jack Foley, and finally orders full austerity: seize every asset the town owns. Chuck, riding high after the Boyd conviction, starts exploring a run for governor with his father, who tells him he must first be anointed by Foley and win him with a clerkship for Foley's granddaughter. Chuck gets Connerty to confess that he called the OPR, denies him the Head of Crim job and dares him to stay and prove his loyalty. Wendy's session with trader Mick Danzig ends with Danzig quitting over Sandicot, and Wendy and Chuck open their marriage to other people.

billions:S02E08.title: The Kingmaker
billions:S02E08.summary: Foley, angry that Chuck did not deliver the clerkship, throws his support to Buffalo mayor Bob Sweeney, and it emerges that Foley moved the casino license as a favour to Chuck Sr. Chuck has Ira dig up oppo research and uses letters from Sweeney's son's conversion camp to force Sweeney out of the race, after which Foley summons Chuck and agrees to make him governor. Axe hunts for Foley's motive: he tries to buy out Foley's scrap-metal supplier, then maneuvers Foley into a room through a charity man-of-the-year award and learns the strike was a favour to someone else. Wags plays a rival prime broker off Spartan-Ives to win a 20 percent fee cut. Axe storms the Yale Club to taunt Chuck and his father, which Chuck reads as a sign that Axe is spiralling and can be induced into a mistake.

billions:S02E09.title: Sic Transit Imperium
billions:S02E09.summary: It is Axe's birthday. Chuck tours Sandicot as the town's defender while Connerty chases the bribery angle, until Connerty's leverage play on casino developer Donald Thayer runs into protection that leads back to Chuck Sr., and Chuck quietly shuts the Sandicot line down. Dollar Bill brings Axe a short on the Belgian carmaker Klaxon, which Axe publicly declines while he vets the source, Victor Mateo, and then brings Victor back with a satellite fund in exchange for proof of a cover-up. Axe hires Sean Ayles to run a foundation that will clean up his image, and skips his own birthday party to be with Lara. Ira asks Chuck for his father's money for the Ice Juice IPO, and Chuck lets his father dip into Chuck's blind trust to fund it. At the party Wendy lets slip to Lara that the no-sessions policy was her own condition, exposing a lie Axe told his wife.

billions:S02E10.title: With or Without You
billions:S02E10.summary: Lara leaves with the boys and a note saying 'You lied to me', and Axe spends the episode swinging between tender voicemails and threats while Lara confronts Wendy and offers to pay her to disappear. Foley's vetter George Minchak takes Chuck through an exhaustive oppo interview and turns his darkest secret, a boarding-school hazing he later avenged with a baseball bat, into an anti-bullying story. Connerty tails Taylor and tries to recruit them as an informant, and Taylor dismisses him for having no leverage. Taylor rewrites the Klaxon short thesis that other analysts could not support, withholds their signature until Axe makes them head of research, and receives a 500K bonus. Larry Boyd summons Axe to his work-release job and tips him that Chuck Sr. has taken a big stake in Ice Juice.

billions:S02E11.title: Golden Frog Time
billions:S02E11.summary: The Ice Juice IPO prices at 18 dollars and runs past 30 while Axe builds a large short, has Taylor confirm that Chuck Sr. is illiquid and must have borrowed from someone close, and arranges for trace bacteria to be slipped into the product through a chain of people who owe favours. Customers fall ill, the press piles in, and the stock closes at 3.89, wiping out Chuck Sr., Ira and, it turns out, Chuck's entire blind trust. Wendy warns Chuck, then takes a personal allocation in Axe Cap's short. Taylor runs the analyst review, fires the weakest person rather than the lowest-ranked, and Axe hands them 250,000 dollars in cash off the books. The closing reveal shows that Chuck arranged Boyd's release on condition that he feed Axe the Ice Juice tip, and that he engineered Oliver Dake's appointment as Eastern District U.S. Attorney with instructions to watch every Ice Juice store.

billions:S02E12.title: Ball in Hand
billions:S02E12.summary: Boyd, freed, tells Axe he will be arrested that day, and Axe spends the day preparing: shredding files, having Taylor build a fire-sale model and naming Taylor CIO, trying to negotiate a clean surrender, and evading the FBI with decoys. Dake cuts Chuck out of the case, then comes back when Axe slips his net, and Chuck raises his price, including Connerty as lead prosecutor at Eastern and a promise that Ice Juice never tracks back to his family. Chuck tells his father and Ira that the IPO was bait, gets his father to sign an affidavit taking the blame for the trust, and his father disowns him. Axe meets Wendy at their old place, apologises, and is arrested there after Chuck predicted that the last person Axe would reach for was Wendy. In the holding cell, Chuck tells Axe he trapped him and that the 27 million dollars was worth it, and Axe vows to find the thread that will unravel Chuck.

billions:S03E01.title: Tie Goes to the Runner
billions:S03E01.summary: Axe has been indicted over the Ice Juice sabotage, his assets are frozen, and Oliver Dake is prosecuting him from the Eastern District with Bryan Connerty. The new Attorney General, Jock Jeffcoat, keeps Chuck in his job but tells him to go easy on Wall Street and hands him a list of cases to drop. Chuck gets Dake to keep Wendy out of the case in exchange for a favor to be named later, tries to buy Ira's silence with a trust seat, and discovers Black Jack Foley holds proof that Chuck Sr. misused Chuck's trust when Senior tries to pull his backing for Chuck's run for governor. Axe refuses to give up trading until Wendy talks him into it; he signs, the money is unfrozen, and Taylor becomes the public face of Axe Capital, walking into an elite idea dinner with a microchip play.

billions:S03E02.title: The Wrong Maria Gonzalez
billions:S03E02.summary: Axe regrets the trading ban at once and starts looking for ways to trade through friendly outside funds while Wags begs him to hold back. The Axelrod case lands with Judge Funt, a free-market libertarian, so Chuck lines up Judge DeGiulio to ask for the case and then corners Funt to collect an old personal debt, forcing him to recuse. Connerty flips Victor Mateo's housekeeper as a witness, but she is picked up in an immigration sweep and deported, and Jeffcoat refuses to help get her back. A tsunami in Brazil tests Taylor's first days as CIO; Axe barges into the office with a compliance officer at his side, Taylor faces him down, and Axe ends up handing Taylor control of a two billion dollar pool. Dake collects his favor by planting Karl Allerd in Chuck's office.

billions:S03E03.title: A Generation Too Late
billions:S03E03.summary: Axe and Lara sign divorce papers and Axe works out that only about 300 million of his fortune is safe from a government clawback, so he starts building money the government cannot see. He recruits the failing manager Michael Panay as a front, gets the police pension fund to invest with him, and then collects kickbacks in crypto along with signed admissions. He buys Ira Schirmer with 30 million dollars, and Ira turns up at Eastern ready to testify against Chuck, until Dake cuts the meeting short to protect the case. Jeffcoat orders Chuck to prosecute José Lugo, an abused inmate; Chuck leaks the warden's account to the press, but Jeffcoat orders the prosecution anyway, so Chuck sets up a secret war room to pursue the cases he was told to drop. Taylor interviews quants, sees through a rigged candidate Wags put forward, and decides to build Axe Capital's own system.

billions:S03E04.title: Hell of a Ride
billions:S03E04.summary: Connerty finds Chuck Sr.'s Ice Juice investment and its link to Chuck's trust, and Axe's people hand Connerty Ira's affidavit. Chuck tries to win his father over with a warm speech at Yale, fails, and then has Foley threaten Senior's Kingsford casino land, after which Senior gives Connerty a statement that clears Chuck. Axe is voted off the World-Aid charity board, but his public attack on Oscar Langstraat's venture philanthropy fund pushes the board to approve it, which sends up the solar stock Taylor has quietly bought. A rocket carrying tech founder Craig Heidecker explodes, making Taylor's short pay out, and Wags uses a rival's mistress to take the last burial plot in Manhattan.

billions:S03E05.title: Flaw in the Death Star
billions:S03E05.summary: Eastern closes in on Dr. Gilbert, the doctor who advised Axe on the Ice Juice toxin and may have kept a slide with Axe's fingerprints. Axe squeezes Gilbert, and Chuck, working from Wendy's session notes about Donnie Caan, approaches Gilbert separately and offers him a way out that involves physical evidence rather than testimony. Connerty starts digging into Lawrence Boyd's secret release; Chuck's office covers it with backdated case files, and Chuck gets Boyd to name real names by quietly getting Boyd's seized yacht back to him. At Axe Capital, Wendy and Axe settle a feud between Dollar Bill and the new compliance chief Ari Spyros, and Taylor visits Oscar Langstraat in Silicon Valley, where their relationship turns romantic.

billions:S03E06.title: The Third Ortolan
billions:S03E06.summary: Chuck pays an operative to plant the slide in Axe's penthouse, while Axe's lawyer Orrin Bach moves to dismiss the case; Judge DeGiulio gives Connerty one week to produce evidence. The operative pulls out, Chuck fails to blackmail Spyros into spying, and Spyros, on his own initiative, gives Connerty proof of Wendy's Ice Juice short, putting Chuck and Wendy in the line of fire. Axe weighs pleading guilty to save Wendy until Lara talks him out of it, and Connerty offers Chuck and Wendy a deal to plead and cooperate against Axe. Foley tells Wendy that when every choice is a bad one, she should break the stick. Wendy calls Chuck and Axe together at Axe's penthouse and tells them their only goal now is to survive, with Chuck carrying the slide and a search warrant ready.

billions:S03E07.title: Not You, Mr. Dake
billions:S03E07.summary: Judge DeGiulio has given Connerty one week to produce real evidence against Axe for the Ice Juice sabotage, and Chuck, Axe and Wendy are now secretly working together to kill the case and clear Wendy's short. Chuck tells Dr. Ari Gilbert that the incriminating slide is being planted at Axe's house, then has the FBI find it in Gilbert's own fridge, while Axe's side builds a backdated $11 million trading account in Gilbert's name. Wendy works on Mafee, the trader who booked her trade, until he tells investigators he initiated the call to her out of personal feelings, and Hall blackmails a phone company employee so the call records back him up. Connerty's case collapses in court, AG Jeffcoat orders Eastern to drop it and fires Oliver Dake, whose attempt to use his plant in Southern (Karl Allerd) was reported straight to Chuck. Gilbert pleads to five years, Axe Cap takes a $390 million SEC settlement, and Mafee is quietly rewarded.

billions:S03E08.title: All the Wilburys
billions:S03E08.summary: Jack Foley and an ally barge in on Chuck and Wendy's private session with a third party to show Chuck they own him, and order him to resign as US Attorney and run for governor under their management. Wendy tells Chuck to reverse the power dynamic by finding someone Foley has hurt; Chuck rebuilds his alliance with Buffalo mayor Bob Sweeney, gets the dirt on Foley's cheap steel scheme, and has Foley's supplier arrested in front of him to set new terms. Judge DeGiulio then calls in Chuck's open promise and asks him to stay as US Attorney, and Wendy helps Chuck see he prefers the power of the office, so at his own campaign launch he endorses Sweeney for governor instead. Chuck also fires Connerty after lulling him with praise. Back at Axe Cap, Axe clears the board, launches a $20 billion capital raise, takes an insider tip from Treasury Secretary Krakow on natural gas, negotiates Taylor into a delayed billion-dollar book, and resets Lara's fee terms.

billions:S03E09.title: Icebreaker
billions:S03E09.summary: Axe needs a first big investor to relaunch the raise and targets Russian oligarch Grigor Andolov, despite warnings about his violence. Taylor quietly sabotages the first pitch with an ESG strategy, so Axe goes head to head with Grigor himself, matches his aggression, and proves his influence by producing Treasury Secretary Krakow at dinner while refusing to let Grigor contact Krakow directly; Grigor signs. Chuck plans to use the death penalty as leverage to get a lenient plea for José Lugo, a prisoner Jock wants executed, but Lugo is killed by guards on the way to court, and Jock shuts down any prosecution of them. Meanwhile Taylor secretly restarts the quant team off campus, Axe exposes Ben Kim for stealing Dollar Bill's lucky dollar, and Connerty lands a job as FBI Special Counsel.

billions:S03E10.title: Redemption
billions:S03E10.summary: Chuck decides to take down Jock Jeffcoat and starts building a secret case: he trades a front-page scoop to a reporter for every unpublished rumor on Jock, uses Kate's father for background on Texas media deals, and squeezes financier Ashley Cutler off the books until he admits the Jeffcoat brothers laundered cable company kickbacks through Zeb Jeffcoat's church. Jock invites himself to dinner at Chuck and Wendy's and senses Chuck is working on something big. Grigor pulls $1.5 billion from Axe Cap just as the raise is gathering pace, and Axe first negotiates with shady middleman Frotty Anisman, then walks away when Frotty re-trades at the table. Axe instead uses a restaurant favor he did for Taylor to learn about a genomics company and buys half of it from under Taylor's romantic partner Oscar, filling the hole in his balance sheet. Ben Kim finds a merger signal in rental car data, and Grigor puts his money back.

billions:S03E11.title: Kompenso
billions:S03E11.summary: It is bonus day at Axe Cap, and Axe, paying out of his own pocket, fights every number: Taylor asks for $50 million and is offered 15, Spyros is shown a bill for the damage he caused, and Ben Kim gets a promotion instead of money. Taylor refuses to accept the number, and through Wendy and then Lara gets Axe to raise it to $25 million and put Taylor on the raise team. Chuck repairs his friendship with Ira by quietly driving off Ira's wife's lover and having his father negotiate her back into the marriage. Connerty volunteers to run Jock's internal leak hunt, which gives him access to agents' messages, and he recruits Oliver Dake against Chuck. Chuck brings New York Attorney General Alvin Epstein a weak case against Jock's brother, designed to bait Jock into obstructing it, while Taylor readies the quant algorithm and asks Grigor's lieutenant for a meeting.

billions:S03E12.title: Elmira
billions:S03E12.summary: At a big capital introduction event, Axe presents Taylor as the future of Axe Capital and wins $6 billion in commitments, but Taylor has secretly pitched Grigor and other investors and the next morning launches Mason Capital, taking $3.5 billion and Mafee. Axe counterattacks with lawsuits, a loyalty purge and a threat, and refuses Grigor's offer to have Taylor killed, knowing it would put him in Grigor's debt forever; Grigor moves his money to Taylor. Chuck's trap for Jock goes ahead: Epstein sends a target letter to Zeb Jeffcoat, Chuck asks Jock for guarantees in exchange for giving him private access to the witness Cutler, but Connerty has already learned the plan from Kate and taken it with Dake to Jock. Epstein backs out, Jock never goes near Cutler, and he fires Chuck, making Connerty interim US Attorney and Dake his Deputy AG. The season ends with Chuck and Axe sitting down together, each planning his next move.

billions:S04E01.title: Chucky Rhoades's Greatest Game
billions:S04E01.summary: Fired as US Attorney at the end of Season 3, Chuck starts over as a private power broker while Jock Jeffcoat swears in Bryan Connerty at Southern and orders a review of all of Chuck's old cases, hunting for misconduct. A wealthy client, Larry Brogan, asks Chuck for a near-impossible New York concealed carry permit, and Chuck spends a single day assembling a chain of favors (holiday service tickets, ski privileges, and the relocation of a charter school arranged through his new ally Axe) until Police Commissioner Sansome owes him enough to hand it over. Axe, now working with Chuck against their shared enemies, sets out to destroy Taylor Mason's new fund by telling a Gulf sovereign wealth fund not to invest with former Axe Cap people. Taylor wins the sovereign fund anyway, adapting their presentation to the room, and when Axe answers a summons to the embassy after Wags is drugged and held, he finds Grigor Andolov waiting, demanding that Axe leave Taylor (and Andolov's money) alone. Chuck ends the episode back inside the circle of New York's elite, drinking with the Commissioner.

billions:S04E02.title: Arousal Template
billions:S04E02.summary: Axe tries to starve Taylor Mason Capital of credit by cutting sweetheart deals with struggling banks so they will pull their business from Taylor. Andolov offers Taylor money from his dangerous associates, the Kozlov brothers, which would put Taylor in zugzwang (every move makes them weaker), so Taylor engineers a way to say yes to Andolov while making sure the Kozlov money never arrives, using Axe's own pressure on Patriot-Trust Bank to cut off the Kozlovs' credit. Chuck is asked by Commissioner Sansome to investigate the police pension fund's Raul Gomez, discovers Gomez is Axe's man and that Axe is quietly running the fund through a surrogate, and steers Sansome toward a result that protects Axe while collecting Sansome's endorsement for his run for New York State Attorney General. Axe meets billionaire Rebecca Cantu, invests in one of her companies and begins a relationship with her. Wendy and Chuck's marriage strains over their mismatched private lives.

billions:S04E03.title: Chickentown
billions:S04E03.summary: Hall hacks Taylor Mason Capital's remote logins and hands Axe a drive of their positions and trading patterns; Wendy turns it into a campaign of front-running, buying ahead of the names Taylor wants to add to so Axe Cap skims a slice off every trade, until Mafee and Sara realise they are being front-run. Dollar Bill's poultry play goes wrong and he is sent to Arkansas to find out why a chicken index report is delayed. Chuck's AG campaign is threatened when Lonnie Watley warns of a coming news story about an old case Chuck declined to prosecute against Sugar Vape, a company marketing flavoured vapes to children, and a whistleblower he abandoned. Chuck kills the story by visiting the whistleblower, Ray Cruz, and convincing him that if it runs Sugar Vape will sue him for everything he and his mother own, so Cruz walks back his account. Axe and Rebecca deepen their business partnership while Wendy tells Chuck she will play the candidate's wife but not on his terms at home.

billions:S04E04.title: Overton Window
billions:S04E04.summary: Black Jack Foley, dying and vengeful, prepares to expose Chuck's BDSM life on the eve of the election. Wendy urges Chuck to withdraw; instead he abandons his prepared remarks at a press conference and tells the public himself that he and Wendy practise sadomasochism, and he wins. At Axe Cap, a tip about an explosion at a natural gas facility sends the firm scrambling to dump positions just as a targeted cyberattack, which Axe blames on Andolov, knocks the whole firm offline, so Axe and Wags work burner phones and call in favors (Rebecca helps) while Taylor and Mafee press the advantage. Chuck delivers his end of the alliance: as the new Attorney General he freezes Andolov's assets and gives him twelve hours to leave the country, refusing Andolov's attempted bribe. Axe meets Andolov at the airport and promises to unfreeze his assets once he is back in Russia, and Andolov's billions leave Taylor's fund.

billions:S04E05.title: A Proper Sendoff
billions:S04E05.summary: Chuck starts work as New York Attorney General, and Foley is cremated. Taylor loses Andolov's money and is gutted, but wins the $3.1 billion New York firefighters' pension fund, a fund that once sat with Axe Cap, in a ten-minute pitch that stresses complete separation from Axe. Axe's old colleague's son John Rice, whose education and first fund Axe paid for, returns Axe's investment with a large profit so he can be free of him; Axe learns he is the only investor being cashed out and destroys John's fund by giving a press interview that casts doubt on his strategy. The episode also reveals why Axe was not in the North Tower on 9/11: he was being pushed out of the firm for borderline trades. Wendy, publicly exposed by Chuck's confession, discovers Taylor has been quietly defending her; she tells Axe she did not take Taylor's call, then calls Taylor back and agrees to talk. Taylor's father, Douglas Mason, appears: an inventor who needs about $28 million to launch a prototype.

billions:S04E06.title: Maximum Recreational Depth
billions:S04E06.summary: Axe discovers a time bomb Taylor left behind: while briefly running Axe Cap, Taylor papered a deal with Victor Mateo's firm with a term that makes Victor's actions legally attributable to Axe, and Victor is now under SEC scrutiny. Chuck and Connerty fight over whether the state AG or Southern prosecutes Abington, a Cayman Islands banker hiding money for Treasury Secretary Krakow, and Chuck uses the case to probe an unscheduled Cayman stop by Jock. Connerty and Kate Sacker win a wiretap on Chuck and his father after a judge reverses an earlier denial. Wendy, against Axe's explicit instructions, confides in Taylor, then uses Taylor's old Axe Cap therapy file and an unwitting Mafee to learn about Douglas Mason's invention, the raw material for a plan to split Taylor from their father. Axe nearly loses Rebecca by refusing to open up about business.

billions:S04E07.title: Infinite Game
billions:S04E07.summary: Axe and Wendy execute their plan against Taylor: a government official, paid off by Axe with a night Axe arranges, declares Douglas Mason's lattice fin technology vital to national security and seizes it, which threatens to scare off Taylor's investors, including the firefighters' fund. Taylor must choose between backing their father and keeping the fund alive; they keep the fund, hand Douglas a $1.3 million cheque and lose his trust, exactly as Wendy predicted, and Douglas tells Taylor that even if they win this infinite game it will not feel like winning. Chuck's early days as AG are spent on favors and messes, including rescuing Brogan after he shoots a neighbour's dog while drunk and armed with the permit Chuck got him. Chuck promises his father help with a financing snag on his real estate development through backchannel contacts, while Connerty listens on the wiretap. Chuck tells Wendy how his father treated his mother as their marriage wobbles.

billions:S04E08.title: Fight Night
billions:S04E08.summary: Taylor fights back. On live television Taylor announces a divestment from fracking and, in a head-to-head with Axe, accuses him of profiting from 9/11. Axe uses his political pull so the governor keeps fracking legal in New York and gloats, then realises Taylor wanted exactly that: Taylor Mason Capital had bought up the region's water utility and profits from the fracking Axe secured. Taylor also files a complaint with the medical board over Wendy's use of Taylor's therapy records, putting her licence at risk. Chuck, learning that Jock opposes a blockchain mobile voting pilot, switches to champion it, and finds a use for his father's ties to tribal casino groups whose applications were denied, running into Connerty and Sacker at the Board of Elections on Jock's behalf. Axe helps Rebecca with her bid for the Saler's department store chain, and Mafee and Dollar Bill settle their feud in a charity boxing match.

billions:S04E09.title: American Champion
billions:S04E09.summary: With Wendy's licence under review and Jock squeezing Chuck Senior's development, Chuck reroutes a freight train of New York sewage to a siding outside Jock's West Texas estate and leaves it there. Jock, through Connerty, offers to lift the pressure on the development and clear things with the medical board if Chuck moves the train and drops the mobile voting pilot; Chuck refuses, choosing the war with Jock over saving Wendy, and then lies to her about why he could not help. He also visits the imprisoned Dr. Ari Gilbert, a former medical board member, looking for leverage. Taylor attacks Axe through Rebecca: Rebecca starts as CEO of Saler's believing she controls the board, then finds two directors have sold their shares to Taylor at a premium. Rebecca quietly opens a negotiation with Taylor to save Saler's. Romances form at both firms (Bonnie and Dollar Bill, Taylor and Lauren), and Wendy leaves Chuck.

billions:S04E10.title: New Year's Day
billions:S04E10.summary: On New Year's Day Axe cuts short a Fiji holiday with his sons and assembles a war room at Axe Cap to run a mock hearing for Wendy, whose defence will be that her work with Taylor was performance coaching and Taylor was a client, not a patient. Chuck gives Wendy a morning and notices Axe is there in person. At Mason Capital, people burned by Axe and Chuck prepare Taylor to testify, and Taylor is warned that attacking Wendy carries risk; when Wendy asks Taylor not to appear, Taylor agrees, telling her she has a chance to save herself. Axe faces at least $75 million in tax on art shipped from a Swiss vault and solves it by storing it in a freeport at a private airport owned in part by Danny Margolis, where it is treated as permanently in transit. Chuck sets up a meeting between his father and Treasury Secretary Krakow over funding for the development, walking further into what looks like corruption.

billions:S04E11.title: Lamster
billions:S04E11.summary: Wendy rejects the deal Chuck quietly pre-negotiated with the medical board and instead confesses that Taylor was her patient and she used confidential information against them, and her licence is suspended. Chuck Senior discovers the FBI has bugged his house; Chuck sends him on the run with orders to check in every eight hours while he works out how to recover papers from Senior's safe linking them to Krakow, and they realise Chuck's home may be bugged too. Senior ends up in FBI custody while Jock appears to hold proof of the corrupt Krakow deal. Chuck's three old associates dig into Jock and find a voter fraud scheme run with Trent Fiske, CEO of the voting equipment company Bougle-Tek. Axe, to rescue Rebecca's Saler's, goes against all his advisors, bypasses company bylaws and liquidates positions to put billions of his own money into the chain. Senior's remarks about an unnamed idiot seed the finale.

billions:S04E12.title: Extreme Sandbox
billions:S04E12.summary: The finale shows its climaxes first and then rewinds to show how each was built. Axe partners with Sanford Bensinger, Saler's biggest debt holder, to shift Saler's toxic debt into Kling Appliances, the company Rebecca and Taylor are tied to through their deal, which wrecks Taylor's fund and betrays Rebecca; he pulls it off while Wendy keeps Rebecca away for a day of driving bulldozers with Mark Cuban. Chuck reveals that the Krakow meetings, Senior's flight and the incriminating safe were all bait: he and Senior used Connerty's and Jock's hatred to lure them into listening to an attorney-client privileged recording in which Senior calls the listener an idiot, catching both men crossing legal lines. Axe asks Chuck to detain Taylor without charging them so Taylor has no choice but to come back to Axe Cap to run the quant unit; Chuck, tired of being Axe's errand boy, does it, but secretly makes Taylor and Mafee his informants inside Axe Cap. The alliance ends, Taylor returns to Axe Cap, and Wendy's loyalty begins shifting from Chuck toward Axe.

billions:S05E01.title: The New Decas
billions:S05E01.summary: The season opens at Charles Rhoades Sr.'s wedding to Roxanne, where Chuck and Wendy are officially separated and Wendy rebuffs his attempt at reconciliation, then announces the divorce on her own terms. Axe and Wags return from an ayahuasca vision quest as Axe crosses the ten billion dollar mark, and Vanity Fair plans a cover on the 'new decas'. Axe only agrees to attend when he learns Mike Prince, a folksy Indiana-born billionaire who sells himself on ESG and social impact, will otherwise get the cover alone; Prince still manoeuvres to take the solo cover and uses the interview to paint Axe's model as outdated. Chuck and Kate Sacker go after a crypto-mining operation tied to Axe Capital that is draining a small town's electricity. Taylor is back under the Axe Cap roof while secretly working as Chuck's source, and the new three-way war (Axe, Chuck, Prince) is set up.

billions:S05E02.title: The Chris Rock Test
billions:S05E02.summary: Axe, Wags and Taylor go to 'The Mike', Prince's annual conference at Mohonk Mountain House, to embarrass Prince on his home turf. Axe's plan is a medical ayahuasca play: buy into a pharmaceutical company, line up clinical trials with a hospital chain CEO, and have Wags prime a future FDA official, all built around their shaman Bram Longriver. At the farewell dinner Prince introduces Longriver as his own partner in a health initiative, taking the deal out from under Axe. Chuck, using EMDR therapy and a reading of Darkly Dreaming Dexter, decides he can control his monster by living to a code, then freezes Wendy's assets in retaliation for her divorce statement; Axe rescues her with an apartment. Chuck also defends his ally Judge DeGiulio over a leaked torture memo, going so far as to be waterboarded, and it is revealed that Chuck leaked the memo himself to steer DeGiulio into the acting Solicitor General post.

billions:S05E03.title: Beg, Bribe, Bully
billions:S05E03.summary: Prince buys Nico Tanner's Implosion Series before Axe can, so Axe goes after the artist himself. Axe is also pursuing a bank charter, which he sees as the weapon to beat Prince, but is pulled away when Gordie is expelled from his prep school after his own crypto-mining experiment knocks out the school's power. Axe's fixer Hall finds that the headmaster has been skimming from a donor's gift, and Axe uses it while also staging an event that lets Gordie save face. Chuck takes a visiting professorship at Yale Law School, where his father's unpaid pledges have stained the family name; he gets Senior to pay by arranging a family introduction, and gets Wendy's help by dropping his financial restraining order against her, without telling her about the Yale quid pro quo. Taylor uses language analysis and Sara Hammon's naval background to win a university's fossil-fuel divestment, but refuses to profit from it, and Sara quits.

billions:S05E04.title: Opportunity Zone
billions:S05E04.summary: Axe goes back to his hometown of Yonkers to win a federal opportunity zone development against Mike Prince and Charles Rhoades Sr. He visits his childhood home, befriends a local kid named Savion, and forms a partnership with Kate Sacker's father Franklin that extends into banking. Chuck quietly meets Prince and urges him to commit a big donation to Yonkers, hoping Axe will respond by bribing the committee or breaking the law. Axe wins the zone, but Prince phones him afterwards and cuts him down over his origins, turning the win into a wound. Chuck starts at Yale and meets Catherine 'Cat' Brant, a sociology professor, and Taylor's divestment pipeline collapses after Axe's own pitch spoils it.

billions:S05E05.title: Contract
billions:S05E05.summary: Axe learns his mother has been giving things to his abusive father, destroys the Lexus she handed over, and buys his childhood home while moving Savion's family out of Yonkers. His bank charter stalls with banking official Leah Calder, who says his target zip code is already served by Vark Community Bank; Axe's team plants a story with reporter Randy Kornbluth that Vark charges minorities higher rates, and Vark takes a public hit. Axe picks Wags as the bank's CEO because he is legally clean and loyal. Chuck secures Calder's foot-dragging by recovering her family heirloom engagement ring with Jackie Connerty's help, and pays that debt by visiting Bryan Connerty in prison, where Connerty punches him. Charles Sr. is diagnosed with kidney failure and is ineligible for a transplant, and Wendy becomes a partner in Taylor's new fund, Taylor Mason Carbon.

billions:S05E06.title: The Nordic Model
billions:S05E06.summary: An old Axe art scheme resurfaces: replicas stored in a tax-free freeport are reported as genuine while the originals, including a prized Van Gogh, hang in his homes. Chuck spots the Van Gogh in the apartment where Wendy is staying, and he and Sacker open a tax case, but Manhattan DA Mary Ann Gramm takes it on jurisdictional grounds. Chuck, with Cat Brant's reluctant help and his promise that it is only a bluff, threatens to crack down on sex work, the cause Gramm wants to decriminalise, and gets the case back without following through. Axe counters by turning his apartment into a public art museum, and Chuck pours an expensive red wine over the Van Gogh during a visit. Axe's pitch to a senior regulator for his bank misfires when Wags sells him as a predator, and Taylor fights Oscar Langstraat over a methane-capture deal.

billions:S05E07.title: The Limitless Shit
billions:S05E07.summary: In the mid-season finale Axe pushes his team onto a cognitive-enhancement drug, Vigilantrix, with chaotic results, and hosts a dinner where Wendy and Nico Tanner are now a couple. Chuck brings Yale Law students into his office to hunt for dirt on Treasury Secretary Todd Krakow, Axe's ally on the bank charter, and secretly tests their blood as potential kidney donors for his father. When the students find nothing, Chuck and Sacker make Krakow believe he is under investigation, and his paranoia leads him to quit in the middle of a cabinet meeting. Taylor and Wendy, facing an unethical tin supply problem at a Mase Carb solar company, accept Prince's help: they leak the story themselves, halt production and switch to a clean source. Axe treats the partnership with Prince as an act of war and vows to find what Prince cares about most.

billions:S05E08.title: Copenhagen
billions:S05E08.summary: After the pandemic break, Axe learns Prince is about to be confirmed as US Ambassador to Denmark and sends Wags to find dirt. Wags targets Prince's number two, Scooter Dunbar, whose huge sports bets look like a security risk, but Prince comes to Axe Cap and reveals the bets were his own, defusing the attack. Dollar Bill points Axe to the real weak spot: a former partner of Prince's who died in a drunk-driving crash, and whose mother blames Prince for cutting him out of a big deal; Axe flies her in, gets her past her NDA, and her story tanks Prince's public profile and the ambassadorship. Chuck's attempt to trade sentence reductions for prisoners' kidneys is blocked by old enemy Dr. Ari Gilbert, he loses the Yale post over a threatened photo from his undergraduate days, Cat leaves him, and he inadvertently helps Axe secure the bank licence. A visit to Axe Cap puts Wendy and Tanner at odds.

billions:S05E09.title: Implosion
billions:S05E09.summary: As Prince reels from the scandal, Axe escalates: he guilts Mafee into having Mase Carb dump all of its Prince-linked holdings, which hurts decent companies and wrecks Mase Carb's standing as an impact fund. Axe uses confidential employee files Wendy compiled years earlier to find a kidney match for Charles Sr., and Danny Margolis donates; Chuck discovers in the hospital corridor that Axe has done what he could not. Axe also backs a master pizza maker's move into frozen pizza, and Tanner struggles to finish his paintings while Wendy worries money is changing him. The episode ends with Prince, Chuck and Taylor meeting under one roof with a shared goal: bringing Axe down.

billions:S05E10.title: Liberty
billions:S05E10.summary: Quarantined at home after his jet's pilot falls ill, Axe announces on a video call that Axe Capital is finished and everyone is let go, with some to be rehired for the new venture, Axe Bank. Chuck uses the divorce as a weapon, giving Wendy a choice between paying a lump-sum settlement or letting him examine the Mase Carb and Axe Cap books. Chuck stages a structured 'Jeffersonian dinner' with his allies, but Axe, tipped off by Wendy that his enemies have gathered, sends his new ally Charles Sr. and Dr. Swerdlow to crash it as his eyes and ears. Axe and Wendy admit deeper feelings for each other and cross a line.

billions:S05E11.title: Victory Smoke
billions:S05E11.summary: Axe Bank needs deposits to get past its probationary period, and Axe sets out to poach a big depositor from Prince: Fine Young Cannabis, run by former music producer Dawn Winslow, who is in an exclusive negotiation with Prince built around Prince's daughters as the brand's faces. Axe needs Charles Sr. to vouch for the bank to the Delaware Attorney General, and Senior demands a profit share in the cannabis deal. Chuck, Prince and Sacker weigh the personal cost of their plan, Taylor recruits an old foe, and Wags gets serious about a young woman named Chelz. Axe lights Red Auerbach-style victory cigars, but the episode ends with Wags telling the floor to put them out: Winslow is about to be arrested for drug trafficking and Axe's bank has been holding her money.

billions:S05E12.title: No Direction Home
billions:S05E12.summary: Chuck, Axe and Prince each try to outmanoeuvre the others as Chuck's case closes around Axe over the bank's link to black-market cannabis money. Just as Chuck has Axe on the verge of arrest, Prince breaks from Chuck and strikes a deal to buy Axe Capital, the bank and Taylor Mason Carbon. Axe escapes to Switzerland, beyond extradition for these financial charges, and walks off free but having lost his firm. Taylor and Wendy are left to sort out their futures, and the season closes with Prince sitting in Axe's chair and Chuck promising to take him down next.

billions:S06E01.title: Cannonade
billions:S06E01.summary: With Axe gone, Mike Prince owns the firm, renamed Michael Prince Capital, and inherits a trading floor that distrusts him, a six-month SEC probation and investors threatening to leave. He hands out Nimbus health rings that let his team track staff vitals, which saves Wags from a heart attack but exposes the surveillance. Prince tries to squeeze out Wags, whose Axe-era contract pays $80 million only if he is fired without cause; Wags refuses every settlement and proves his worth. Prince then stages an investor meeting that looks like a purge of the staff and instead fires every investor except the New York firefighters' pension, creating the exclusive 'Prince List'. Upstate, Chuck, working from his farm, defeats his cannon-firing billionaire neighbour Melville Revere by rallying the town and getting endangered bog turtles found on Revere's land.

billions:S06E02.title: Lyin' Eyes
billions:S06E02.summary: Chuck returns to the city and opens a war on the whole billionaire class, starting with the doormen whose wealthy tenants fled during the pandemic. He uses a video of Bud Lazzara paying off the union president to extract a raise for the doormen, then leaks the story anyway. Prince tells the floor to tank the stock of athletic apparel company Rask over its use of forced Uyghur labour, and the team doubts his motives. Wags, a friend of Rask's CEO Stuart Rask from rock fantasy camp, hides a conflict of interest and quietly serves both sides. Taylor and Wendy try to work out what Prince is really after.

billions:S06E03.title: STD
billions:S06E03.summary: Prince's hidden goal is out: he wants to bring the 2028 Summer Olympics to New York. A rival bid appears, led by disgraced former Treasury Secretary Todd Krakow through a SPAC and backed by Dollar Bill and Mafee's new fund, High Plains. Prince gets the new mayor to announce heavy reviews of Krakow's Manhattan stadium, which kills Krakow's timeline, and Krakow folds into Prince's bid. Taylor, Wendy and Ben Kim have to take down their old colleagues' position, and Mafee accuses Taylor of having a calculator for a heart. Chuck notices someone buying large amounts of property from the AG's land bank, then disrupts the Olympics announcement and turns public attention against Prince.

billions:S06E04.title: Burn Rate
billions:S06E04.summary: Facing political headwinds, Prince turns to Wendy, who realises he wants her to pitch her friend Kate Sacker on joining his Olympic effort. Kate tells Chuck about the approach and Chuck tells her to take the meeting to gather intelligence. Kate instead takes the job, on terms that make her Prince's peer rather than his protege. Wags and Scooter work together to keep the visiting Olympic delegation happy, and Taylor chases a big trade.

billions:S06E05.title: Rock of Eye
billions:S06E05.summary: Chuck, reeling from losing Kate, looks for a replacement and recruits Daevisha 'Dave' Mahar, a defence attorney from a white-shoe firm who goes up against him on a case and impresses him. Prince's bid is threatened when his daughter Gail publicly berates Governor Sweeney at a Knicks game, costing Prince the governor's support. Prince reads Sweeney as thin-skinned and vain, takes him to the stadium site and tells him it will be named after him, and Sweeney comes back on board. Kate settles into Prince's Olympic team.

billions:S06E06.title: Hostis Humani Generis
billions:S06E06.summary: Chuck switches from trying to win in one decisive stroke to a war of attrition, framing it as a game of Stratego. He sends Dave to meet Kate under the pretext of needing help on old cases, really to read her for signs of Prince's next move, and learns Prince plans to donate a new fleet of subway cars. The transit workers' union, fearing job losses, brings its complaint to Chuck. The cars are rejected on the ground that they are made by a Chinese company, and when Prince goes to Governor Sweeney he finds Chuck got there first, leaving Prince giving the transit system $2 billion for almost nothing in return.

billions:S06E07.title: Napoleon's Hat
billions:S06E07.summary: As the Olympic decision nears, Prince threatens to take his subway renovation plan to another city, finds Sweeney and the mayor mean to spend his $2 billion anyway, and wins after Taylor's trading against the MTA leaves the city no choice but to accept his help, including an Olympic Express rail line. To win committee votes without paying bribes, Prince funds scholarships at his old university and lets committee members hand them out. Chuck's team recognises the arrangement as sophisticated bribery and zeroes in on the middleman, Colin Drache. New York wins the Games, but when Chuck arrives with police to arrest Drache, Drache has vanished.

billions:S06E08.title: The Big Ugly
billions:S06E08.summary: On the last night of the Albany legislative session, Chuck dines with Prince's partners Todd Krakow, Bud Lazzara and Sruthi Reddy and tells them he has slipped a clause closing the carried interest loophole into the end-of-session legislation. To make it go away, the partners publicly disown the bid, saying they were unknowingly drawn into an attempt at high-level bribery. The International Committee strips New York of the 2028 Games and moves them to Los Angeles. Prince, who had pursued the Games partly to win back his estranged wife Andy, loses her again. Taylor, overcommitted to Olympic sponsor Hypersonic out of rivalry with Philip Charyn, uses the news to escape the position.

billions:S06E09.title: Hindenburg
billions:S06E09.summary: Chuck visits Prince offering to buy back Olympic land and 'dignity in defeat', and his gloating convinces Prince to go to war. Prince and Kate set out to remove Chuck from office, which needs the governor's letter and a two-thirds vote of the state Senate; Prince threatens Sweeney with a funded primary challenger and assembles the 42 votes, buying the last holdout, Senator Clay Tharp, with a redevelopment deal for his district. To distract Chuck and create a pretext, Prince's plant Stuart Legere lures Chuck's team to the Bates Club beside the private Van de Veld Park, where a staged incident sets Chuck against every billionaire keyholder; the billionaires come back to Prince, who makes each invest $250 million in MPC. Taylor stops Dollar Bill and Mafee poaching Ben and Tuk with a threat to destroy High Plains. Chuck gives a powerful speech to the Senate but is removed as Attorney General, and Dave Mahar is named acting AG.

billions:S06E10.title: Johnny Favorite
billions:S06E10.summary: MPC celebrates Chuck's fall, with Prince telling the team they have slain the dragon and will now eat its heart. Chuck, in shock, is dragged on a retreat by his father and old friends, cuts down an entitled rich man named Ron Chestnut, and in meditation realises that Prince needed to watch his fall in person. Wendy skips the celebration and presses Prince on what he really wants, and he admits to needing fear, respect and love. Kate learns that her father got her out of a youthful incident that her friends did not escape, and confronts him before it can be used against her.

billions:S06E11.title: Succession
billions:S06E11.summary: Prince sends Scooter to offer Chuck a job in his empire, and Chuck refuses. Chuck instead parks a large screen outside Prince's home that shows his net worth climbing in real time, letting the public and press do the attacking. Prince pushes 'Mike Money', a Prince-funded form of basic income to fight inequality, tells Taylor and Philip that one of them will succeed him at MPC, and sees a Wags-arranged meeting with Chinese officials go wrong. Wendy's upcoming book unsettles the firm. The episode ends by revealing Prince's real aim: the presidency of the United States.

billions:S06E12.title: Cold Storage
billions:S06E12.summary: Chuck, now out of office, works out that Prince is moving computer drives holding untaxed cryptocurrency that he plans to use to fund Mike Money and his political rise. Chuck tries to pressure Kate, uses a fake warrant while impersonating a prosecutor, and seizes one of the storage boxes. In an interrogation run by Dave Mahar, Prince faces a bind: unlock the drives and face tax charges if they hold crypto, or insist they are empty and let Chuck go to jail for an illegal seizure. Prince says he has no passwords and lets the technician burn through all ten attempts, destroying $3.5 billion, and Chuck is arrested. Dave, who saw Prince lying, later secures a court order that legitimises the raid and frees Chuck.

billions:S07E01.title: Tower of London
billions:S07E01.summary: Mike Prince decides to run for President in 2024 rather than 2028 and asks Wendy to prepare him for the job, and an opening flash-forward shows him in a rage, smashing the glass walls of Wendy's office at Mike Prince Capital. Prince grooms Taylor and Philip Charyn to run the fund while he campaigns; they resist, then accept, and Taylor makes the return of Dollar Bill a condition. Chuck, arrested at the end of the previous season after his case against Prince fell apart over a dummy warrant and evidence gained under false pretences, makes a deal with his former colleague Dave to keep fighting Prince, while his own agitation leads him into a plan that risks costing him his only ally. Wendy, Wags and Taylor privately conclude Prince is unfit for the presidency and go looking for the one man who can beat him, and Wendy finds Axe in London, where his arms-for-Ukraine brokering has made him welcome despite being a fugitive from the US.

billions:S07E02.title: Original Sin
billions:S07E02.summary: Wendy, Wags and Taylor visit Axe at his English estate, where he runs Axe Global with his son Gordie in digital currency, and ask him to come home and stop Prince. Axe refuses and offers them a comfortable life in England instead; tempted, they decline and go back to New York to fight without him. Chuck works his way back toward power at the Southern District: he meets Solicitor General Adam DeGiulio, who tells him the President will not simply reverse his firing, so Chuck visits the imprisoned former Attorney General Jock Jeffcoat and trades on Jock's self-interest until Jock records a confession that he forced the President to fire Chuck. Prince builds his campaign team, hires a campaign manager (Bradford Luke), and has to submit his personal life to their vetting.

billions:S07E03.title: Winston Dick Energy
billions:S07E03.summary: An episode about Chuck, Wendy and Wags each reasserting themselves. Wags finds his old contacts now see him as a has-been and a politician's servant; after a whiskey session with Wendy, both decide to get back to their old selves. Wags goes after Winston, who has quit MPC and is pitching risk software he built on Prince's time to Prince's competitors: he bugs Winston's apartment, tracks who Winston will pitch, and kills his chances. Wendy discovers the office has been seeing an outside therapist, Dr. Mayer, and confronts her for taking her patients. Chuck returns to the Southern District, rallies the troops and recruits Ira to his team.

billions:S07E04.title: Hurricane Rosie
billions:S07E04.summary: Chuck finds that Kang Lou, a fugitive wanted by US authorities, is travelling on Prince's plane as a billionaire's friend; he calls Kate Sacker, now Prince's counsel, and she has Prince ground the plane. Prince buys Scooter the chance to guest-conduct the New York Philharmonic with Leonard Bernstein's baton, but Bradford Luke kills the moment as bad optics for voters. MPC holds billions in catastrophe bonds tied to Southern Property and Casualty, which would be devastated if Hurricane Rosie is rated Category 5, so Wags learns how storms are classified and bribes the responsible scientist with a research grant to rate it Category 4. The bonds survive, saving MPC a fortune, but Prince and Bradford are furious: thousands have lost their homes, the insurer is drowning in claims, and a candidate whose bonds stayed pristine through the disaster faces ruin if the fix ever comes out.

billions:S07E05.title: The Gulag Archipelago
billions:S07E05.summary: Philip and Taylor chafe at the $500 million cap Prince has placed on investment decisions they can make on their own, telling Prince and Scooter that without full authority they lack the floor's respect; Prince and Scooter leave to court rapper Killer Mike's endorsement. Dollar Bill brings in a lucrative helium production opportunity, Taylor gives it to Rian to find a better entry point, but the position needed exceeds the cap and the only two people who can approve it are unreachable, and MPC ends up losing more than a billion dollars. At the end Wendy, Taylor and Wags meet, and it emerges Taylor set the helium situation up to hurt Prince. Chuck, meanwhile, recovers a precious item Ira lost in a mugging by calling on an old contact, Raul Gomez, and continues to build his legal position to go after Prince.

billions:S07E06.title: The Man in the Olive Drab T-Shirt
billions:S07E06.summary: Axe, Grigor Andolov and other oligarchs receive video thanks from President Zelenskyy for brokering weapons for Ukraine, which has made Grigor a traitor in Russia. Axe invites Chuck to a remote airstrip in Iceland and asks a personal favour: safe passage into the US for Grigor, whose estranged wife is suing him for divorce in New York on grounds of abandonment and could win billions by default. Chuck discovers Todd Krakow is bankrolling the suit and sleeping with Mrs Andolov, brings Grigor in as an expert witness in another case, lets Grigor frighten Krakow off, and then stages a public arrest that makes both Chuck and Grigor look good to their home audiences. Wags works on Kate Sacker to leave Prince for her own congressional run, but on her father's advice she stays. Wendy runs an employee feedback exercise meant to puncture Prince's confidence, it backfires, and Prince decides to run as an independent, with his wife Andy revealed as a driving force behind his ambition.

billions:S07E07.title: DMV
billions:S07E07.summary: Charles Rhoades Sr tries to tip a DMV examiner after grandson Kevin fails his driving test, lands them both in trouble, and Chuck has to use charm and his office to get them out, even persuading the examiner that his father has bouts of senility. Waiting outside, Wendy asks Chuck to use his contacts at the Department of Defense to take one of Prince's political advantages off the board while her team looks for a permanent way to hobble him from inside. At MPC, Prince makes a play that promises to boost his platform but wrecks Philip: after Philip introduces his old professor Ruloff, Prince starts buying up rival patents, even loosely related ones, to gain standing to sue for infringement, and cannibalises the professor's work. Prince, having heard his employees' real opinions through Wendy's feedback exercise, has Wags and Scooter run a performance review panel to lift morale.

billions:S07E08.title: The Owl
billions:S07E08.summary: Chuck and Prince both go upstate to a retreat of wealthy power brokers, where Prince debates Governor Nancy Dunlop on how to handle a nuclear standoff, and Chuck tries and fails to get the kingmaker known as Fourth to drop his support for Prince. Fourth promises to back Prince if he solves a problem for Andy: her friend (and, it emerges, lover) Derek is injured and stranded on the Chinese side of a mountain on the Nepal border. Prince hires an elite private rescue, but as Prince, Andy, Wendy, Scooter and Bradford listen in, Chinese authorities swoop and the team aborts. Andy realises Prince tipped off the Chinese himself, getting Derek off the mountain as promised while avoiding a clash with China. Wendy helps Wags unpack desires he has been hiding.

billions:S07E09.title: Game Theory Optimal
billions:S07E09.summary: Chuck decides the way to stop Prince is to separate him from the billions that give him power and voter appeal, and to prove his commitment he invites Wendy, Wags and Taylor to his brownstone and puts in front of them a drive containing a full confession of every illegal act of his career, from the Ice Juice blind trust violation to the Hap Halloran bribe and voter suppression with Axe. The four form an alliance. Prince is then tipped off about the mutiny, including Taylor's earlier secret meeting with Axe, and summons Wendy, Wags, Taylor and Philip to his home, where he, Scooter, Kate and Philip lay out the 'attempted assassination'. Instead of firing them, Prince strips them of power and locks them inside MPC until the election, then heads for London. Wendy is tempted by an outside offer to lead a mental health tech company, Mental.

billions:S07E10.title: Enemies List
billions:S07E10.summary: Prince visits Axe in London and warns him off: if Axe digs, warns Wendy or attacks, Wendy will be ruined, because the Mental job was a trap. Mental keeps a second set of books that bills insurers for AI check-ins as if they were human sessions, which is Medicare fraud, and Wendy has signed a certification of the company's financials, making her personally liable; Rian uncovers the scheme when Wendy asks her to look at the numbers. Prince reorganises MPC around loyalists and promises the loyal new slots, while Taylor skips work to plan with Axe. Chuck calls in the Grigor favour and Axe hangs up, but Axe then returns to the US, ambushes Prince at a concert in Prince's honour with Derek, the man Prince left to the Chinese, and blackmails him into releasing Wendy. Rattled, Prince orders his people to clear every position in his portfolio, and Chuck and Axe, reunited, go to work together.

billions:S07E11.title: Axe Global
billions:S07E11.summary: Axe launches Axe Global in New York and the campaign intensifies. Axe meets Governor Nancy Dunlop and promises to help her reach the White House if she plays his game against Prince; Dunlop then publicly throws her support behind Prince and becomes his running mate, which looks like a win for Prince. Prince visits Axe at the new firm and tells him that, against Philip's advice, he has liquidated everything. Chuck meets former Prince Cappers to find weaknesses in Prince's companies and asks Torre to write briefs against them; she hesitates and the list reaches Kate Sacker. Loyalties inside MPC are tested as everyone prepares for the final confrontation.

billions:S07E12.title: Admirals Fund
billions:S07E12.summary: The series finale reveals that people inside Prince's camp have been working with Chuck, Axe and Wendy for weeks: Philip turned four weeks earlier when Wendy found him at the Corner Bistro, and Kate Sacker ratted out Wendy, Wags and Taylor so Prince would trust her and Philip. While Prince meets the President at Camp David, a sign he is the front-runner, with his phone locked away by Marine security, Philip puts MPC's funds into natural gas, Taylor alters the Winston risk algorithm to sell when it should hold, and Chuck's SDNY investigation of the sector leaks to the press. The stocks crater, the algorithm dumps everything at the bottom, margin calls cannot be met because Prince had barred pledging his private holdings, and the Admirals Fund, an old quasi-legal account Axe set up, buys the stocks at the bottom before Chuck announces the investigation found only hearsay and prices rebound. Prince is left with only the $100 million he put into Black-owned banks, his campaign is finished, the employees get rich, Axe Global takes over MPC's headquarters, Chuck ends up as US Attorney for the Southern District again, Wendy becomes CEO of a telehealth company, and Taylor leaves finance for philanthropy.

house-of-cards:S01E01.title: Chapter 1
house-of-cards:S01E01.summary: House Majority Whip Frank Underwood backed Garrett Walker for president in exchange for a promise of Secretary of State, but chief of staff Linda Vasquez tells him the promise is off and that Senator Michael Kern will get the job. Frank accepts graciously in the room, then tells his chief of staff Doug Stamper that they now serve no one and will hold everyone accountable, starting with Kern. He acquires Congressman Peter Russo by having Russo's drunk-driving arrest quietly erased and then confronting him with it, and he takes on ambitious metro reporter Zoe Barnes as an anonymous channel, feeding her the far-left first draft of the administration's education bill. Meanwhile his wife Claire loses a promised Sancorp donation to her charity, the Clean Water Initiative (CWI), and responds by cutting half her staff. Frank also sounds out Senator Catherine Durant as an alternative Secretary of State.

house-of-cards:S01E02.title: Chapter 2
house-of-cards:S01E02.summary: The leaked Blythe draft embarrasses the White House, and Frank uses the fallout to maneuver Congressman Donald Blythe into volunteering to step aside, leaving Frank in charge of the education bill while six hand-picked experts write a new draft in secret. He gives Zoe a 1978 college editorial from Kern's student paper calling the Israeli presence in Gaza and the West Bank an illegal occupation, and sends Russo to the editorial's real author, Roy Kapeniak, who goes on record saying Kern wrote it. Kern's defensive public answers turn a thin story into a scandal and he withdraws. Frank then has Zoe report Durant as the likely replacement before the White House has decided, and the resulting chorus of approval makes her the choice. Claire fires eighteen staff and then her longtime office manager Evelyn.

house-of-cards:S01E03.title: Chapter 3
house-of-cards:S01E03.summary: In the middle of tense negotiations with the teachers' unions, Frank has to fly home to Gaffney, South Carolina, where a teenager died in a crash beside the Peachoid water tower and his local rival Orrin Chase is using the death to attack him. Frank wins over the grieving parents with a sermon on faith and grief, a scholarship, safety measures and an offer to resign, then corners Orrin with county liability and a threat to his property before offering him a seat in Congress. While he is away, union lobbyist Marty Spinella nearly walks out and Frank gives up concessions by phone. Claire courts Gillian Cole, founder of the water charity World Well, to join CWI. Zoe defies her editor Tom Hammerschmidt by going on television, with Frank's encouragement.

house-of-cards:S01E04.title: Chapter 4
house-of-cards:S01E04.summary: Speaker Bob Birch refuses to bring the education bill to the floor because Frank has secretly added an anti-collective-bargaining provision. Frank talks the President out of conceding and then engineers a fake coup: he pitches Majority Leader David Rasmussen on replacing Birch, is turned down, recruits Terry Womack and the Black Caucus anyway in David's name, and then reveals the plot to Birch as David's. Birch demotes Rasmussen, makes Womack majority leader and agrees to move the bill. To pay for keeping Womack's air force base open, Frank forces Russo to let his own district's shipyard close, and Russo's life falls apart. Claire turns down a doubled Sancorp donation at Frank's request and lines up Felicity Holburn's money instead. Zoe turns down the White House beat and is fired from the Herald, and she begins a sexual relationship with Frank.

house-of-cards:S01E05.title: Chapter 5
house-of-cards:S01E05.summary: Spinella discovers the collective-bargaining amendment and threatens war. Frank peels off one of the two unions, but Spinella moves toward a national teachers' strike and gets the hotel's union staff to shut Claire's CWI gala out of its ballroom. Frank and Claire hold the party on the hotel steps instead, and the picketers go home after being handed food. Zoe joins the start-up Slugline, and Frank gives her burner phones and asks for private photos as security. Tom Hammerschmidt is forced out of the Herald. Frank tells Doug his plan to run Russo for governor of Pennsylvania, hinting that the real target is the Vice President. When a drunk Russo turns up to blame him, Frank humiliates him, tells him he is still on the shortlist, and gets a promise of a month's sobriety.

house-of-cards:S01E06.title: Chapter 6
house-of-cards:S01E06.summary: A month into the strike, the White House wants Frank to gut the bill, and he buys one more week.
