peaky-blinders:S05E01.summary: October 1929: the Wall Street crash wipes out the Shelby Company's legitimate money in America because Michael ignored Tommy's instruction to sell. Tommy, now a Labour MP, calls a board meeting with Arthur as figurehead chairman, tells the family that cash from the illegal side is now king, and reveals the Peaky Blinders killed a child-selling pimp in Chinatown as a favour to a judge, Scotland Yard and a peer. He squeezes that peer, Lord Suckerby, for the unpaid balance by holding the compromising photographs, plays the man of the people in his pub and in the Commons, and destroys a Times journalist's attempt to dig into his past by revealing he has researched the journalist's own secret. In private he is secretly informing on communists to intelligence officer Ben Younger via Ada, paid in military contracts. Oswald Mosley introduces himself and tells Tommy he has come to his attention.

peaky-blinders:S05E02.title: Black Cats
peaky-blinders:S05E02.summary: The IRA take Michael off his ship in Belfast, accusing him of meeting the Glasgow Billy Boys who want Tommy dead, and send him home at Tommy's request. Tommy quarantines Michael in the Midland Hotel, interrogates him before the family, accepts his story, then binds him to the company by the debt from the crash. The journalist Levitt has been shot, and Tommy sends a detective away by invoking the Chief Constable. Mosley courts Tommy with flattery and the offer of a junior ministry, which Tommy refuses. Jimmy McCavern of the Billy Boys crucifies Aberama Gold's son Bonnie as a message that Tommy must share his racecourses. Meanwhile Tommy has Finn recruit the old footballer Billy Grade to fix matches, and Lizzie makes clear that if Tommy dies she, legally, takes his place.

peaky-blinders:S05E03.title: Strategy
peaky-blinders:S05E03.summary: Tommy takes Arthur and Michael to meet Mosley, who demonstrates that he knows every family weakness within seconds, then reveals he has made the Levitt murder inquiry disappear and invites Tommy to be deputy leader of a new party. Tommy takes Mosley's letter to Ben Younger and pushes him to sanction an operation in which Tommy joins Mosley to undermine him from inside. Polly, sent to calm the grieving Aberama Gold, instead helps him go north for revenge, and Arthur and Johnny Dogs are sent after him into a Billy Boys ambush. Lizzie, having nearly left, renegotiates her marriage like a contract. Arthur, desperate over Linda, beats the Quaker who befriended her, and Tommy tells Mosley he accepts, while asking Younger to confirm his role as informant is officially sanctioned.

peaky-blinders:S05E04.title: The Loop
peaky-blinders:S05E04.summary: Tommy makes a truce with McCavern under a white flag and turns the enemy into a customer. Brilliant Chang, back from the dead, offers £250,000 to move seven tonnes of opium by canal from London, and Tommy wins the family vote by offering Polly her son's return from quarantine as the man in charge. Tommy uses Polly's engagement to Aberama as the price for Aberama postponing his revenge on McCavern. Mosley threatens to use Lizzie's past against Tommy, and Tommy answers with Mosley's own affairs. At a ballet party in Tommy's house, Tommy gets Mosley to sign a guarantee for McCavern's cheque, creating written proof of a link between Mosley and a criminal gang, while Michael and Gina privately plan for the day Tommy is gone. Linda arrives with a gun for Arthur.

peaky-blinders:S05E05.title: The Shock
peaky-blinders:S05E05.summary: Polly shoots Linda to stop her killing Arthur, and Linda then leaves him. Mosley uses Tommy's party to announce the British Union of Fascists, publicly claiming Tommy will be at his side, and privately carves up the country, giving the north to McCavern. Tommy hands Ben Younger the Mosley guarantee and a list of sympathetic MPs, but Younger is killed by a car bomb outside Ada's home, a result Tommy blames on his own good intentions. The opium pick-up in London is ambushed by the Titanic gang, which means someone is leaking. Tommy visits his wartime comrade Barney Thomason in an asylum and recruits him as a sniper, then tells Arthur the plan: Barney will shoot Mosley on stage while Tommy stands beside him and inherits the party.

peaky-blinders:S05E06.title: Mr Jones
peaky-blinders:S05E06.summary: Winston Churchill visits Tommy, having found out he is spying on Mosley, and gives him a quiet blessing. At a family meeting Michael proposes a restructure in which he becomes managing director of an American narcotics expansion and Tommy becomes a figurehead under a dead man's name; Tommy throws him out. Tommy lays out the assassination plan to his inner circle, buys a Jewish fighting crew from the not-dead Alfie Solomons to make the riot explicable, and exposes the barman Micky as the informer behind the bomb and the ambush. At the Bingley Hall rally the plan collapses: Barney and Aberama are killed before the shot, the shooters knew everything, and Tommy cannot work out who betrayed him. Alone by the water, he puts a gun to his head.

peaky-blinders:S06E01.title: Black Day
peaky-blinders:S06E01.summary: The morning after the failed attempt on Oswald Mosley, the IRA's Captain Swing tells Tommy that her men stopped the shooting, killed Polly and others, and that from now on the Shelbys will lean on the IRA. Michael swears to his dead mother that he will take revenge on Tommy, whatever lies it takes. Four years later, on the last day of Prohibition, a sober Tommy lands on French-ruled Miquelon Island and pitches the idle bootleggers and Michael (now married to Gina, niece of Boston power broker Jack Nelson) a plan to run his opium into Boston. Tommy then anonymously tips off the police so Michael is jailed with the opium, uses the arrest to put Jack Nelson in a political bind, threatens to sell to the rival Solomons family instead, and visits Michael in prison with a letter from the President's secretary keeping him there. News that his daughter Ruby is ill and speaking Romany curse words sends Tommy home.

peaky-blinders:S06E02.title: Black Shirt
peaky-blinders:S06E02.summary: Ruby's first tests come back clear and Tommy, suffering seizures, pushes on with 'one last deal'. He gives a rousing socialist speech in Birmingham, then quietly recruits IRA commander Laura McKee (from the unit that killed Polly) into a scheme to court Jack Nelson with British and Irish fascists, using Nelson's stolen private letters. He offers Alfie Solomons the opium as the 'final act' of his revenge on the Boston Irish, pays for property he can demolish for housing, and at a Mosley rally slaps a black-shirted Arthur and bribes him toward sobriety with the promise of reuniting him with Linda. He meets Mosley and his mistress Diana Mitford, then Jack Nelson in a church, offering fascist contacts and intelligence on Churchill in exchange for access to South Boston. Gina tells jailed Michael that Jack has agreed Michael can be the one to kill Tommy. Ruby relapses and is coughing blood.

peaky-blinders:S06E03.title: Gold
peaky-blinders:S06E03.summary: Ruby is diagnosed with consumption and Tommy, convinced it is a Gypsy curse, hands Ada his London business for five days and rides into the hills with Esme to find its source. Ada holds her own at Diana Mitford's lunch with Mosley, Nelson and Gina, asserting that the Shelbys hold the power because they hold the information and incentives, and delivers Tommy's invitation to the real meeting. Ada also takes charge of the company, sending Isiah and a newly clean Arthur to Liverpool to punish union man Haydn Stagg for stealing opium, where Stagg talks Arthur out of the beating by speaking to his addiction. Esme shows Tommy the grave of a Barwell girl who died after Tommy's cursed sapphire was put around her neck, and names her mother Evadne as the likely curse-layer; Esme demands payment in gold. Tommy returns to the sanatorium too late: Ruby has died.

peaky-blinders:S06E04.title: Sapphire
peaky-blinders:S06E04.summary: Tommy speaks at Ruby's Gypsy funeral, then tracks down Evadne Barwell and kills her and three men; Esme uses the moment to sell him the existence of a son, Duke, born to a girl at Appleby Fair in 1914. Tommy rallies Arthur with memories of their childhood and the Dudley tunnel. Four nights after the funeral he hosts Mosley, Diana, Nelson, Gina and Laura McKee at his house, proves his commitment to the fascist cause, and wins the opening of Boston to his opium; afterwards he types up the meeting word for word for Churchill. He catches Gina leaving Mosley's flat and uses the affair to make her his spy in Berlin. His doctor Holford then tells him the shadow on his X-ray is an inoperable tuberculoma and gives him 12 to 18 months.

peaky-blinders:S06E05.title: The Road to Hell
peaky-blinders:S06E05.summary: Tommy uses his position as MP and the council's demolition powers to shut opium dealing out of Small Heath. He brings Duke into the family, pays Linda's foundation £10,000 to help Arthur, and recruits Haydn Stagg to store the Thompson guns coming from Boston for his IRA partners. Arthur's attempt to force a religious referee to fix a match ends with Arthur making Billy Grade kill the man, while a man working for Jack Nelson tortures the Shelby informant into giving up Arthur. Tommy sleeps with Diana to secure the Guinness family's support for his housing plans; at dinner with Nelson, Diana and Mosley reveal it to Lizzie and urge Tommy to find a more suitable wife. In Boston, Michael accepts Nelson's condition for release: he will kill Tommy.

peaky-blinders:S06E06.title: Lock and Key
peaky-blinders:S06E06.summary: Lizzie leaves Tommy and takes Charlie. Arthur finds out about the tuberculoma and gets clean. Tommy gathers his trusted men and, in front of the informant Billy Grade, lays out a 'party' at Arrow House while Arthur lets it be known he will be at the Garrison with his wife for their anniversary, and Tommy switches into Romany ('tachipen', truth) for what the insiders need to know. Nelson's IRA hit team comes for Arthur at the Garrison and is killed; Billy dies at Arrow House, which Tommy blows up to make way for housing; Finn fails a loyalty test with an unloaded gun and is thrown out of the family. On Miquelon, Johnny Dogs switches the timer on Michael's bomb and Tommy kills Michael, while Alfie Solomons takes over Boston. Tommy leaves to die alone in a wagon, sees Ruby in a vision telling him he is not sick, and confronts Holford: the diagnosis was a fascist plot to make him kill himself.

suits:S01E01.title: Pilot
suits:S01E01.summary: Harvey Specter, the top closer at Pearson Hardman, bluffs a client into closing a deal, is found out, and loses a promised promotion to senior partner. Ordered to hire a Harvard associate, he instead hires Mike Ross, a college dropout with a photographic memory who stumbles into his interviews while fleeing a police drug sting. When Harvey tries to fire Mike to protect himself, Mike points out that firing him guarantees the lie gets exposed, and Harvey uses the same logic on Jessica to win back his promotion. Jessica attaches a price: Harvey must personally handle a pro bono sexual harassment case, which he quietly passes to Mike. Mike and Harvey force the company to open its personnel files, recover a hidden former victim, catch the CEO paying her to sabotage the case, and use witness tampering to extract a large settlement. Along the way Louis Litt, who lost the promotion race to Harvey, stages a fake firing to intimidate Mike, and Harvey keeps a major client by digging up his own client's vulnerabilities.

suits:S01E02.title: Errors and Omissions
suits:S01E02.summary: Mike fails to file a patent for Harvey's client Wyatt on time, and a billion dollar rival, Velocity Data, files first. Harvey's injunction is blocked by a judge who holds a grudge because he believes Harvey slept with his wife; the judge then offers the injunction in exchange for a signed admission he can use in his divorce, and Harvey answers by having him investigated. Meanwhile Louis shows Mike a forged failed drug test and pressures him into smoking pot with Tom Keller, a prospective client, to win his business; Mike confesses the setup to Keller, which makes Keller trust him more. Harvey closes the patent fight by threatening to publish the phone's designs online, which drives Velocity to a $400 million settlement. The episode ends with Harvey revealing the drug test was fake and Mike using Louis's own drug policy against him.

suits:S01E03.title: Inside Track
suits:S01E03.summary: Harvey learns that Robert Stensland, the new CEO of McKernon Motors (Harvey's first ever client), plans to sell the land under the flagship factory and move production overseas, which Harvey believes will destroy the company. Mike finds a flaw in the bylaws Harvey drafted: Stensland is only interim CEO until the board votes, so Harvey stalls the sale and recruits Dominic Barone, the production chief who distrusts him, to challenge for CEO. Stensland sees the stall for what it is, moves the board meeting, gets confirmed, and fires both Dominic and the firm. Harvey responds by calling in a favour from Laurence, a hedge fund manager he let have a Tesla at the start of the episode, who offers to buy the company, while Mike invents a procedural argument to get them into the board meeting. Behind the scenes, Jessica sends Louis to Stensland to hedge the firm's bets, and Mike learns that a rookie dinner and first impressions matter.

suits:S01E04.title: Dirty Little Secrets
suits:S01E04.summary: Jessica hands Harvey a case defending her ex-husband Quentin Sainz, whose ALS drug is accused of causing liver failure, and promises to stay out of it. Plaintiff lawyer Collin Church opens with a $250 million demand and a threat to run a libellous ad; Harvey digs up evidence that Church recycles plaintiffs, but is blindsided when Church uses company financials Quentin never handed over. Jessica and Harvey then extract a confession from Quentin's partner Lisa that she hid a trial participant with liver damage, and learn Quentin himself has ALS. Harvey resolves it by going around Church and speaking directly to the plaintiffs, offering them partial ownership of the company. In the B plot, Louis gives Mike a housing court case meant to go nowhere; Mike loses the first hearing, then finds the landlord is forcing out rent-controlled tenants for condo conversions, gathers 15 former tenants, and proves the landlord planted bedbug infested carpet.

suits:S01E05.title: Bail Out
suits:S01E05.summary: Mike answers a call from Trevor in jail during a client meeting and bails him out with all his savings. A cab crashes into Harvey's car and its driver, Mr. Santana, sues Harvey's driver Ray Benghazi; Harvey takes Ray's defence pro bono and, to jump the court queue, accepts an open-ended favour from Louis that Louis then tries to collect by borrowing Donna. Mike talks toy company founder Joy McAfee out of a $200 million licensing deal by accident, and Harvey rescues the relationship by selling her stake and flying in her family. In court, Harvey dismantles Santana with a timeline that shows Santana was the one running late, then settles on generous terms. Trevor's former drug associates come to the firm looking for him and take him hostage for $50,000; Harvey defuses it by turning the dealers into his own clients. Louis plants a tabloid story about Harvey bullying a cab driver.

suits:S01E06.title: Tricks of the Trade
suits:S01E06.summary: Harvey negotiates a plea deal for Gabby Stone, a trader at his client Morello Asset Management, to take the blame for an insider trade, but she flees when Mike leaves her alone and runs back to the office to hunt for proof of innocence. Mike persuades Harvey that if someone else at Morello did it, the client is at risk, so Harvey investigates. When second in command Burt Kimball personally delivers a set of trade records, Harvey reads the courtesy as a tell; Mike gets the real trades by posing as a rival trader in a bar. The pattern shows Burt handed out rigged tip sheets and paid Gabby's own lawyer, and Harvey exposes him in front of founder Dean Morello, who fires him. Meanwhile Jessica courts Louis with King Lear tickets to keep him loyal as a counterweight to Harvey, and Rachel discovers Mike used to take the LSAT for money.

suits:S01E07.title: Play the Man
suits:S01E07.summary: The first-year associates face a mock trial, and Louis pairs Mike against Kyle, a three-time mock trial champion (Harvey has quietly rigged the draw and bet Jessica on the result). Kyle agrees a settlement with Mike in private, then denies it in court, and Mike has to recover with a delay and a defamation countersuit. Meanwhile Harvey's client Jones Debeque has rushed into a hotel merger with Daniel Vega, whose lawyer is Harvey's old rival and lover Dana 'Scottie' Scott. Scottie tricks Harvey into opening Debeque's private books, and Vega starts a hostile takeover. Harvey threatens to sell Debeque's best hotels, forces both clients back to the original merger, and Scottie is fired. Mike wins his trial but backs off before breaking a witness, and Harvey and the partners read that as weakness.

suits:S01E08.title: Identity Crisis
suits:S01E08.summary: Pearson Hardman is suing Anthony Mazlo, whose firm embezzled about $150 million from Lucille Jackson's housing charity, Stable Shelters. Jessica forces Harvey to work with Louis, who deposes Mazlo's number two, Elliot Perkins, so harshly that Perkins collapses and dies. Mazlo blames the dead Perkins, offers ten cents on the dollar, then plants a fake whistleblower who accuses Louis of bribery and uses that to halve the offer. Harvey wins Louis back to the case. Louis's forensic reasoning, together with bank records that Lola Jensen hacks, traces the money to seven Liechtenstein accounts, and Mazlo returns the money and resigns. On the side, Mike deals with Lola, a client's daughter who is stealing from her father's fracking company for good causes, and who finds out he never went to Harvard.

suits:S01E09.title: Undefeated
suits:S01E09.summary: Jessica's class action for 200 cancer victims from Apple Creek against Emerson Petroleum draws in Travis Tanner, a Boston lawyer who specialises in breaking class actions. Tanner gets under Harvey's skin, and Harvey takes the case over. Tanner then works to split the plaintiffs apart with a proxy who threatens them with their past, and with a lowball offer of $25,000 each. Harvey matches the offer with a loan against the future award, backed by a million dollars of his own money, and bluffs with an illegal wiretap to force a $2 million per plaintiff settlement. Inside the firm, Louis's witch hunt for a leaker gets Rachel suspended. Mike tracks the real leaker to Jimmy, a fellow associate, and Rachel comes back on her own terms.

suits:S01E10.title: The Shelf Life
suits:S01E10.summary: Tori, CEO of Drybeck Accounting (the firm's own accountants and a client worth $10 million a year), asks Harvey to fire senior VP Stan Jacobson quietly for lying on his resume. Mike lets Stan see that the background check is five years old, and Stan claims he is being pushed out for asking questions about the books. Harvey closes the firing with a two-option squeeze, then investigates against Jessica's orders. Mike slips into a Harvard mixer and an Unger and Macy office, Harvey calls in a judge's favour and silences a security guard who tries to extort him, and Rachel types up the files Mike memorised. They uncover a chain of shelf companies Tori used to skim from Pearson Hardman. Jessica and Harvey drop Tori as a client and confront her with Stan as their consultant. In the background, Louis plants doubts about Rachel in the mind of Mike's girlfriend Jenny.

suits:S01E11.title: Rules of the Game
suits:S01E11.summary: Harvey's old boss, District Attorney Cameron Dennis, stages a chance meeting to find out whether Harvey will protect him from an Attorney General investigation into buried evidence. Investigator Alexandra Leeds subpoenas Harvey and threatens to go after him too. Harvey refuses to testify, but Cameron quietly cuts a deal to sell Harvey out. Donna gives Jessica a file she kept from Harvey's D.A. days, and Jessica uses it to force Cameron to step down and clear Harvey. The file shows that a man Harvey convicted, Clifford Danner, is innocent. In the case of the week, Harvey and Louis split a tabloid owner's estate between two feuding daughters. Mike gives away his client's priority, then sets a fax machine trap that Louis sees through, and Louis wins the bet in which Harvey had staked Mike.

suits:S01E12.title: Dog Fight
suits:S01E12.summary: Harvey sets out to free Clifford Danner, the man he wrongly convicted 12 years earlier, and gets a new trial on the grounds of buried evidence. The new D.A., Terrance Wolf, answers by threatening a life sentence, and the key evidence (a blood-stained camisole) is thrown out on chain of custody. With the help of an unauthorised DNA test, which Jessica forces Louis to arrange after he tries to trade it for senior partner, Harvey and Mike turn the two real killers against each other. A staged threat, played by Mike's friend Trevor, frightens Matt Bailey into confessing. Clifford goes free. Earlier, Harvey had confronted Donna and Jessica for going behind his back. In the final scene Trevor, angry about Mike and Jenny, goes to Jessica to tell her Mike's secret.

suits:S02E01.title: She Knows
suits:S02E01.summary: Trevor has told Jessica that Mike never went to Harvard. She takes Mike to dinner to size him up, checks the records, finds no college degree anywhere, and orders Harvey to fire him. At the same time Alicia Hardman dies, which removes the leverage Jessica and Harvey used five years earlier to push Daniel Hardman out of the firm. Harvey tries to scare Hardman off with the threat of telling his daughter about his affair, but Hardman confesses his embezzlement to the whole firm and walks back in. Harvey then turns Hardman's return into a reason Jessica cannot fire him or Mike. Mike's case of the week is a nuisance suit holding up a merger, which he settles by using the employment contracts of both women involved against them.

suits:S02E02.title: The Choice
suits:S02E02.summary: Hardman moves into a new office beside Jessica's and starts building a following with gifts and perks. Jessica goes on the offensive and sends Harvey to win over Paul Porter, the head of bankruptcy, whose vote she will need if Hardman ever forces a partner vote. Harvey promises Paul he will steer Paul's client into bankruptcy, but instead he and Mike find the lending bank's hidden agenda and force it to extend the loan. The client is happy, Paul is humiliated, and Jessica loses his vote and tells Harvey he may be her biggest liability. Harvey forbids Mike to tell Rachel the truth, so Mike ends their relationship before it starts.

suits:S02E03.title: Meet the New Boss
suits:S02E03.summary: Hardman tells the partners he is only a number two and an adviser, then immediately tries to take over a hospital negotiation with the nurses' union. Jessica lies to hand it to Harvey, and Hardman answers by taking over Harvey's court hearing in front of a judge who is his golf partner. Hardman quietly uses Mike as a back channel to the union leader, and Harvey turns what Mike learns into leverage that forces the nurses to sign. Louis has to rescue the firm's Harvard recruiting privileges after a poor associate survey, and wins back his associates by daring them to leave. Harvey warns Mike that Hardman lied about his wife's cancer five years ago.

suits:S02E04.title: Discovery
suits:S02E04.summary: Travis Tanner, Harvey's old enemy, reopens a four-year-old product liability win and adds a fraud suit against Harvey and the firm, based on an internal memo Harvey says he never saw. Tanner persuades the client, Coastal Motors, to fire Harvey, then leads him to the engineer who shows that CEO Lawrence Kemp lied. Harvey uses the firing to escape privilege and forces Kemp to settle, but Tanner keeps the fraud claim alive. Harvey and Jessica hide the suit from Hardman, who finds out and uses it to insist on a joint defence. Louis borrows Mike for a false-advertising case and shows he can be a formidable litigator.

suits:S02E05.title: Break Point
suits:S02E05.summary: Hardman brings in outside counsel Allison Holt to defend the firm. Holt believes Harvey may have buried the memo and tries to get him to sign an affidavit. Donna finds the memo carrying her own date stamp and shreds it in panic. Mike stops Harvey from signing, and Tanner's settlement terms demand Harvey's disbarment. Hardman leans on Jessica to cut Harvey loose; she makes Hardman fire Holt and then fires Donna herself. In the case of the week Harvey files for a tennis prodigy's emancipation as a pressure tactic, and Mike wins it in court before finding out the boy lied about abuse.

suits:S02E06.title: All In
suits:S02E06.summary: Harvey, still unsettled by losing Donna, takes Mike to Atlantic City to find that client Keith Hoyt has put up his company as collateral on a cocktail napkin and lost it at poker. Harvey loses the first rounds in court to opposing counsel Tommy, who turns Harvey's own arguments against him, so Harvey threatens to wreck the company unless Tommy settles, then beats him at poker for it. Jessica forces a hostile judge, whom Harvey humiliated in law school, off the fraud case with a campaign donation. Louis's ballet client turns out to be embezzling. Mike and Rachel discover from Louis's dictaphone that Louis bugged Harvey's office and passed the Tanner secret to Hardman.

suits:S02E07.title: Sucker Punch
suits:S02E07.summary: After Harvey punches Tanner at a deposition, Jessica runs an in-house mock trial with Hardman as judge and Louis playing Tanner. Its real purpose is to convince the partners that Harvey is innocent. Jury consultant Zoe Lawford, Harvey's old flame, tells him he has to show he cares. Louis breaks Donna on the stand, and Jessica turns Harvey's hidden decency and Louis's grudging respect into evidence. Hardman then finds dirt on Tanner and gets a settlement that clears Harvey but costs every partner $100,000. As soon as the partners vote to settle, he calls a vote on whether Jessica stays as managing partner.

suits:S02E08.title: Rewind
suits:S02E08.summary: In a flashback five years earlier, Harvey is an associate and Mike a slacker taking the LSAT for money. Jessica secretly asks Harvey to find who is stealing from client escrow accounts. Harvey first wrongly accuses Louis, then uses Louis's forensic skill under a cover story and traces the theft to Hardman, who claims the money paid for his wife's cancer treatment. Harvey proves it funded an affair with associate Monica Eton and forces Hardman to resign with a hotel-room ultimatum, and Jessica rewards him with partnership. In the present, Harvey has Mike approach Monica about suing Hardman, so the affair reaches the partners before the vote while Jessica publicly disowns the move.

suits:S02E09.title: Asterisk
suits:S02E09.summary: Days before the managing partner vote, Hardman erases Jessica's one-vote lead by getting a Jessica loyalist (Hanson) a job at the Justice Department, then secretly makes Louis a senior partner to lock in the swing vote. Donna, newly returned, spots the move because Louis is wearing the suit he saved for the day he made senior partner. Jessica sends Harvey to work on Louis first (dinner, the truth about Hardman using him as a fall guy, a Roger Maris 'asterisk' parable), then goes herself but refuses to buy his vote. Hardman, confronted with the fall-guy evidence, admits it and asks for nothing but Louis's conscience. In the case of the week Harvey defends a sportscaster sued for libel by a baseball star, finds the sportscaster's secret source, and forces both sides into a quiet settlement. Mike's grandmother dies at the end of the episode.

suits:S02E10.title: High Noon
suits:S02E10.summary: Louis votes for Hardman, who becomes managing partner. Hardman exiles Harvey and Donna to the 46th floor, and Louis starves Harvey of associates and buries him in dull ERISA work. Jessica refuses Harvey's call to walk out and tells him to wait for a position of strength. While Mike grieves his grandmother, a stoned Harvey and Donna work out that Hardman planted the Coastal Motors memo and set up Tanner's suit against the firm. Louis introduces a partner drug test to fire Harvey; Harvey refuses the test and uses the bylaws to force a hearing, where he traps Hardman in a flat denial and then produces an 'affidavit' (signed by Harvey himself) from the CM executive. The partners vote Hardman out, and Jessica buys his silence with a take-it-or-leave-it confidentiality deal.

suits:S02E11.title: Blind-Sided
suits:S02E11.summary: A longtime client's son, Liam, is in a hit-and-run, and Harvey insists he turn himself in before the police trace his 911 call. The victim dies, the charge becomes a felony, and ambitious ADA Katrina Bennett offers ten years. Mike works out that the victim was dressed in black and fleeing a graffiti scene, so Katrina accepts a misdemeanour plea, then asks Harvey's people for a job at Pearson Hardman. Mike settles generously with the victim's family, learns Liam was high, and breaks privilege by telling Katrina, but Harvey has already hired her, which neutralises the leak. Separately, Louis hires a Harvard first-year, Maria Monroe, who would expose Mike as a fraud, so Jessica imposes a sudden hiring freeze that she frames as a punishment of Louis.

suits:S02E12.title: Blood in the Water
suits:S02E12.summary: After the Hardman civil war, rivals smell weakness. Allison Holt, now at Bratton Gould, poaches Pearson Hardman's best fifth-year associates and courts its clients, including Harvey's tech client Trent Devon. Harvey runs a client-by-client retention blitz, blames Louis for the associate leak and freezes him out, and Louis tries to defect to Bratton Gould, where he negotiates badly. Harvey tells Trent to take Allison's too-good-to-be-true deal but asks to review it; Mike and Louis find it is a scheme to buy Trent's company and dismantle it, so Harvey keeps Trent and signs Allison's hedge fund as a new client. Jessica refuses Harvey's demand to be made name partner, arguing he is a closer and not yet a leader.

suits:S02E13.title: Zane vs. Zane
suits:S02E13.summary: Rachel's father, Robert Zane, takes over the defence of Folsom Foods in a gender discrimination case and tries to cut a signed $10 million settlement to $2 million, going over Harvey's head to tell Jessica the firm 'needs a win'. Harvey puts Rachel in the deposition to unsettle her father; Zane shreds the plaintiff anyway, the client caves and Zane withdraws the offer. Mike and Rachel find sixteen coded words used in every female promotion rejection, turning one plaintiff into a class of 113; Zane counters by threatening to break the class into 45 cases and then proposes a merger, which Jessica rejects with a press release. Katrina and Louis fight a petty war of sabotage before reaching a truce. Zane drops the case for Rachel's sake and hands it to Daniel Hardman.

suits:S02E14.title: He's Back
suits:S02E14.summary: Hardman, working as a contractor for Zane, sues Pearson Hardman on behalf of Monica Eton (his former lover) for wrongful termination, knowing the confidentiality agreement Jessica signed stops the firm from mentioning his affair or embezzlement. He frames Jessica's firing of Monica as gender bias to undermine the firm's Folsom Foods case, and seeds distrust between Harvey and Jessica. Mike's deposition of Monica backfires when she accuses Louis of harassment, a trap Hardman planned. Harvey, Jessica and Mike then depose Hardman off the record and force him to admit the affair. Mike persuades Monica to settle by showing her how her suit hurts the 113 women suing Folsom, but Zane refuses Jessica's merger offer and fast-tracks seven cases at once.

suits:S02E15.title: Normandy
suits:S02E15.summary: The firm's credit line is gone and seven Folsom cases are on the fast track, so Harvey argues for concentrating on one decisive case. Dana 'Scottie' Scott of the London firm Darby International takes the Bakersfield clients and uses them to get Harvey to accept a joint action bankrolled by Edward Darby. Harvey and Scottie secretly open in Parkville, the hardest division to win, but Hardman tracks their flight plan. Scottie's real agenda is a Darby merger that would make her a name partner, and Jessica uses the merger's due diligence to let Darby 'discover' Hardman's embezzlement and tell Hanley Folsom. Katrina and Mike fight over credit, Rachel is rejected by Harvard, and Louis learns his ex, Sheila, sank Rachel's application.

suits:S02E16.title: War
suits:S02E16.summary: Harvey sues three of Darby's clients to wreck the merger, and Jessica turns his defiance into a wager: if Harvey loses, he stays, extends his non-compete and gives up his immediate claim to name partner. Darby 'sportingly' warns he will freeze the clients' assets, which baits Harvey's side into a malicious litigation exposure. Harvey breaks the Chinese wall using Louis's access to merger files; Jessica sits in as Darby's number two and, when Mike gets a winning file from Scottie, forces him to bury it by threatening to report his fraud to the District Attorney. Harvey loses, confronts Jessica and learns she has his loyalty on a leash; Scottie is fired. Louis breaks a pact with his British counterpart, and Mike tells Rachel he never went to Harvard.

suits:S03E01.title: The Arrangement
suits:S03E01.summary: The merger is done: the firm is now Pearson Darby, Edward Darby holds 51%, and Harvey is stuck with a noncompete and a merger he never wanted. Harvey bluffs the Nets into tripling Deron Williams' contract, and Darby forces him onto the case of Ava Hessington, an oil CEO facing a federal bribery charge. Harvey first bargains with Darby to be released if he wins; when the U.S. Attorney recuses himself and hands the case to Harvey's old mentor Cameron Dennis, Harvey reopens the deal and asks for Darby's backing to replace Jessica as managing partner. Mike, frozen out by Harvey for siding with Jessica, traps and then befriends an I.T. worker, recovers the extortion letter Jessica used against him, and hands back the office she gave him. Nigel Nesbitt baits Louis into grabbing the quartermaster job and uses the new firm's bylaws to take the associates from him.

suits:S03E02.title: I Want You to Want Me
suits:S03E02.summary: Harvey tells Donna he means to take the firm from Jessica. Cameron Dennis sends Harvey a silent video of the bribe, hides Ava's number two Nick Howell as a cooperating witness, and leaks the video to corporate raider Tony Gianopolous, who launches a takeover of Hessington Oil. Harvey keeps Ava from bribing Nick, and he and Jessica depose Nick to show Cameron how badly Nick will look at trial; Cameron agrees to the original fine-only deal but insists Ava plead guilty rather than no contest, and they accept. Louis, handed his pick of associates, courts Mike through an 'unwinnable' eminent domain case for Peter's Steakhouse and wins it with a valuation argument. Harvey, who gave Mike away to spite him, takes him back at the end.

suits:S03E03.title: Unfinished Business
suits:S03E03.summary: Cameron arrests Ava for conspiracy to commit murder, using her guilty plea to bribery as the foundation: six protest leaders were killed by the troops of the Colonel she paid. Harvey and Mike work together again and win bail of $1 by exposing Cameron's personal vendetta. Stephen Huntley arrives from London as Darby's fixer; Harvey forces him to admit Darby sent him to help Harvey's coup. Cameron produces five witnesses, Ava fires Harvey when he refuses to bribe them, and Stephen talks her back while Mike neutralises the witnesses through a lawful civil settlement. Harvey hands Louis the takeover fight, Katrina Bennett joins Louis, and Harvey tells Mike about his deal with Darby.

suits:S03E04.title: Conflict of Interest
suits:S03E04.summary: With a takeover vote two days away, Louis wants Ava removed as CEO; Harvey overrules Jessica by invoking Darby's 51% and his authority over the case. Louis's antitrust plan against Gianopolous fails, and Jessica quietly lets him go to the Hessington board, which ousts Ava and keeps Pearson Darby as counsel. Harvey's practice deposition of Ava convinces him and Mike that she is innocent, too late to save her job. Harvey accuses Jessica of acting because she cannot stand being number two, and Jessica openly defies Darby. Donna starts an affair with Stephen, and Mike and Rachel say they love each other.

suits:S03E05.title: Shadow of a Doubt
suits:S03E05.summary: Harvey asks for a dismissal he does not expect and gets the expedited trial he wanted. He plans to knock Cameron off the case by proving he colluded with Gianopolous; Stephen takes over the approach, threatens a London lawsuit, and escalates until Gianopolous retaliates by buying and firing firm clients and dumping Hessington stock. Harvey throws Stephen off the case and goes to Jessica, who designs a deal splitting ownership from control; Gianopolous swears Cameron left him alone with the tape, the tape is thrown out, and Ava is reinstated. Mike and Rachel recover $30 million from an embezzling accountant despite his marrying his bookkeeper to invoke spousal privilege. Jessica puts Harvey's name on the wall.

suits:S03E06.title: The Other Time
suits:S03E06.summary: Flashbacks show Harvey at the D.A.'s office under Cameron, who offers him head litigator while making him bury a toxicology report in a murder case; Harvey discloses it, resigns, returns to Jessica's firm and brings Donna. Jessica recruits him by reading Cameron's counteroffer and showing him how she and Hardman take over a firm in the night. Parallel flashbacks show Mike at college being hustled at poker, selling a calculus test to cover his friend Trevor's debt, and being expelled and denied Harvard. In the present, Cameron claims Colonel Mariga as a witness and offers a plea; Mike discovers Cameron never had Mariga, but Stephen's unauthorised call leads Cameron to him. Harvey tells Jessica about his deal with Darby and says he no longer wants it.

suits:S03E07.title: She's Mine
suits:S03E07.summary: Harvey confronts Stephen, and Jessica takes charge of the case and cuts Darby and Stephen out. Mariga's deposition reveals a phone call Ava never mentioned; Harvey tries to blame Nick Howell, and Mike raids Cameron's files through a fake settlement visit, but the alternative-suspect defence collapses. Jessica confronts Darby, then gets Harvey to admit he confessed partly to turn her against the merger. Louis hides Nigel's cat and loses a mock custody trial on the merits of a trade: Rachel wins the trial, and Nigel swaps the associates back for the cat. Donna catches Stephen spying, and Mike works out that Stephen ordered the killings.

suits:S03E08.title: End Game
suits:S03E08.summary: Darby fires Stephen but refuses to testify that Stephen acted without Ava's knowledge. Mike fails to turn Mariga, Harvey fails to win Cameron over man to man, and Mariga's testimony lands hard; Harvey puts Stephen on the stand, where he takes the Fifth but reveals that Ava once asked him to bribe witnesses. Jessica forgives Harvey and designs the finish: Darby offers to testify, Harvey sells Cameron a plea from Darby as a surer win, and the deal Jessica pre-arranged with Cameron strips Darby of his right to practise law in the U.S., dissolving the merger. Ava goes free. Louis crushes Harold in a settlement fight, is outmanoeuvred on one clause, and is shamed by Rachel into accepting Harold's original offer.

suits:S03E09.title: Bad Faith
suits:S03E09.summary: Pearson Darby Specter is dissolving, and the split of assets will be set by each side's revenue at closing. Jessica sends Louis in as a calm, 'fair' negotiator while Harvey quietly hunts Samsung to tip the revenue totals, but Nigel Nesbitt provokes Louis into signing an agreement that locks client allocations, and Scottie (promised her name on the door by Darby) has already got to Samsung. The firm fights back by pulling revenue into the window: Mike squeezes an early payment out of Robert Zane on Folsom Foods, and Katrina's audacious pitch to Tony Gianopolous lets Harvey and Louis sign him with front-loaded billing. Scottie asks Harvey for mercy and he excludes the Folsom money, but when Hessington Oil fires the firm he assumes she set it up, and she responds by refusing to dissolve at all. The episode ends with the real reason for the firing: Ava Hessington is suing everyone for malpractice.

suits:S03E10.title: Stay
suits:S03E10.summary: Ava Hessington's malpractice suit is run by Travis Tanner, who uses depositions to split Harvey and Scottie by exposing Jessica's attempt to cut Darby loose and by dragging Scottie's private life and a false affidavit from Stephen Huntley into the record. Donna and Mike visit Huntley in prison as non-lawyers so that his admission that he is lying is recorded. Once Scottie lets Harvey off the leash, he deposes Ava, threatens to use her own bribery against her now that she has waived privilege, then apologises off the record and asks her to aim her anger at Darby, and she drops the suit. Jessica discovers Rachel knows Mike's secret and demands she sign an affidavit; Rachel turns the demand into a trade for a waiver of the firm's Harvard-only hiring rule. Rachel chooses Columbia over Stanford, Harvey asks Scottie to join Pearson Specter, and Louis notices Mike's file is missing from the Harvard file room.

suits:S03E11.title: Buried Secrets
suits:S03E11.summary: Scottie negotiates her entry as a senior partner, and Jessica, worried about turnover and Scottie's relationship with Harvey, insists on a $500,000 buy-in paid up front. Scottie tries to change the maths by landing Michael Phelps as a client, Harvey brokers a noncompete in place of the early buy-in, and then secretly pays the buy-in himself, which Scottie discovers and calls manipulation. Mike insists on fighting Nick Rinaldi, the insurance lawyer who settled cheaply with his grandmother after his parents died; Rinaldi rattles him, Mike destroys the opposing expert, and Rinaldi answers with a photo of the deceased drinking and a report showing Mike's own father had been drinking. Louis starts to suspect Mike never went to Harvard; Donna steers him to order the (forged) transcript and then shuts him down by confronting him over how he got the interview list. Jessica gives Harvey her 'two presidents' speech about trust between number one and number two.

suits:S03E12.title: Yesterday's Gone
suits:S03E12.summary: Louis spots Mike's impossible A-plus from Professor Henry Gerard and invites Gerard to lecture at the firm as a test. Mike pre-empts exposure by confessing to a smaller crime (changing a grade), Rachel pleads for him, and Louis agrees to keep quiet only if Mike confesses to Gerard; Harvey's attempt to blackmail Gerard fails when the professor refuses to be coerced, and Harvey finally persuades Louis by invoking the time he covered for Louis as an associate. Meanwhile Jessica and Harvey are co-executors of Quentin Sainz's estate, and Jessica's history with his widow Lisa leads her to send a letter in both their names to stall a sale to Pryzen, which Harvey calls out as a breach of her own trust doctrine. Jessica then learns Pryzen would bury Quentin's ALS drug, drafts a $100 million development-commitment clause that makes Pryzen withdraw, and wins the challenge to her role as executor by testifying honestly about Quentin's intent.

suits:S03E13.title: Moot Point
suits:S03E13.summary: Scottie arrives as senior partner and takes Louis's client transaction (Franklin Courier) on a technicality in his own bylaws, a fight she picks deliberately so she is known as the partner who beat Louis. Louis retaliates with an invented bylaw and an FTC tip that sinks her proposal, and she counters with a bylaw violation that forces him off the matter and reveals she was the one who assigned Nigel against him. Mike gives Harvey a gift: a case against A. Eliot Stemple, the Harvard rival who beat him three times in moot court and has ducked him since, and traps Stemple into staying on it. Stemple runs a rope-a-dope, baiting Harvey into obtaining data that lets Stemple countersue for patent infringement, until Mike works out Stemple's real goal and Harvey forces a public admission of wrongdoing. Jessica keeps Mike's name out of a magazine interview, and Louis calls in the favour Harvey owes him to get Franklin Courier back.

suits:S03E14.title: Heartburn
suits:S03E14.summary: Louis has a heart attack mid closing argument, and Jessica orders that no client ever learns of it. Tony Gianopolous wants a division head who is trying to leave crushed as an example; Mike's spin-off idea is rejected, then Mike quietly tips Tony's number two, Jonathan Sidwell, to a precedent that breaks his non-compete. Harvey forces Mike to enforce it, and Mike kills Sidwell's new job by claiming his algorithm as Tony's property, then hands Sidwell a business solution built on the one thing Tony cannot force: engagement. Rachel learns Louis never recorded his promise that the firm would pay her tuition, discovers from Louis (via a hypothetical) that the verbal promise is unenforceable, and negotiates a new written deal with Jessica using Harvey as precedent. Louis proposes to Sheila, then chooses New York and his 'family' at the firm over Boston, and learns Sheila does not want children. Sidwell offers Mike a job as an investment banker.

suits:S03E15.title: Know When to Fold 'Em
suits:S03E15.summary: Lawyer James Quelling threatens to file a toxic-playground claim against Marathon Footwear on the morning of its IPO. Harvey discovers Quelling is a gambler, beats him at a no-limit poker game to find his tell, and offers a settlement that shuts out copycat plaintiffs, but Quelling digs into Harvey's boast and finds the Hessington witness settlement Mike arranged with Harold Gunderson, raising his price to $2 million. Mike, who has decided to take Sidwell's job, discovers Quelling's suit was funded by the client's competitors and forces him to drop it. At the firm, Charles Van Dyke demands an audit; Katrina covers for a heartbroken Louis with a fix that fails, Jessica fires her, Rachel intervenes, and Jessica rouses Louis, who converts the firm to an LLC overnight while Jessica stalls in court. Mike ends the episode having had Lola Jensen hack him into the New York bar so that he can stay.

suits:S03E16.title: No Way Out
suits:S03E16.summary: US Attorney Eric Woodall, tipped off by Harold's former firm, brings Mike in and offers him a deal to give up Harvey over the Hessington witness settlement. Harvey cannot contact Harold directly, so Mike stages a public argument with Harold to rehearse their story; both are arrested, and Woodall holds them for hours without a phone call on a thin terrorism pretext while he works on Harold's fear. Harvey sends Louis in as Harold's lawyer, Louis keeps Harold from flipping, and Harvey threatens Woodall with malicious prosecution. Jessica and Harvey recognise they are becoming Edward Darby by not wanting to know what their people do; they release Scottie from her noncompete and Harvey tells her the truth about Mike before she leaves. Mike, unwilling to keep putting people in jeopardy, takes Sidwell's job.

suits:S04E01.title: One-Two-Three Go...
suits:S04E01.summary: Mike is now an investment banker at Jonathan Sidwell's fund, and Sidwell tells him to stop hitting singles and bring in a home run. Mike decides to save Gillis Industries, an ailing DVD business, from predators by buying it and keeping it whole, but Harvey mocks the idea and sends a dismissive message through Rachel, so Mike puts Pearson Specter 'in review'. Logan Sanders, the new head of Harvey's biggest client, then walks in wanting a hostile takeover of the same company, and Harvey drops Mike to keep Logan. Meanwhile Jeff Malone from the S.E.C. offers to defend the firm against Eric Woodall's coming revenge campaign if Jessica hires him, forcing Jessica to choose between hiring him and continuing their affair, while Louis waits for Jessica to come to him and loses the job. The episode ends with Mike and Harvey formally at war and Rachel revealing she once had an affair with Logan.

suits:S04E02.title: Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner
suits:S04E02.summary: Mike gets a temporary restraining order against Logan's tender offer by showing that Harvey broke privilege when he moved up the timeline after Mike disclosed his target. Harvey tries to buy Mike off with $20 million and then $30 million, but Logan's arrogance and Mike's promise to Walter Gillis blow the meeting up, and in the process Logan reveals that Mike cares most about the workers. Harvey uses that to flip the union head, Pete Kreeling, with a promise to fund the pension, and Mike answers by persuading Walter to fund the pension himself with his expansion money. Malone joins as a senior partner, takes the corner office and clashes with Louis over the Todd Smith deposition, where the two briefly work well together. Donna gets Jessica to give Louis the corner office to restore his dignity.

suits:S04E03.title: Two in the Knees
suits:S04E03.summary: Logan pushes Harvey to hit Mike 'below the belt'. Harvey first tries to choke off Gillis's credit line by threatening a banker, but Mike blocks it with the threat of a grand jury. When Logan threatens to hire a private investigator to dig into Mike, Harvey instead tells Walter Gillis privately that Mike was once a drug dealer, which breaks their partnership. Mike hits back by buying the master tapes of Harvey's late father's album, using information Donna gave him in confidence, and Rachel uses a debt Logan owes her to stop the personal attacks. At the firm, Malone manipulates Louis to get time alone with Jessica, and Louis finds out.

suits:S04E04.title: Leveraged
suits:S04E04.summary: Mike buys more Gillis stock on margin by leveraging Sidwell's fund, and Sidwell gives him a week to find a new investor or lose his job. Harvey sends Louis to lift the restraining order, but Mike rattles Louis with a doctored photo of Sheila 'engaged' and the order stands. Louis gets revenge by turning Tony Gianopolous against Mike, but his gloating gives Mike the idea that grudges drive investors, and Mike finds Charles Forstman, who hates Harvey. Forstman's money comes with a secret price: cut Sidwell out of the deal. Meanwhile Jessica and Malone force Sean Cahill, the S.E.C. official targeting their clients, to drop seven cases, only to learn his real goal was dirt on Harvey.

suits:S04E05.title: Pound of Flesh
suits:S04E05.summary: Mike tries to use Forstman's promised money to scare Harvey into settling, but Harvey sees that Mike has not yet taken the money and calls the bluff. Both sides chase a block of Gillis shares that Wexler is forced to sell; Malone designs a 'retainer' structure so the firm can buy shares Logan cannot, and Wexler sets up a dark pool auction between Mike and Harvey. When Rachel collapses from overwork, Harvey postpones the sale and has dinner with Mike, but Jessica buys the block behind his back, and Cahill, who has been tailing Harvey, now suspects collusion. Mike tries to back out of the Forstman deal and finds Forstman has already funded Sidwell directly, locking him in. Donna gets Louis through stage fright and then gives him a starring role in her play.

suits:S04E06.title: Litt the Hell Up
suits:S04E06.summary: Cahill hauls Logan into the S.E.C. and accuses Harvey of collusion in front of him. Harvey uses Rachel's knowledge of Logan's board troubles to force a settlement meeting, where Mike agrees to buy Logan out but then demands that Harvey drop Logan as a client, an idea planted by Rachel after she kissed Logan. The deal collapses. Harvey tries to buy Forstman out, but Louis has already unwound the firm's Wexler purchase without Harvey's approval, so Harvey has lost his leverage. Louis then goes to Forstman alone, bonds with him over hatred of Harvey and gets him to sell to Logan. Forstman takes a secret fee arrangement with Louis, and Sidwell learns of Mike's betrayal and fires him.

suits:S04E07.title: We're Done
suits:S04E07.summary: Mike, now unemployed, is offered a job with a $1 million signing bonus by Forstman. Jessica offers Louis any reward except name partner, and Louis first asks for a schedule to win back Sheila, then uses the reward to rehire Mike to stop him working for Forstman. Harvey instantly endorses the choice so Jessica cannot refuse without raising suspicion. Rachel confesses kissing Logan, Logan taunts Mike that she 'loved it', and Mike leaves her. Forstman forces Louis to accept a fee routed offshore so that Louis is complicit. Harvey drops Logan as a client and threatens him to stay away.

suits:S04E08.title: Exposure
suits:S04E08.summary: Cahill arrives with a search warrant for the Gillis files, which Harvey gets revoked because Cahill went to another judge. Mike and Harvey bluff Cahill with a fake list of S.E.C. surveillance requests to prove his tails were unauthorised, but Cahill has Logan, now dropped by Harvey, waive privilege in exchange for immunity. Harvey then turns the fight around by handing over every file under court catalogue and filing a malicious prosecution claim at the same time. That exposes Louis, who has hidden the offshore Forstman payment in those files. Forstman offers to let Louis put the blame on Harvey, Louis refuses, and Katrina forges a replacement document. Rachel tells Mike to decide whether he loves her more than he hates what she did, and Mike starts to suspect Louis.

suits:S04E09.title: Gone
suits:S04E09.summary: Louis admits to Harvey and Jessica that Charles Forstman forced him to route money offshore and to take a million dollars himself, just as SEC director Sean Cahill is about to comb the firm's Gillis takeover files. Harvey fails to bully Forstman into undoing the deal, so the firm goes on the offensive with a malicious prosecution case, deposing Eric Woodall and exposing his history of deciding guilt first. Cahill hits back by revealing Jessica's relationship with Jeff Malone and, in depositions, deduces that because neither Harvey nor Mike got paid, someone else did. Louis confesses to the SEC against orders, but Woodall waves him away, which tells Harvey and Mike that Woodall is protecting Forstman. They hand Cahill the evidence and let Woodall's refusal to open his bank accounts do the rest. Jessica resolves to fire Louis anyway, and Louis resigns first.

suits:S04E10.title: This Is Rome
suits:S04E10.summary: Louis, jobless and cut off from his clients by the partnership agreement, begs for three clients and Jessica refuses on precedent grounds, pre-emptively having Katrina contact all of Louis's old clients. Harvey finds Louis jobs in Cincinnati and Boston, but Louis's attempt to win Sheila back fails. Mike gets Louis an interview with Robert Zane, who offers senior partnership if Louis can poach a client from Pearson Specter, and Louis, fed by Katrina, uses a by-law notice loophole to sign VersaLife at the moment Harvey is hiding an antitrust problem from them. Mike and Harvey win VersaLife back by persuading Walter Gillis to buy VersaLife's drug-trial division, dropping it below the market-share threshold. Jessica forces Katrina out, and Louis, noticing Mike does not recognise the Order of the Coif key, works out that Mike never went to Harvard and demands his name on the wall.

suits:S04E11.title: Enough Is Enough
suits:S04E11.summary: Jessica agrees to make Louis a name partner under threat of exposure, but asks him to keep it quiet while she sells it to the partners. Louis instead tells Robert Zane, forces an immediate announcement, and sets out to break Mike by burying him in paralegal work and then attacking Rachel. Zane deduces that Louis must have leverage and uses the threat of gossip to collect the favor Harvey promised, which Harvey pays by asking Scottie to settle a case, costing him their relationship. Jessica tells Jeff Malone a substitute secret (her cover-up of Hardman's embezzlement) to explain Louis's rise. At the unveiling Louis insisted on, Jessica produces a partnership agreement that names Louis a co-conspirator in hiring a fraud, disarming his leverage before he can sign.

suits:S04E12.title: Respect
suits:S04E12.summary: Henry Gerard, Harvey's old ethics professor, asks for help after being accused of taking a bribe as mediator of the Liberty Rail compensation fund, and Mike talks Harvey out of refusing on grudge grounds. Harvey turns the opposing lawyer's national security defence into a way to have Gerard testify under seal, but Mike spots that Gerard's poker alibi does not add up, and Gerard admits he took $25,000 to change a student's grade. Harvey recasts the payment as a loan by squeezing the student, and he and Gerard end with a mutual silence over Mike and Gerard's gambling. Meanwhile Louis demands one of Harvey's clients as the price of backing Jessica's cover story to Malone, blunders with cosmetics CEO Joan Walsh, and is rescued by Rachel's legal fix before learning Harvey had dumped Joan on him.

suits:S04E13.title: Fork in the Road
suits:S04E13.summary: A flashback episode. Harvey and Louis, as fifth-year associates, pitch Daniel Hardman on making both of them junior partners, and Hardman counters by making them compete over McKernon Motors. Harvey wins Avery McKernon by reading that he values loyalty, but Hardman uses the McKernon pursuit to lure the larger Fletcher Engines, and Louis feeds Fletcher Harvey's game plan to win the partnership. In the present, Harvey tricks Louis into a road trip to McKernon with Mike, engineering a blow-up that ends with Louis and Mike reconciled. A parallel flashback shows Mike lying to a law student, Claire, about being at Columbia and being caught, and Jessica hiring Rachel despite knowing she is Robert Zane's daughter.

suits:S04E14.title: Derailed
suits:S04E14.summary: Gerard sends Mike a Liberty Rail whistle-blower, Joe Henderson, and Harvey reluctantly lets Mike take the case. Mike demands a public admission, but Liberty Rail's lawyer Evan Smith produces an exonerating report and Henderson's sealed history of prior whistle-blower claims. Donna, reasoning that the sensors must have been replaced, talks her way into Liberty Rail's file room and brings back maintenance records, which Harvey and Mike use to trap the CEO in a deposition. Evan then reveals she has video of Donna in the file room. Jeff Malone, bonding with Louis over drinks, catches a timeline slip that proves Jessica lied to him, and ends the relationship.

suits:S04E15.title: Intent
suits:S04E15.summary: Harvey tries to trade the Liberty Rail case for Donna, but Evan refuses and ADA Terrance Wolf investigates Donna for impersonating the NTSB, a fact Donna had hidden from Harvey. Liberty Rail pays off Henderson with a sealed settlement, and Harvey argues fraud needs damages that Evan cannot prove without incriminating her client, so Wolf escalates to an intent charge carrying three to five years. Mike and Rachel revive the civil case with a new plaintiff, the train's engineer Jaworski, who was made the fall guy. Harvey outbids Liberty Rail for Henderson's story and uses it to force Evan to make the witness against Donna change her testimony, trading away the case. Jeff Malone resigns, and Harvey tells Donna he loves her before leaving.

suits:S04E16.title: Not Just a Pretty Face
suits:S04E16.summary: Flashbacks show how Donna joined Harvey at the DA's office and how Charles Forstman tested young ADA Harvey, extracted an inside tip about DuPont, shorted it and tied Harvey to the trade by secretly funding his gambler brother Marcus. In the present, Cahill cannot find Woodall's money, so Harvey reasons it went to someone Woodall cares about, and Rachel finds Woodall's first wife, Mary Ann, in a Forstman-funded care home. Harvey pressures Woodall, then confronts Forstman, who threatens to expose the 12-year-old tip and Marcus, not knowing Harvey is wearing a wire while Cahill listens. Louis grieves Norma with Donna's help, Mike proposes to Rachel, and Donna leaves Harvey's desk to work for Louis.

suits:S05E01.title: Denial
suits:S05E01.summary: Donna leaves Harvey's desk to work for Louis, and Harvey refuses to admit it matters while secretly seeing a psychiatrist (Dr. Agard) after a panic attack. Harvey takes on Kevin Slattery's trucking company two weeks from bankruptcy, demands 20% equity as his fee, and with Mike forces the largest creditor to buy up all the other debt by threatening to move the fleet to Canada through a defunct Canadian company bought for a dollar. One creditor, Katzen Financial, is missed because of a printer error and sells its debt to Slattery's chief rival, so Harvey salvages the company by letting the rival take the trademark. Jessica warns Harvey that Jack Soloff, an ambitious senior partner, is telling the firm Harvey cannot deliver. Donna establishes herself on Louis's desk by sending an early-arriving client home and landing him anyway.

suits:S05E02.title: Compensation
suits:S05E02.summary: Jack Soloff, new head of the compensation committee, proposes weighting pay toward billable hours, a change aimed at Harvey's contingency-heavy earnings, and times it for a meeting Jessica will miss. Louis lets the proposal come up so he can publicly defend Harvey, but Harvey rebuffs him, reveals he has been topping up Donna's salary for years, and Louis, now on the hook for that money, switches sides and leaks Harvey's income statements via the copier so Jack can win the vote. Harvey stops his friend Teddy Doyle selling his sneaker company cheaply to Adidas after his new secretary Gretchen works out Teddy is grieving, and doubles the offer. Mike takes a class action against Kelton Insurance that Jessica refuses to fund, signs Robert Zane's prenup to show his character, and ends up recruiting Zane as co-counsel. Harvey tells Louis he will one day take Donna away from him.

suits:S05E03.title: No Refills
suits:S05E03.summary: Jessica orders Harvey to make peace with Jack, but Jack rejects Harvey's offer of golf with Charles Barkley, so Harvey uses Barkley to poach one of Jack's clients and threatens four more. Jack blackmails Louis into backing a new proposal to abolish contingent pay, and Harvey answers with a bluff that Jack's other clients are already in play, which Mike makes credible until Jack backs down. Jessica negotiates the Kelton co-counsel terms with Robert Zane, trading fees for a demand that Zane treat Mike as a partner, and tells Jack she personally sent Harvey after him. In court Zane pushes for an expedited trial against Mike's wishes, and Mike wins the motion by reciting any page of a 5,000-page complaint from memory. Harvey has a second panic attack in front of Mike and returns to Dr. Agard, who makes him voice his anger at Donna.

suits:S05E04.title: No Puedo Hacerlo
suits:S05E04.summary: Kelton offers $25 million; Zane wants to take it and Mike wants trial, so Zane goes over Mike's head to Jessica and the clients and settles. Mike spots that a subsidiary of Arcadian, the hedge fund funding the suit and Zane's client, bought Kelton shares, and Rachel forces Arcadian to divest those shares to the plaintiffs, saving her father from an insider trading scandal. Louis hands Harvey his sister Esther's divorce as a peace offering, and Harvey accepts on two conditions, the second left open. Harvey keeps Esther out of the negotiation, stops her from committing perjury, puts her 50% promise on the record himself, then exposes that her husband never got into medical school, and settles at 25%. Harvey sleeps with Esther after the case closes, breaking a promise to Louis, then cashes his open condition to get Louis to fix the compensation vote.

suits:S05E05.title: Toe to Toe
suits:S05E05.summary: Harvey faces Travis Tanner, who claims to be a changed man and opens with a settlement offer for his client Alyssa Lang, accused of taking IP from her employer BetaSoft. Harvey attacks first by buying Lang's debts and padlocking her offices, but Tanner reveals Lang signed her contract at 16, kills the TRO, and produces a draft sexual harassment complaint against BetaSoft's CEO. Harvey escalates to criminal charges, punches Tanner after Tanner mocks Donna and Harvey's mother, and Mike resolves the case by getting Tanner to step aside so Katrina can present the same deal. Louis tries to reverse the compensation vote by faking the signing of a big client to buy Jack's support, but Jack sees through it and uses Louis's own proxies to freeze all policy changes for 12 months. Louis confesses to Jessica that he leaked Harvey's salary, and Jessica turns that confession into a trap that forces Jack to accept the reversal.

suits:S05E06.title: Privilege
suits:S05E06.summary: Harvey represents Sam Tull, a trader his firm is blaming for unauthorised trades, and threatens Butler Trading with a malicious prosecution suit. Butler calls Tull's company therapist, who turns out to be Harvey's own psychiatrist Dr. Agard, and Harvey destroys her credibility in deposition using a confession she made to him in therapy, then later wins her help with a bluff. Louis and Mike uncover a buried EPA problem at Range Tech, the company their client Dominic Barone of McKernon Motors wants to buy, and try to arrange an alternative through Jack's client Tanaka; Jack demands the whole fee, then sabotages the deal, gets them fired for a day, and signs McKernon's rival Fletcher Engines in the gap. Jessica orders Jack to drop Fletcher and reveals she knows Daniel Hardman is advising him. Donna gets Mike and Rachel The Plaza for their wedding by impersonating a French wedding planner and leaning on the groom of the booked couple.

suits:S05E07.title: Hitting Home
suits:S05E07.summary: Hardman is back in New York and tells Jessica she hurt herself by dropping Fletcher, a story Jack spread through the firm; Jessica nearly fires Jack, then pairs him with Mike on a pension fund case against Straussbank to learn how deep his Hardman ties go. Jack trades away criminal charges to get Straussbank's emails fast, planning to catch them destroying evidence, and Mike fabricates incriminating emails to bluff an executive into giving up the CEO, fooling Jack as well. Louis defends Esther against a serial frivolous litigant by counter-suing and then paying the plaintiff to turn on his own lawyer. Donna warns Harvey to confess to Louis that he slept with Esther and lies to Louis to cover for him; Harvey refuses, rejects Esther, and when Louis learns the truth and taunts him about his childhood, Harvey hits him. Jessica tells Mike he must turn down the junior partnership Jack has nominated him for.

suits:S05E08.title: Mea Culpa
suits:S05E08.summary: Louis threatens to sue Harvey and demands a suspension, so Jessica sends Harvey on a vacation backed by a conveniently old leave request to let Louis cool off. Mike cannot find a believable reason to decline partner, and Jessica makes him junior partner and gives him his first case, where the opposing lawyer Claire Bowden is a woman who knows he never went to law school. Harvey apologises to Louis and reveals his panic attacks, Louis invites him back for Mike's partnership vote and then announces a suspension in front of the partners, but Jack blocks it with Louis's own bylaws and schedules a vote; Donna finds that Louis secretly recorded Harvey's confession and threatens to quit if he uses it. Rachel fronts the case for Mike, blows up the deal with an aggressive threat, then rescues it by bringing in GigaDyne, a defence contractor whose involvement triggers background checks. Claire spots Mike's name being removed from the paperwork, and Rachel's plea persuades her not to report him, though Claire warns Mike to let Rachel go. Hardman sends Jack an ultimatum.

suits:S05E09.title: Uninvited Guests
suits:S05E09.summary: Harvey survives the partners' vote on suspending him for punching Louis when it splits 8-8, after he publicly apologises and cuts his own pay to the median. Jack Soloff immediately proposes letting Daniel Hardman back in exchange for sharing a billion-dollar client; Jessica refuses, so Hardman turns the client into a weapon and launches a hostile tender for McKernon Motors, Harvey's oldest client. Mike and Harvey counter by taking McKernon private with money from Tony Gianopolous, only for Hardman to top them thanks to a Japanese client and a strong yen. Harvey realises the timing does not add up and traces the money to Charles Forstman in prison, who says he will pull his funding only if Harvey resigns. Meanwhile Louis and Donna fail to find what Hardman has on Soloff, Jessica tells Soloff to resign, and Mike's wedding plans strain his cover with Rachel's mother; an old friend, Trevor, tells Mike he should quit.

suits:S05E10.title: Faith
suits:S05E10.summary: Soloff calls an emergency no-confidence vote to remove Jessica, and Hardman forces Louis to vote against her by threatening to buy and destroy his sister Esther's company. Harvey spends the day with his therapist, Dr. Agard, working through the memory of telling his father about his mother's affair, and decides whether to accept Forstman's price. Mike, in flashbacks to his parents' death and his school days, seeks out Father Walker and resolves to stop practising. Harvey arrives at the vote with Forstman's letter firing Hardman, tells the partners the coup was funded by a man behind bars, and Jessica keeps her job with only Soloff opposed. Afterwards Harvey tells Jessica he agreed to step down, Mike hands Rachel his resignation, and Mike is arrested for fraud.

suits:S05E11.title: Blowback
suits:S05E11.summary: AUSA Anita Gibbs interrogates Mike overnight and denies him his lawyer, and Mike turns her demand for a taped confession into evidence of her misconduct. Gibbs sends Robert Zane in as Mike's lawyer to push him to turn on Harvey; he refuses. Jessica keeps Harvey's resignation secret and has him represent Mike so their communications are privileged, but Harvey's attempt to trade Mike's resignation letter for leniency backfires when Gibbs uses it to try to remove him as counsel, and Mike saves him with a camera's serial number. Soloff circles to take the firm, until Mike threatens to tell Gibbs that Soloff knew about him. Louis fires Donna so she can return to Harvey, and Harvey prepares to return to the office.

suits:S05E12.title: Live to Fight...
suits:S05E12.summary: Gibbs arrests Donna's father on an old bank-fraud issue to pressure Donna, and subpoenas every document the firm has ever touched. Harvey and Mike force Gibbs to reveal her source, an anonymous email from a Harvard address, which Louis recognises as the work of his ex-girlfriend Sheila Sazs; she refuses to retract it. Mike gets Professor Gerard to sign a vaguely worded letter, and Harvey trades that bluff in chambers for the charges against Donna's father being dropped. Harvey's secret history of coercing Donna's father seven years earlier comes out and strains their relationship. Jessica rebuilds trust with Mike through Jeff Malone, and the episode ends with Sheila coming forward and the subpoenas granted.

suits:S05E13.title: God's Green Earth
suits:S05E13.summary: Harvey's demand for discovery gets the trial set in two weeks, and Gibbs buries the defence in boxes. A Wall Street Journal op-ed claims a name partner must have known, clients are circled, and Jessica rejects Soloff's pro bono idea in favour of poaching a department, which fails because nobody wants to join a firm that may not survive. Gibbs ambushes Rachel with a dangled deal and a threat to her bar prospects, then gets the Columbia dean to threaten her with expulsion; Mike blackmails David Green, an old LSAT client now in Gibbs's office, for proof and forces Gibbs to back off. Soloff gives Jessica the file Hardman had on him, Louis sends Sheila to Argentina to keep her off the stand, and Mike announces he will represent himself just as the defence learns Gibbs has found Trevor.

suits:S05E14.title: Self Defense
suits:S05E14.summary: Harvey stages a mock trial against Mike, playing Gibbs, on the bet that if he wins he represents Mike in court; both sides use fabricated documents, and Harvey savages Rachel on the stand. Gibbs tracks Louis's trips to Sheila and threatens witness-tampering charges, Jessica answers with a restraining order, and Gibbs gets the trial moved up. Rachel persuades Mike to let Harvey lead because the jury can hate Harvey but not Mike. In the real trial Harvey dismantles Trevor's credibility, Donna takes the Fifth, and Jimmy Kirkwood lies for Mike as a rebuttal witness before Gibbs impeaches him. Harvey concludes they will lose, and Gibbs secretly offers Louis a way out.

suits:S05E15.title: Tick Tock
suits:S05E15.summary: Mike takes over his own defence midway through the trial on the grounds that he has been co-counsel from day one, and calls the mother of Clifford Danner, the innocent man he freed, who has since been killed. Mike gives a candid closing that admits he wasted his gift, and Gibbs answers with a hard case that he is a fraud. While the jury deliberates, Harvey reads Gibbs's demand for a mistrial waiver as proof she cannot retry the case and tries to force a mistrial through David Green, who refuses. Mike takes on a petty theft defendant, Diaz, who later takes a deal to testify against his friends. Louis secretly records Harvey admitting he hired a fraud and approaches Gibbs, then drops the plan; Gibbs offers Mike two years in prison or immunity in exchange for a name partner, and Mike goes to accept a deal.

suits:S05E16.title: 25th Hour
suits:S05E16.summary: Mike pleads guilty to two years in exchange for immunity for the partners, with a clause that stops Gibbs renegotiating with Harvey. Robert Zane sets out to empty the firm: Katrina Bennett records Louis admitting he knew, the morals clause frees partners from their noncompetes, and Jack Soloff defects. Harvey learns from the jury foreman that the verdict was not guilty, lies to Mike that it was guilty, then tries to trade Gibbs the Liberty Rail murder case for Mike's freedom at the cost of letting Evan Smith raid the firm; Gibbs refuses because she wants Harvey himself. Jessica makes peace with Zane so Rachel's parents come to the wedding, but Mike calls off the wedding so Rachel can finish law school, and he leaves for prison.

suits:S06E01.title: To Trouble
suits:S06E01.summary: Mike reports to Danbury prison on the day he was meant to marry Rachel, and the firm discovers that every partner and employee has walked out. Within hours Pearson Specter Litt is served with a $100 million class action over every case Mike touched. The name partners fight among themselves until Donna and Rachel shame them back together, Harvey apologises for hiring Mike, and they pool their personal fortunes into a war chest. When the departed partners hack the client files and move to bifurcate the firm to recover their buy-ins, Jessica and Harvey decide to use that buy-in money to settle the lawsuits. In prison, a friendly 'cellmate' who wins Mike's trust turns out to be Frank Gallo, a man Harvey put away 13 years ago, who now has Mike's story and Rachel's phone number.

suits:S06E02.title: Accounts Payable
suits:S06E02.summary: Gallo baits Mike into attacking him in front of a guard, costing Mike his visitation, and then taunts Harvey from inside the prison. Harvey breaks his promise to Mike by threatening Gallo, then leans on federal prosecutor Sean Cahill to get Gallo moved. Jessica and Harvey settle the class action for ten cents on the dollar using the partners' buy-in money, but Jack Soloff, now at Robert Zane's firm, tips attorney Elliott Stemple to an excluded class member who can blow up the deal. Stemple reads that Harvey's duck painting matters to him and takes it as his price, and Harvey hands it over to save the firm. Mike stays in public view and stalls Gallo's attack until his real cellmate Kevin brings a guard, and Jessica quietly lends Soloff the money for his new buy-in.

suits:S06E03.title: Back on the Map
suits:S06E03.summary: Louis sublets empty floors to a group of crude traders led by Stu Buzzini, tries to evict them over a lease clause about his prune juice, and is overruled when Harvey trades Stu a better lease for market intelligence. Harvey refuses to represent William Sutter, a billionaire facing an SEC indictment, and tries to land energy CEO Nathan Byrnes instead; when Sutter secretly buys 5% of Nathan's company to scare him off, Harvey buys in too and forces Nathan to hire him. Rachel is humiliated in an ethics class over Mike, pressures her classmate into a public apology, and moves to an Innocence Project death row case. Gallo beats up Kevin to get to Mike, and Mike answers with a carrot and a stick: a parole motion for Gallo backed by the threat of exposing him as an informant. Cahill then offers Mike early release if he informs on Kevin, whose father-in-law turns out to be the target.

suits:S06E04.title: Turn
suits:S06E04.summary: Mike refuses to inform on Kevin, the one friend he has inside, and sends his refusal through Donna so Harvey cannot pressure him. Harvey and Cahill stage a poisoning with the warden and prison doctor so they can take Mike out of Danbury on an ankle monitor, and Harvey then drives him to Rachel instead of to Cahill's planned briefing on the victims. Faced with the life he is giving up, Mike tells Rachel everything and takes the deal. Jessica punishes Stu for dumping Nathan Byrnes' stock by tanking one of his positions with a well-timed press release, and turns him into a client. Rachel meets death row inmate Leonard Bailey and wins over a sceptical Professor Dunbar with two boxes of prosecutorial misconduct evidence, while Louis falls for architect Tara Messer and invents a Hamptons house to keep her around.

suits:S06E05.title: Trust
suits:S06E05.summary: Harvey takes Sutter as a client so he can steer the case from inside, and makes himself Kevin's lawyer too. He forces Cahill to indict by threatening to sue the SEC for harassment, Cahill counters by suspending Sutter's trading license, and Louis routes Sutter's trades through Stu's firm as a new holding company. In court Harvey moves to have Cahill removed for bias, and Cahill neatly blocks it; privately they congratulate each other. Kevin learns Mike left the prison for hours, so Mike has the warden stage an interrogation of Kevin that makes Mike's cover story believable, and Kevin finally admits he is in for drunk driving. Harvey becomes Gallo's attorney and uses the role to force Gallo to protect Mike, while Rachel takes Leonard Bailey's case to the firm and Jessica agrees to take it for the sake of the firm's image.

suits:S06E06.title: Spain
suits:S06E06.summary: Sutter admits his biggest trades have nothing to do with the algorithm Kevin wrote, and Harvey beats Cahill's subpoena for it by showing a pattern of Cahill's past fishing expeditions. Jessica corners Sutter in a public restaurant into giving the firm all of his business, which Sutter then uses to force Harvey to move for dismissal. Harvey offers Cahill the algorithm in a fast-food bag, and Cahill refuses it but buys time with deposition subpoenas.
