Mike plays Cahill in a practice deposition to drive a wedge between Kevin and Sutter, then catches the hole in Kevin's story and learns that Kevin's wife Jill was part of the insider trading. Rachel discovers Leonard hid that he and his alibi witness were high, and Louis's fake-house scheme collapses in front of Tara, who is charmed by his confession.

suits:S06E07.title: Shake the Trees
suits:S06E07.summary: Cahill wins a trial date by using the leaked algorithm to show that Sutter's billion-dollar trades fall outside it. Harvey interrogates Sutter's staff to scare out the insider, Louis traces the leaks to a consulting bank, and Donna gets Stu's database by showing she knows all his contacts. The insider, Phillip Allen, runs to Cahill and gets a deal, and Cahill's superiors then pull Mike's deal. Mike has Donna lure Jill to Danbury under a false pretext and urges her to come clean, which enrages Kevin. Gallo works out that Mike is informing and threatens to expose him, while Rachel asks her father for a favour as a lawyer and finds that Leonard's alibi witness is dead.

suits:S06E08.title: Borrowed Time
suits:S06E08.summary: Harvey wins a three-day delay after Cahill introduces Phillip Allen without disclosing him, then dismantles Allen in a mock cross-examination to force Cahill to reinstate Mike's deal. Mike confesses to Kevin that he has been informing, gets beaten, and uses Gallo's parole hearing as leverage to get Kevin out of solitary. Harvey offers Sutter a deal to protect his daughter, records him refusing, and plays the recording for his other client Kevin with Jill in the room. Jill turns on her father with Mike negotiating her immunity and getting Cahill to put Mike's credit in writing, and Sutter is forced into a plea. Jessica and Rachel buy Leonard Bailey another month through his sick aunt, at the cost of Leonard's trust in Jessica, and Mike calls Rachel to say he is coming home.

suits:S06E09.title: The Hand That Feeds
suits:S06E09.summary: Mike's release from Danbury is delayed while Sean Cahill seizes everything Kevin and Jill Miller own, including money Jill earned before the insider trading. Harvey reluctantly represents Frank Gallo at his parole hearing to honor the deal that bought Mike's protection inside, while former DA Cameron Dennis vows to keep Gallo locked up. Mike threatens Cahill with an abuse-of-power suit to free Kevin, gets his own deal pulled in retaliation, then trades testimony against Gallo to Cameron in exchange for Kevin's release, sparing Harvey from perjuring himself. Mike secretly delays his own release to catch Gallo on a hidden camera trying to kill him, and Harvey uses Cahill's power to pin Gallo down with a two-door choice. Meanwhile Jessica forces Leonard Bailey's original public defender to sign an affidavit, gets the case reopened, and extracts a seven-year plea offer, but Rachel persuades Bailey to fight for full exoneration. Louis waits anxiously while Tara turns down Joshua's proposal.

suits:S06E10.title: P.S.L.
suits:S06E10.summary: Mike comes home and Harvey offers him a consulting job at junior partner pay. Robert Zane tips Harvey that Jim Reynolds, the firm's founding client, is taking meetings with other firms: board member Donald Mannis is using William Sutter's rumor that Harvey threw Sutter's case to oust Reynolds and the firm together. Jessica refuses to leave the Bailey retrial for the board meeting, so Harvey forces Sutter to recant by revealing his house is about to be seized, and Harvey and Louis bring Stu Buzzini, now Reynolds's largest shareholder, to overrule Mannis. In court Rachel questions Bailey, the victim's father testifies against him, and Jessica breaks the father with an invented roommate until he admits he paid the alibi witness to disappear; Bailey is exonerated. Jessica turns down Zane's merger offer, announces she is stepping down from the firm she built, and leaves for Chicago, while Louis proposes to the pregnant Tara.

suits:S06E11.title: She's Gone
suits:S06E11.summary: With Jessica gone, Harvey and Louis are running a firm with no managing partner. Mike turns down Harvey's offer, finds that every clinic application asks about felony convictions, and briefly teaches at his old Catholic school until parents have him removed. Robert Zane offers a merger and predicts the partners will fight over Jessica's chair; Louis takes it as an insult, recruits Katrina Bennett to bring ten of Zane's best associates over, then overreaches by targeting Zane's biggest client before learning Zane had quietly waived their noncompetes. Harvey asks Anita Gibbs to support Mike's future bar application, and she sees through him and promises to block Mike from any clinic. Harvey explodes at Louis, Louis admits he is not ready to lead and formally offers Rachel an associate job, and Donna tells Harvey to reconcile with his mother.

suits:S06E12.title: The Painting
suits:S06E12.summary: Harvey travels to Boston to make peace with his mother Lily, intercut with flashbacks to his father's funeral years earlier; the first dinner collapses into mutual blame, but after his brother Marcus reveals that Lily and her husband Bobby cared for him through a cancer relapse, Harvey apologizes and reconciles. In New York, Nathan hires Mike to supervise his Queens legal clinic at a fraction of his market value, and Mike clashes with Marissa, a law student who assumes he is a burned-out corporate lawyer. Mike tells the whole staff the truth about his fraud, and he and Marissa build a case for a single mother, Sofia Price, facing eviction, but opposing counsel humiliates Oliver in court with a staged phone call and wins an eviction deadline. Mike pays Sofia's back rent himself. Donna gets Louis to help Harvey's client Teddy Doyle, and on his return Harvey proposes that he and Louis serve as co-interim managing partners, keeping Jessica's name on the door.

suits:S06E13.title: Teeth, Nose, Teeth
suits:S06E13.summary: Mike and Rachel set their wedding at Harvey's place. Rachel is denied a character and fitness interview, and Harvey discovers the committee member responsible, Craig Seidel, is holding her hostage to get someone to sue his competitor Velocity Data Solutions and crash its stock. Harvey has Louis investigate, learns Velocity stole Seidel's technology, forces a confession of an affair, and makes Seidel clear Rachel's path while offering to do his lawsuit only in exchange for a hearing for Mike. Mike's clinic case for Sofia Price unravels: he misses the rent deadline, wins a $25,000 settlement, then tries to reopen it for $100,000 when his client wants more, and opposing counsel Linda Johnson crushes Oliver at trial. Donna and IT man Benjamin build an AI assistant called The Donna, and Louis struggles with Joshua's role in Tara's pregnancy. Mike first refuses Harvey's plan, then, after watching Oliver lose, agrees.

suits:S06E14.title: Admission of Guilt
suits:S06E14.summary: Harvey structures the Velocity suit to run through Mike's clinic with a demand for an admission of guilt, and orders Seidel to get Mike a bar hearing by 'reading the law'. Mike and Oliver find sealed settlements with dying miners, Mike wins over their former supervisor, and when Velocity CEO James Palmer threatens to fight every NDA separately, Mike bluffs that Pearson Specter Litt is co-counsel and Harvey makes it true with 150 separate suits. Rachel passes character and fitness and makes Harvey promise to pull the plug if things get risky. Palmer rejects Harvey's $500 million demand, deduces the Seidel connection and declares the quid pro quo a crime; Harvey then discovers Seidel sold the secrets himself and turns the leverage on him. Louis, stood up by Harvey, brings Rachel and Katrina to a key client meeting and loses the client, and Oliver works out Mike's real motive.

suits:S06E15.title: Quid Pro Quo
suits:S06E15.summary: Mike withdraws his bar application rather than drop the miners, which removes Palmer's collusion threat, but Palmer then gets ten of Pearson Specter Litt's clients to threaten to leave, the firm withdraws, and the offer falls to $10 million. Harvey and Louis pay Louis's old fixer Jerry, who identifies the woman who seduced Seidel as a headhunter who does this for Palmer, and Harvey recruits Rachel (behind Mike's back) to confront her. Mike is furious but agrees to use the evidence, and Harvey forces Palmer to pay the miners $200 million and honor his original deal with Seidel, which Harvey then uses to make Seidel fight for Mike's admission. Donna walks away from Stu Buzzini's demand for 90% of The Donna, fails to win over professional investors who dismiss her as a legal secretary, and then gets Stu back on fair terms. Louis confesses to Tara that he used Mike's secret to make name partner, and the conversation turns into a fight.

suits:S06E16.title: Character and Fitness
suits:S06E16.summary: Anita Gibbs gets onto the character and fitness committee as Walter Samson's hand-picked replacement and warns that Mike will never get her vote. At the hearing Rachel invokes an obscure rule to allow a rebuttal witness, and prison psychologist Julius Rowe defends Mike and accuses Gibbs of prejudging him, while Harvey fails to find any dirt on Samson. Gibbs offers Harvey a trade (Mike's admission if Mike names Harvey as knowing about the fraud), which Mike refuses. Jessica flies in, admits she knew, and reminds Gibbs of the mercy she once showed Samson's godson, and Mike is admitted. Mike confesses the quid pro quo to Nathan and keeps his job only because Oliver speaks for him; Louis negotiates a buyout for The Donna after a patent problem and Donna admits she wants 'something more'; Harvey closes Mike on returning to Pearson Specter Litt, on Mike's terms.

suits:S07E01.title: Skin in the Game
suits:S07E01.summary: With Jessica gone, Harvey has quietly told Mike he is head of the firm but has not told Louis. Mike returns from the clinic on a 'one for you, one for me' pro bono deal, and Donna asks Harvey for a seat at the partnership table. Harvey and Mike run an auction for Neil Stillman's vodka division, then discover Stillman is dumping it ahead of a recipe-theft lawsuit and is threatening to fire them if they do not close. After Mike tells Harvey he is hiding in Jessica's shadow, Harvey stops the sale, turns Stillman's threat around, grants Donna's partnership request, and at a snap partners' meeting defends her and gets Louis to accept him as managing partner. Louis, raw from Tara's breakup, abuses the associates and eventually hands them to Rachel.

suits:S07E02.title: The Statue
suits:S07E02.summary: Harvey sets out to show the world the firm is his: he offers his friend Alex Williams a name partnership in exchange for bringing over Pfizer, which means dropping Jessica's oldest client. Louis tries to poach Pfizer behind his back and then calls Jessica, whose vote Harvey needs; Jessica tells Harvey he is rushing. Harvey reverses himself, gives Alex a take-it-or-leave-it senior partner offer, and withdraws Donna's partnership, which she converts into a COO title with a vote. Mike's insurance case for a widower is ambushed when opposing counsel shows the judge his fake Harvard diploma; Mike and Rachel pay corporate spy Holly Cromwell for an internal memo, threaten a class action, and trade away an admission of guilt for a public story about his redemption.

suits:S07E03.title: Mudmare
suits:S07E03.summary: Alex joins the firm, and Louis swings between courting him and panicking that Alex will replace him as Harvey's friend. Harvey and Alex force a merger partner's lawyer out after catching a hidden escape clause. Mike takes the case of a father whose son died in a private prison, gets a guard to talk, and files suit, but Alex's client Masterson Construction (which builds those prisons) demands the case be dropped. Harvey breaks his word to Mike, Mike hands the case to Oliver at the clinic, and Harvey makes him sign a written wall. Donna undercuts Rachel in front of an insubordinate associate, Stephanie Patel; the two reconcile, and Rachel later fires Stephanie privately.

suits:S07E04.title: Divide and Conquer
suits:S07E04.summary: Donna warns Harvey his honeymoon as managing partner is over: Louis, Mike and she are all angry with him. Jessica advises him to give Louis new business, and then, unknown to Harvey, tells Tommy Bratton of Bratton Gould how to play Harvey against Louis. Bratton poaches Louis's client and sues one of Harvey's, and the partners unite, swap roles and fight off the first wave. Bratton threatens a far bigger assault, Robert Zane refuses Harvey's request for a fake merger, and Alex ends the war privately by threatening to expose a secret he and Bratton share. Mike coaches Oliver into a bluff that produces a suspiciously generous settlement, persuades Oscar Reyes to refuse it, and finally agrees to work the growing class action in secret.

suits:S07E05.title: Brooklyn Housing
suits:S07E05.summary: Mike secretly works the prison class action with Oliver while telling Harvey and Rachel he is on a housing case. Harvey signs energy client Rick Dunn with a bold promise to stop Lockwood launching a copied solar panel, then has to lean on Holly Cromwell to deliver. Harvey asks Louis to defend Paula against her ex-partner's lawsuit; Louis wins her trust, uncovers the full story and destroys the ex's blackmail threat with proof of stalking. Donna uses her COO authority to vet Holly and ends up losing the hire. Mike recruits Frank Gallo, the inmate who once tried to kill him, by offering money for Gallo's estranged daughter, and Nathan reveals he knew all along that Mike was breaking his agreement.

suits:S07E06.title: Shame
suits:S07E06.summary: Mike keeps working the prison case, pressures a former prosecutor into handing over records, and pays Gallo for information. Harvey learns of the Gallo connection, confirms Mike's involvement through the client, and orders him off the case. Stephanie sues Louis for harassment; Katrina negotiates a settlement Louis refuses because it requires an admission, and Louis finally ends the suit with a sincere apology. Alex exposes Mike's breach in open court and the clinic is thrown off the case. Harvey tells Donna he is seeing Paula, and Donna pretends she already knew.

suits:S07E07.title: Home to Roost
suits:S07E07.summary: Alex tells Harvey what Masterson and Bratton have on him, and a long flashback shows Harvey's days as a sixth-year associate: Louis is promoted over him, Jessica tells him to play the long game, Harvey goes behind Louis's back on a trial and Jessica publicly removes him, and he accepts a Bratton Gould offer through Alex, only to renege when Jessica backs him. In the present, Mike tries to take the prison scheme to Anita Gibbs as a criminal case and has Benjamin pull evidence from Reform Corp's server. Harvey signs Reform Corp as a client to shut Mike down and threatens to fire him. Alex finally tells Mike the truth: Bratton framed him in a cover-up that included a guard's murder.

suits:S07E08.summary: Mike and Harvey agree to stop Reform Corp and save Alex at the same time, and Harvey quietly hands the case to Robert Zane, who refuses to be anyone's puppet and makes an enormous demand. Gallo refuses Mike's money because he wants to testify for his daughter's forgiveness, so Rachel's plan is used: Harvey produces Gallo's old photos of Rachel in court to block Gallo's testimony, enraging Zane. Gallo is murdered in his cell, and Harvey and Zane use a recorded confession, now admissible, to force Reform Corp's CEO into a settlement and a written confession implicating Tommy Bratton. Harvey and Alex use that confession to take back Alex's affidavit and force Bratton to resign. Donna meets an ex, Mark, who is married, and Louis turns down a last fling with Sheila.

suits:S07E09.title: Full Disclosure
suits:S07E09.summary: Mike wants Harvey to stop playing defence, so he signs Elmont Investments, a client already being pursued by the new Deputy Attorney General, Andrew Malik. Malik turns out to be an old colleague from the DA's office with a grudge against Harvey. Harvey records Malik saying he doesn't care whether the CEO is innocent and uses the tape to get a 24-hour ultimatum from the judge. Malik answers by leaking a newspaper story about a damning memo and then announces that Harvey has buried evidence before, which puts Donna in line to be subpoenaed over the Clifford Danner case. Meanwhile Louis's associate Brian lets an opponent's insult about his parenting push him into a drafting error that wrecks a patent case, and Robert Zane brings Rachel into a predatory-lending suit that is really about a personal debt to his late sister.

suits:S07E10.title: Donna
suits:S07E10.summary: Louis finds a work-product privilege argument to keep Donna off the stand, so the firm cancels her mock-trial preparation. Malik gets around it by asking about the Coastal Motors shredding instead, and humiliates Donna by suggesting she slept her way to COO. Donna works out that Malik planted the memo story through Holly Cromwell, and Harvey and Mike force Malik to drop the case by threatening to put his own character on trial. Malik retaliates by getting Jessica disbarred. Rachel rescues her father's deposition disaster by going straight to the defendant's board with a settlement that makes the directors personally liable, and Alex fakes a surrender to Eli Gould to get him on tape admitting he engineered a takeover to get round their non-poaching agreement.

suits:S07E11.title: Hard Truths
suits:S07E11.summary: The firm needs to pay Jessica out without triggering claims from the old partners, which means restructuring, and the bylaws require one of the old founding partners to sign off. Harvey pitches Stanley Gordon a cover story and pays Gordon's price by pressuring a charity to put his name on a building. Gordon sees through the cover story and demands to come back as name partner. Louis works out that Gordon really wants Jessica humiliated, and Harvey signs a public statement condemning her. Louis tries to blackmail a bar ethics official into delaying the disbarment announcement and fails. Mike turns down a suspiciously easy $30 million offer for Quality Foods, and with Rachel's help finds that the trucking company is dumping cargo and reselling the space.

suits:S07E12.title: Bad Man
suits:S07E12.summary: Jessica asks for $2 million of her payout in an untraceable account and won't say why. Donna pushes Harvey to get it by calling in a decade of unpaid legal work from Vic, his late father's producer, which forces Vic to sell his jazz catalogue to Driscoll Records, where Harvey then has to fight a new executive over the price. Mike tries to broker a quiet deal for his friend Oliver against a firm client and doesn't disclose the friendship. Oliver rejects the deal, beats Mike in a deposition, and then loses to Mike's 'either way you lose' contract argument. Louis works through his history with unavailable women with Dr. Lipschitz, and at the end of the episode he resumes the affair with Sheila.

suits:S07E13.title: Inevitable
suits:S07E13.summary: Teddy Doyle asks Harvey to save the workers at his old shoe factory after Kurt Baxter buys the company and plans to move production overseas. Mike's supplier deal fails because Baxter only wants to sell to a Chinese buyer. Donna persuades Stu Buzzini to short Baxter's stock, and Harvey and Mike offer Baxter two ways out. Baxter refuses on principle, so Harvey has Teddy raise the money by offering the employees equity through their pension fund. Paula tells Harvey she can't stay with him while he works beside Donna. Harvey quietly gets Stu to offer Donna a job, Donna sees through it, and in the end Harvey tears up her resignation and ends things with Paula.

suits:S07E14.title: Pulling the Goalie
suits:S07E14.summary: Judge Ralls, who presided over Mike's fraud trial, asks Mike to defend her against a misconduct complaint. Harvey and Mike work out that the complaint is a plan by Smith and Devane to remove her from the bench so her past rulings can be reopened. Donna is tricked by the landlord, David Fox, into signing a letter that voids the firm's lease, and then beats him by buying the air rights in front of his most prized buildings. Louis provokes Sheila's fiancé Zander into a legal duel over printer cartridges, wins a humiliating settlement, and then drops it when Sheila asks. By the end Sheila leaves Zander for Louis.

suits:S07E15.title: Tiny Violin
suits:S07E15.summary: Stanley Gordon sues on behalf of the old partners, using the firm's own statement condemning Jessica as proof that they were damaged by association. Harvey gets Jack Soloff to drop out by threatening to read his bad performance review into the record. Donna's research then shows Gordon's real plan: bring the partners back so they can vote to merge the firm into Rand Kaldor Zane. Mike joins Nathan's clinic on a lead-poisoning class action and plays hardball on settlement until Discharge Power gets the clinic's donors to pull out. He then persuades Nathan to drop non-profit status, and Louis anonymously gives the clinic $500,000. Jessica asks Harvey to come to Chicago, and before he leaves he makes Mike promise to put the firm ahead of the clinic.

suits:S07E16.title: Good-Bye
suits:S07E16.summary: In Chicago, Harvey and Jessica fight developer Pat McGann and City Attorney Keri Allen over a housing project. Allen exposes the fact that the plaintiff is Jessica's aunt, and McGann gets Harvey removed on a procedural technicality. Jessica then springs a trap: she has photographs of McGann handing her a $1 million cashier's check, which was really her own money. The mayor answers by offering her a job, on condition that she drops the suit, and she accepts. In New York, Alex's attempt to use Eli Gould fails because Gordon has more on Eli. Mike talks Robert Zane into merging his loyal partners into the firm, which Zane does in secret before Gordon can act. Mike wins the lead-poisoning case by exposing an insurance policy that matches the settlement offer. Mike and Rachel marry and leave for Seattle.

suits:S08E01.title: Right-Hand Man
suits:S08E01.summary: With Mike gone to Seattle, Harvey saves the firm by merging with Robert Zane, and the question of who will be managing partner becomes a live fight. A conflict between Harvey's client and Zane's client (Dexterol and Clavatin) turns into a proxy war: Harvey sends Alex Williams, dangling his promised name partnership, while Zane sends his fixer Samantha Wheeler. When Alex starts losing, Harvey breaks his word to stay out and takes the case to Judge Thomas himself; Zane uses that broken promise to argue only one of them is managing-partner material, and Harvey concedes the job. In parallel, Katrina uses an algorithm to cull post-merger associates, clashes with Louis over Brian Altman, and learns from Donna that some people's value does not show in the numbers. Samantha ends the episode by demanding Zane make her name partner before the year is out.

suits:S08E02.title: Pecking Order
suits:S08E02.summary: Harvey signs over managing partner to Zane, while Louis, pushed by Sheila to seize the throne, lies to her about getting the job and then finally demands that Harvey and Zane treat him as an equal. Mike's old clients from Pod Space come to Harvey because 50 million dollars is missing; Zane secretly sends Samantha to shadow Harvey, and her methods (a cash test, forcing Max out, a bank-driven IPO) clash with Harvey's until her fix works. Donna and Samantha spar over an expense account and Donna quietly investigates Samantha's contradictory background. Alex, told by Zane to impress him with a big client, goes after Gavin Andrews of Starboard Airlines despite Samantha's warning. The episode ends with Harvey learning that Zane promised Samantha the next name spot, the same promise Harvey made to Alex.

suits:S08E03.title: Promises, Promises
suits:S08E03.summary: Harvey tells Zane about the double promise and they agree to kick the can down the road. Alex's courtship of Gavin Andrews turns into a trap: after Alex recovers Gavin's Renoir, Gavin announces the firm as his counsel and demands help laundering 55 million dollars, and Samantha, whom Alex had pressured Louis into making drop Delta Airlines, rescues him by taking control of Gavin's Cayman trust. Harvey takes up a cleaning woman's overtime claim against the firm's landlord David Fox, who retaliates against the firm and fires her; Donna closes the dispute with a class action and a deal that commits Harvey to a year of free work for Fox. Katrina, told she can make senior partner by proving she can manage, hides stress migraines, lets Brian take the blame, then confesses to Louis to protect him.

suits:S08E04.title: Revenue Per Square Foot
suits:S08E04.summary: Louis is mugged at gunpoint, hides it from Zane, misses a client meeting and loses the client to Samantha, then freezes in court mid-cross when the memory returns. Harvey brings Alex to Paxson BioScience, which wants help choking off a rival; the two decide to represent the target instead, Zane orders them to sign Paxson and threatens Alex's future, and Alex finds a third route by signing the target's star scientist. Donna quietly arranges for a headhunter to call Alex so everyone learns where they stand, and tells Zane his leadership style is the reason Rand and Kaldor turned on him. Harvey gets Louis to admit what happened, and Zane shares a secret from his own youth to help Louis recover.

suits:S08E05.title: Good Mudding
suits:S08E05.summary: Harvey goes to Boston to represent his brother Marcus in a divorce, discovers Marcus hid a gambling relapse and asked his daughter to keep it secret, walks out, then returns and wins shared custody by showing Katie the ammunition he will not use. Alex brings his suspended daughter Joy to work and asks Samantha, the cool one, to connect with her; Samantha uses Joy's secret recording of opposing counsel in a coffee shop to break a patent deposition, and Alex is furious. Louis learns he must give up mudding to improve his odds of conceiving, and Sheila uses Gretchen to test whether he will. Alex and Samantha finally admit to each other that they were both promised the next name spot.

suits:S08E06.title: Cats, Ballet, Harvey Specter
suits:S08E06.summary: Harvey, raw from Marcus's divorce, takes Louis's client Joan Walsh while Louis is with Sheila, sues a 16-year-old influencer out of anger, and refuses couples therapy with Louis until Dr. Lipschitz helps him see he fears being left behind. Samantha takes on Donna's charity as a way to make peace, spots a small fundraising anomaly, runs an unauthorized test that gets Donna's friend Peggy fired, and then partners with Donna to force out the corrupt CEO. Katrina, told this case will secure her senior partnership, works Emmet Ford's blocked IPO with Brian, using a deposition to expose the exchange chairman's grudge and then a procedural tell to prove he lied. Donna notices Katrina and Brian are getting close.

suits:S08E07.title: Sour Grapes
suits:S08E07.summary: Donna's deal makes Harvey represent David Fox, who wants to secretly buy a rival's building; Harvey's straw-man buyer fails, Harvey nearly drops Fox over hidden payments, and Donna tells him that dropping Fox makes her a liar. Samantha steps in and, with Harvey, finds a clause in the rival's investor agreement that forces a sale. Upstate, Zane asks Alex to sue the barrel supplier he believes sabotaged his vineyard for racial reasons; Alex extracts a damaging admission, then advises de-escalation and is fired, until Zane comes round and proposes a shared community tasting room. Louis and Sheila celebrate a pregnancy, fight over raising the child Jewish, get engaged, and then learn it was a false positive.

suits:S08E08.title: Coral Gables
suits:S08E08.summary: Samantha, trying to regain ground with Zane, uses the False Claims Act to pry a client away from Eric Kaldor, who gets her disqualified with a billing sheet showing she once worked for that client. Harvey helps her counter by threatening to subpoena Kaldor's billing records, but Kaldor finds Betty Palmer, a former employee Samantha ran out of town after burying evidence in a criminal case, and uses her as blackmail. Harvey forces Samantha to give up her client rather than silence Betty, and Samantha turns the loss into a senior partnership for Betty. Gretchen's failure to send a signed document costs Alex a client, and the client demands she be fired. Louis discovers the top fertility specialist is his high-school bully and works through it with Dr. Lipschitz.

suits:S08E09.title: Motion to Delay
suits:S08E09.summary: Tommy Bratton, forced into retirement by Robert and Harvey's Frank Gallo tape, sues the firm for $20 million, claiming they paid Gallo for fabricated testimony. Louis tries to use the Alex tape to turn Eli Gould against Bratton, Donna visits Gallo's daughter, and Robert confronts Bratton, reading the case as a bluff; Bratton responds with a trial date. Harvey learns Bratton has terminal cancer and threatens endless delay, which only hardens Bratton, who then dies of a heart attack. Meanwhile Samantha and Alex go to war over Gavin Andrews and Dexhart Insurance, Samantha cashes in a favour with Louis, and Louis and Harvey back Alex for name partner against Robert. New senior partner Katrina, with associate Brian, beats a fashion knock-off company, and Harvey and Robert agree to let Samantha and Alex settle the name-partner question in one head-to-head case.

suits:S08E10.title: Managing Partner
suits:S08E10.summary: Samantha and Alex go to trial against each other (Dexhart Insurance v. Starboard Airlines), with the winner promised the next name on the wall. Alex speeds the trial up, Samantha gets around their no-privilege rule through a publicly filed divorce document, and Alex obtains a buried report by having Katrina request it from Dexhart. Flashbacks show how Samantha protected Robert from a money-laundering scandal at his old firm by stonewalling the FBI and installing Rand and Kaldor, which is why Robert owes her. When Robert breaks his word to Harvey and moves to put Samantha's name up, Donna turns an office confrontation into a formal partner vote, installs Louis as managing partner, and Louis promotes both Samantha and Alex to name partner.

suits:S08E11.title: Rocky 8
suits:S08E11.summary: Louis starts as managing partner and delegates so heavily that Donna accuses him of abdicating. Harvey and Robert take on Andrew Malik (the prosecutor who went after Jessica) by defending boxing promoter Jim Allen against fight-fixing charges, then discover that the fighter, Ricky Crosby, threw the fight himself because of brain damage. Louis finds the way through: threaten Malik with a wrongful-prosecution compensation claim unless he gives Ricky a deal and publicly apologises. Alex saves Louis's client Thomas Kessler from a ruinous contract by spotting that Kessler's general counsel planted the clause on purpose, Samantha pressures Katrina over the leaked Dexhart report, and Donna finds Kessler a new general counsel and catches his eye.

suits:S08E12.title: Whale Hunt
suits:S08E12.summary: Louis asks Harvey to land a big client, Steven Palmer, who rejects Harvey for not listening. Harvey lies to Louis about his progress, Louis goes around him, and the two end up fighting at Palmer's charity poker game before making peace and each telling Palmer to sign with the other. Samantha teams up with Alex's wife Rosalie on a for-profit college case, breaking a witness in deposition, but Rosalie accepts a low settlement after the school claims poverty, and Alex backs his wife over Samantha. Katrina and Brian find that their perfume opponent rigged its focus groups, but the late night working together at Brian's home forces them to admit their feelings, and Katrina ends their working relationship. Donna and Thomas Kessler start dating.

suits:S08E13.title: The Greater Good
suits:S08E13.summary: Stu Buzzini is blackmailed by one of his traders, Nick Pavonotti, over the Teddy Doyle stock trade Harvey and Donna asked him to make. Harvey's attempts to scare Nick off (posing as a consultant, getting Kevin Miller to offer him a job) only show Nick that Harvey is exposed, and Nick finds Donna's name in the visitor log. Cahill refuses to bury the matter, but Donna's idea of asking him a different question ends with Cahill using his prosecutorial discretion to make Nick back off. Samantha's former foster mother Judy asks for help on a drug charge she took for a foster son; Samantha learns Judy gave her up years ago, then wins a deal by showing the prosecutor her own juvenile record. Katrina and Brian agree on a face-saving plan for him to move toward junior partner.

suits:S08E14.title: Peas in a Pod
suits:S08E14.summary: Dana Scott (Scottie) returns, fishes information out of Harvey at a coffee cart, and uses it to embarrass Samantha in a judge's chambers. Samantha and Katrina discover that Scottie's client has been creating fake accounts; Scottie, complicit, goes to Donna for help, and Donna gets Harvey to lean on Samantha in exchange for Scottie staying away from the firm. Alex undermines a grieving widower in a medical-device case, then finds a software glitch his client wants buried, and hands the file to the widower himself. Louis takes over Dr. Lipschitz's malpractice defence and resolves it by approaching the patient as a fellow patient, at the cost of losing Lipschitz as his therapist. Donna tells Louis, and then Harvey finds out, that she is seeing Thomas Kessler.

suits:S08E15.title: Stalking Horse
suits:S08E15.summary: Harvey's client Simon Lowe offers Thomas Kessler a mall anchor deal, then reveals to Harvey that it was a ploy to bring Restoration back to the table, and orders silence under privilege. Harvey and Alex try to fix it quietly, but Donna, fearing Thomas will lose a better offer that expires in the morning, tells him. Thomas takes the other deal and publishes his reasons, Restoration demands a discount, and Simon fires Harvey and hires Daniel Hardman to sue the firm. Louis testifies against the man who mugged him, the case is thrown out on a warrant error, and Samantha forces the mugger to confess by threatening his family's housing, which alarms Robert. Katrina wins Brian's first client with a bluff, and Brian leaves the firm to protect his marriage.

suits:S08E16.title: Harvey
suits:S08E16.summary: Hardman uses Simon's lawsuit to try to extract an admission that Harvey broke privilege, which he plans to use to take Harvey's licence, and his price for stopping is his name back on the wall. Harvey and Louis get the suit dropped by showing Pierpont's chairwoman that Simon planned to oust her, but Hardman responds with an ethics hearing. Robert tries to buy Hardman off with a seat at Rand Kaldor, and flashbacks reveal that eight years ago Robert and Samantha put away the man who mugged Samantha, who was later killed in prison. At the hearing Robert, with Alex's help, takes the blame for the privilege breach, forfeits his licence and retires. Donna tells Thomas she cannot cut Harvey out of her, and Harvey is left realising what she means to him.

suits:S09E01.title: Everything's Changed
suits:S09E01.summary: The morning after Harvey and Donna get together, the firm reels from Robert Zane taking the fall for the privilege breach that Donna actually committed. Clients start leaving: Thomas Kessler fires Alex, Eric Kaldor of Rand Kaldor poaches Robert's clients by spreading the word early, and the New York Bar's Steven Faulkner leans on Alex to take Zane's name off the wall, then offers him managing partner if he will act against Louis. Samantha discovers Harvey spent the night with Donna, demands he give his clients to Kaldor, and the two settle it with a boxing match and a pact to keep Robert's name up. Louis and Alex, pushed by Katrina and Sheila, try to get Harvey's vote to take the name down, Samantha threatens to go to the Bar, and Harvey pays Kaldor off with his own clients to hold the line. The episode ends with Faye Richardson arriving with a court order that gives her full control of the firm as special master, on pain of a six-month suspension for every partner.

suits:S09E02.title: Special Master
suits:S09E02.summary: Faye Richardson takes charge, gives the partners a list of the firm's sins, orders Zane's name removed on day one and claims approval over all new cases and firm resources. Harvey and Donna tell Louis they are together, then scramble to stop Faye interviewing Kessler about why he left: Harvey persuades Kessler to stay by answering honestly about Donna, and when Kessler backs out Donna tells Faye the personal truth about her affair with him, which closes the inquiry. Samantha takes a pro bono wrongful termination case for Lucas Hodges, a fellow veteran with hidden PTSD, and after the company uses his own secret as leverage she hires him through her own shell company on condition that he gets treatment. Louis orders Benjamin to find a loophole in the Bar's bylaws, Benjamin hacks them, Faye catches it, Louis tries to fire Benjamin, and Faye strips Louis of his title as managing partner.

suits:S09E03.title: Windmills
suits:S09E03.summary: Louis is demoted and Faye makes herself acting managing partner, then asks Donna to be her secretary, and Donna hands the work to Gretchen. Harvey signs CEO Dan Foley by pitching a shared enemy, sues the board, runs a full-page ad, and Dan gets fired, which Harvey wrongly blames on Faye before fixing it through an old friend who buys the company and rehires Dan. Susan tries to blackmail Katrina over Brian Altman into making her an associate, and Katrina calls the bluff by walking Susan into Faye's office. Sheila quietly arranges a judgeship offer for Louis, who nearly takes it before realising his colleagues are what he would lose, and Samantha proposes and Alex refuses a scheme to get Faye removed by inducing a client to leave.

suits:S09E04.title: Cairo
suits:S09E04.summary: Faye rules that Donna must give up her vote because of her relationship with Harvey, and recruits Katrina to write a firm code of conduct. Alex's old colleague Craig Cameron blackmails him with the Bratton Gould prison cover-up, and flashbacks show how Tommy Bratton handed Alex a prized client and a bonus to make him the fall guy. Alex finally tells Rosalie, who goes to Samantha for dirt on Craig, and Samantha confronts Craig herself, then chooses to beat him on the merits. Harvey's first attempt to win over Donna's father James, by fixing his deal behind his back, backfires, and his second, built on respect, succeeds. The partners use a conflict waiver added to Katrina's code of conduct, plus a threat of mass resignation, to make Faye back down on Donna's vote, and Harvey proposes to Donna.

suits:S09E05.title: If the Shoe Fits
suits:S09E05.summary: Mike Ross returns from Seattle representing basketball star Jeremy Wall, who wants out of his endorsement deal with Brick Street, now Samantha's client. Harvey and Mike agree to fight fair, and Harvey and Samantha appear to win by exploiting a contract deadline and waiving a jury, but Mike has planned the whole thing: his ad baits a defamation suit, he leaks a sealed deposition, and the goal is to free Jeremy to start a rival company. Samantha then fabricates evidence through the activist Charles Hu to win, Harvey refuses to betray her to Mike, and the Harvey and Mike friendship fractures. Louis's anonymous donation to rescue Sheila backfires and couples therapy reveals her doubts about her career. Faye accuses Harvey of fabricating the evidence, Samantha refuses to let him take the blame, and Faye fires Samantha.

suits:S09E06.title: Whatever It Takes
suits:S09E06.summary: Faye Richardson fires Samantha without proof after seeing Harvey berate her for fabricating evidence against Mike, then calls Donna to ask her to stop the partners retaliating. Harvey and Louis agree to do 'whatever it takes' to remove Faye and find her ex-husband George, who claims she used his ethics violation as leverage to take his money in their divorce; Gretchen gets emails proving Faye asked the Bar to quash his investigation. Faye reveals she did it to keep her daughter from learning her father was a criminal, and Donna talks Harvey out of using it. Samantha, meanwhile, trades Gavin Andrews to an FBI agent in exchange for dirt on Faye, using his niece's blackmail to get Gavin to trust her; Robert Zane forces a blanket immunity deal but the agent delivers nothing. Katrina faces her former associate Brian in a founder-ouster suit, uses their own working relationship to win discovery of the plaintiff's personal emails, and ends the case with a countersuit threat.

suits:S09E07.title: Scenic Route
suits:S09E07.summary: Harvey drives Samantha to Pittsburgh to find her biological father, and flashbacks show her childhood in foster care and her affair with Eric Kaldor; she learns she was never given up, because her mother died. Back in New York, Louis answers Harvey's phone as a prank, gets trapped pretending to be Harvey with celebrity client Ted Tucker, and ends up blackmailed by Harold Gunderson, now in-house counsel at a company Tucker buys to erase a conflict. Louis refuses Harold's escalating demand, discovers Harold only wants his job back, and finally tells Tucker the truth, signing him as himself. Donna trades favors with Alex (who trades part of one to Katrina) to get a forgery made and swaps it for a painting Harvey loves. Harvey reconciles with Samantha over the fabricated evidence and, back home, calls his mother to forgive her.

suits:S09E08.title: Prisoner's Dilemma
suits:S09E08.summary: Andrew Malik arrests Sean Cahill for conspiring with Harvey two years earlier to swap Mike's release for Cahill's conviction of William Sutter, and Harvey makes himself Cahill's lawyer so their talks are privileged. Faye tries to take the case from Harvey, Kevin Miller has given Malik an affidavit, and Harvey traces the real source to Charles Forstman, Sutter's last cellmate, who claims a deathbed confession. Malik arrests Harvey too and plays them against each other; Cahill takes Malik's deal through Faye. Harvey then finds that Sutter died instantly of a heart attack and that Forstman called Malik minutes after Harvey's visit, so Cahill and Harvey arrest Malik for fabricating evidence. In a parallel story Louis learns Paul Richmond assaulted his sister Esther years ago and is now forcing a merger on her company; Katrina and Samantha flip the company lawyers who arranged his victims' NDAs, and Esther forces him to resign. Louis proposes to Sheila, and Donna tells Harvey his mother has died.

suits:S09E09.title: Thunder Bolt
suits:S09E09.summary: After his mother's funeral, Donna recruits Mike to reconcile with Samantha and sue Faye for wrongful termination, a suit that would remove Faye. Faye counters by making Harvey and Louis defend her on a secret promise: win honestly and she leaves; cheat or tank it and she goes to the Bar to dismantle the firm. Mike beats their motion to dismiss with a later paragraph of the bylaws, Harvey and Louis humiliate Faye in a mock trial to 'prepare' her, and Louis savages Samantha on the stand. Katrina secretly feeds Mike Faye's sealed prior lawsuit and quotes from the mock trial, and Samantha uses them to destroy Faye on cross. Faye, believing Harvey cheated, demands he prove Samantha fabricated evidence; Katrina confesses to protect him and Faye fires her. Harvey spends an evening with Mike, then serves him with a subpoena.

suits:S09E10.title: One Last Con
suits:S09E10.summary: Harvey crosses Mike using his perfect memory to establish that Faye had the same gut certainty Mike had, but Faye still insists on putting Harvey on the stand. Harvey confides in Mike, who proposes 'one last con': Katrina threatens to testify that Faye fired her for refusing to collude, Faye asks Harvey to shut her down, Harvey insists the deal be put in writing, and during a staged fight Gretchen swaps the document for one ordering Harvey to tamper with a witness. Faye still refuses to fold, so Harvey closes alone by offering what she always wanted: he and Donna leave the firm. Louis and Sheila marry as her water breaks and their daughter Lucy is born; Harvey and Donna marry the same night. Samantha returns as name partner on her own conditions, Katrina Bennett is made a name partner, and Harvey and Donna leave for Seattle to work with Mike.

vikings:S01E01.title: Rites of Passage
vikings:S01E01.summary: Ragnar Lothbrok, a farmer and raider in Kattegat, wants to sail west instead of east, and secretly acquires a sun board and sunstone that make open-ocean navigation possible. At the local assembly (the thing), Earl Haraldson uses a legal technicality to condemn a man whose land he wants, then publicly refuses Ragnar's request to raid west because he owns the ships. In private he warns Ragnar that farms are easy to take from those who embarrass him, and sets a watcher on him. Ragnar and his brother Rollo agree to go anyway as equals, and the boat-builder Floki launches a new, lighter ship built for long voyages.

vikings:S01E02.title: Wrath of the Northmen
vikings:S01E02.summary: Ragnar and Rollo recruit a crew of young men at a secret meeting, but one of the men present, Olafur, reports it to Earl Haraldson, who chooses to watch and wait. Haraldson tests Olafur's loyalty by offering him his wife Siggy, and has him killed when he accepts. Floki threatens the blacksmith's daughter to keep him quiet, but Haraldson extracts the truth anyway. At sea the crew nearly mutinies during a storm and after days without land, until seabirds appear and they reach Lindisfarne, sack the monastery, and Ragnar spares the English-speaking monk Athelstan.

vikings:S01E03.title: Dispossessed
vikings:S01E03.summary: The raiders return rich, and Earl Haraldson claims the whole haul as his by right, letting each man take one item. Ragnar, seeing that the Earl is looking for a reason to kill them, chooses the monk Athelstan and questions him about England's kings and towns. He then uses that knowledge to persuade the Earl to sanction a second raid, offering all the plunder to Haraldson and calling himself expendable. The Earl agrees on condition that his man Knut goes along to watch Ragnar and learn his navigation method. Haraldson buries treasure with a sacrificed boy, and Siggy flatters his sense of power.

vikings:S01E04.title: Trial
vikings:S01E04.summary: Ragnar times the attack on the English town of Hexham for Sunday Mass, then defeats a Saxon force with a shield wall, provoking King Aelle of Northumbria. During the raid Knut rapes a Saxon woman, attacks Lagertha and is killed. On their return Haraldson arrests Ragnar for murdering Knut, his half-brother and agent, and privately works on Rollo's resentment, offering treasure and hinting at marriage to his daughter Thyri. At the trial Lagertha claims she killed Knut, and Haraldson's star witness Rollo swears Ragnar's account is true, forcing an acquittal. Haraldson's men then attack Ragnar.

vikings:S01E05.title: Raid
vikings:S01E05.summary: Haraldson raids Ragnar's farm; Ragnar is badly wounded and his family flee to Floki's hidden home, where he recovers. Haraldson confiscates Ragnar's ship and marries his daughter Thyri to the old Swedish Earl Bjarni, a cousin of King Horik, for silver and alliances. Rollo approaches Haraldson asking to be included in the raids, but Haraldson later imprisons and tortures him to find Ragnar, turning Rollo into bait. Siggy secretly warns Rollo and gets word to Ragnar, who responds by challenging Haraldson to single combat.

vikings:S01E06.title: Burial of the Dead
vikings:S01E06.summary: Haraldson first rejects Ragnar's challenge as beneath him, then accepts after remembering the seer's prophecy. Privately he admits Ragnar was right about the west but that supporting him would have cost Haraldson his followers. Ragnar kills Haraldson in the duel and is hailed as Earl; he takes oaths of fealty, lets the men vote to take the old warrior Tostig raiding, and gives Haraldson a great funeral. Rollo offers Siggy protection and proposes marriage. In England, King Aelle executes the commander Lord Wigea in a snake pit for his defeatism.

vikings:S01E07.title: A King's Ransom
vikings:S01E07.summary: Ragnar leads three ships up the Tyne into Northumbria, digs in, waits, and destroys the army of Aelle's brother Lord Aethelwulf in a night attack, taking him hostage. Aelle's council splits between fighting and paying the raiders off. Ragnar dines with the king and demands two thousand pounds of gold and silver; Aelle agrees, but insists on a baptism and a truce while he 'collects' the money, and meanwhile raises more men. Rollo is baptised as a joke, the delivered chests are empty, and a Saxon ambush follows, which the Northmen defeat. Aethelwulf is sent back dead and Aelle declares eternal war on Ragnar, while in Kattegat Lagertha settles a village dispute and takes in Siggy, and loses her pregnancy.

vikings:S01E08.title: Sacrifice
vikings:S01E08.summary: Grieving the loss of his unborn son, Ragnar takes his household to the nine-yearly festival at Uppsala. There he meets King Horik, flatters him, pledges fealty and proposes joint raids west, using Athelstan as proof that the rich kingdom of Frankia exists. Horik accepts and immediately asks Ragnar to act as his emissary to Jarl Borg, who is pressing a claim to Horik's land. Siggy works on Rollo's resentment of being left out. Athelstan is considered as a human sacrifice but rejected because he has not truly renounced his God, and Leif volunteers in his place.

vikings:S01E09.title: All Change
vikings:S01E09.summary: Ragnar negotiates with Jarl Borg in Gotaland; Borg opens hostile, warms when he learns who Ragnar is, and proposes creative compromises that Ragnar has no authority to accept. Borg keeps Rollo as security while sending Ragnar on a trip to a famous ash tree, and uses the time to court Rollo. On the trip Ragnar meets Aslaug, sets her a riddle test, and is tempted into an affair that Bjorn discovers. King Horik refuses any deal, Borg declares war, and Rollo agrees to fight alongside Borg against his brother. Meanwhile a fever spreads through Kattegat.

vikings:S02E01.title: Brother's War
vikings:S02E01.summary: Rollo fights for Jarl Borg against Ragnar and King Horik, kills Arne, then refuses to strike his brother and throws himself on Ragnar's mercy. With the battle a stalemate, Horik offers Borg a third of the disputed lands; Borg refuses until Ragnar reframes the quarrel as a waste of young men and proposes they all raid West together instead. Ragnar declines to judge his own brother and hands Rollo to the Law-Giver, who spares him because the gods spared him in battle. Aslaug arrives in Kattegat pregnant with Ragnar's child; Ragnar and Aslaug float a two-wife arrangement, Lagertha refuses, divorces Ragnar and leaves, and Bjorn chooses to go with his mother.

vikings:S02E02.title: Invasion
vikings:S02E02.summary: Four years on, Ragnar announces a new raid on England with King Horik and Jarl Borg. Siggy forces a drunk, disgraced Rollo to ask his brother for a second chance; Ragnar accepts him back but forbids him to raid. Horik then uses the same logic to drop Borg from the alliance and makes Ragnar deliver the news, leaving Borg humiliated. Siggy quietly offers Horik knowledge of Ragnar's weaknesses, and Borg tries and fails to recruit Rollo. The fleet is blown off course and lands in Wessex, where King Ecbert learns the Northmen have arrived.

vikings:S02E03.title: Treachery
vikings:S02E03.summary: Athelstan guides the raiders to the minster at Winchester and shows them the gold buried under the altar; Bishop Swithern is killed. Ecbert reveals to his court that he left Winchester unprotected on purpose to learn where the pagans would strike. Ragnar tells Ecbert's envoy that the Northmen want peace and will stay or leave depending on what the king offers. In Gotaland, Jarl Borg turns his exclusion from the raid into a public insult to his whole people and sails on Kattegat while its fighting men are away; Rollo organises a doomed defence and is told his first duty is to save Ragnar's sons. Meanwhile Lagertha's new husband, Earl Sigvard, abuses her and belittles Bjorn.

vikings:S02E04.title: Eye for an Eye
vikings:S02E04.summary: Borg declares himself ruler of Kattegat, claims Ragnar forfeited his right to rule, and puts a bounty on Ragnar's family while Rollo, Siggy and Aslaug hide in a hovel. In Wessex, Ecbert insists on an exchange of hostages before talks and meets Ragnar alone in a Roman bath, where he offers land in return for help with his ambitions. News of Borg's invasion sends Ragnar home, but Horik stays behind to deal with Ecbert, keeping Athelstan as interpreter; Ecbert learns the Northmen have split their forces. Rollo proposes a harassment campaign against Borg, Lagertha fails to persuade Sigvard to intervene, and Ecbert saves Athelstan from crucifixion. Lagertha arrives with warriors to support Ragnar.

vikings:S02E05.title: Answers in Blood
vikings:S02E05.summary: Reinforced by Lagertha, Ragnar's side still cannot storm Kattegat, so Rollo proposes destroying Borg's winter grain stores. Ragnar and Bjorn burn the grain under cover of a diversion, Borg rides out to hunt them and is beaten in open battle and flees. Ragnar retakes Kattegat. In Wessex, Ecbert makes a ruling in a nun's favour on Athelstan's account of pagan law and credits Athelstan publicly. Word arrives that the Saxons attacked Horik's camp after Ragnar left, and Lagertha announces before everyone that Bjorn will stay with his father while she returns to Sigvard.

vikings:S02E06.title: Unforgiven
vikings:S02E06.summary: Horik arrives in Kattegat, lies that Athelstan is dead and worthless, and argues that without Borg's ships the alliance cannot raid again, so Borg should be invited back. Ragnar agrees and sends Rollo, who persuades Borg that Ragnar looks beyond revenge. Siggy becomes Horik's lover and tells him she acts for Rollo's rise. Ecbert shows Athelstan hidden Roman paintings and books, makes him their secret guardian and threatens him with crucifixion if he tells anyone. When Borg arrives and swears loyalty, Ragnar houses his men in a barn, burns them at night and seizes Borg for the blood eagle.

vikings:S02E07.title: Blood Eagle
vikings:S02E07.summary: Horik persuades Ragnar to delay Borg's execution until a new ally is found. Ecbert forms an alliance with King Aelle of Northumbria against both the Northmen and the leaderless kingdom of Mercia, sealed by marrying Aethelwulf to Aelle's daughter Judith. Borg works on Horik's jealousy, telling him Ragnar wants to be king, and Horik agrees to help him escape and kill Ragnar. Floki turns sour on Ragnar and Siggy reports it to Horik, while Siggy tells Rollo to keep Horik close in case the allies fall out. A mysterious Earl Ingstad offers ships and turns out to be Lagertha, and Borg is blood-eagled.

vikings:S02E08.title: Boneless
vikings:S02E08.summary: Aslaug gives birth to Ivar, whose deformed legs lead Ragnar to want him exposed; Aslaug refuses. Lagertha, now Earl after Einar killed Sigvard for her, rejects Einar's claim to marry her. Ecbert brings Princess Kwenthrith of Mercia to Wessex and plans to back her claim with his son and Northmen mercenaries. Horik courts Floki, forms a bloc with Lagertha against Ragnar, and publicly rebukes Ragnar for sending Torstein to Ecbert without consulting him. Ecbert sends Athelstan's cross as a token and invites Ragnar to talk, but the escort under Aethelwulf is attacked.

vikings:S02E09.title: The Choice
vikings:S02E09.summary: Horik's men have killed Ecbert's envoys, and Horik overrules Ragnar's wish to negotiate. Ecbert, studying Caesar's tactics with Athelstan, hides cavalry and archers behind a ridge; Horik charges downhill and the Northmen are routed, Rollo is left for dead and captured. Ecbert chooses not to finish the Northmen off and sends Athelstan to offer peace, with King Aelle as hostage. Ragnar and Lagertha accept payment, 5,000 acres of farmland, mercenary fees for fighting for Kwenthrith, and Rollo's release; Athelstan returns with Ragnar. At home Horik approaches Floki with a proposition.

vikings:S02E10.title: The Lord's Prayer
vikings:S02E10.summary: Horik brings his wife and children to Kattegat and publicly offers Ragnar a deeper alliance through marriage while testing Floki's loyalty by asking him to kill someone who matters. Torstein's murder is announced and Horik accepts it as proof, then reveals his plan to wipe out Ragnar's whole family, asking Floki to deal with Bjorn. Horik also asks Siggy to kill Ragnar's sons in return for making her a queen. When Horik's men strike, Siggy has led the boys away, Ragnar's people are ready, and Floki reveals he only betrayed Horik. Ragnar kills Horik and takes the Sword of Kings; Horik's son Erlendur is spared.

vikings:S03E01.title: Mercenary
vikings:S03E01.summary: Ragnar, now king after Horik's death, sails back to Wessex to claim the land King Ecbert promised. Ecbert honours the treaty but adds a new condition: some of the Northmen must fight for Princess Kwenthrith to win the Mercian throne, while Lagertha and Athelstan stay behind to establish the settlement. In Hedeby, Kalf declines to sail with Lagertha, positions himself as her indispensable steward, and turns her enemy Einar into his own ally. On the river in Mercia, Ragnar sees that the two opposing armies are split by water with no bridge and throws everything at the smaller force of Kwenthrith's uncle Brihtwulf.

vikings:S03E02.title: The Wanderer
vikings:S03E02.summary: Brihtwulf is dead and Kwenthrith wants his head; her brother Burgred escapes with his advisors and his army. Ragnar interrogates a rider to find where Burgred has gone and learns the army is on a hill fort, though Rollo notes they are being drawn away from their boats. In Hedeby, Kalf is acclaimed Earl in Lagertha's absence, framing the coup as peaceful and legal. In Wessex, Lagertha works the settlement land, Ecbert courts her, and Judith confesses to Athelstan that she dreams of him. A wanderer calling himself Harbard arrives in Kattegat and asks for help.

vikings:S03E03.title: Warrior's Fate
vikings:S03E03.summary: Ecbert confronts nobles who whisper against the settlement and dares them to say he is unfit to rule, calling Kwenthrith his puppet and the Mercian alliance the real prize. Floki accuses Ragnar of fighting the Christians' war; Torstein dies and Porunn is badly wounded in the fight on the hill, and Ragnar answers Floki's blame by insisting everyone chose to come. Burgred submits and begs forgiveness. Ecbert gives the settlers a new plough and takes Lagertha and Athelstan to a Roman bath, planting the idea of Paris. In Kattegat, Harbard soothes Ivar's pain and wins Aslaug's household while two boys drown.

vikings:S03E04.title: Scarred
vikings:S03E04.summary: Kwenthrith tells Burgred that Ecbert needs a legitimate Mercian heir and so will not kill her, then at the victory feast publicly toasts their alliance and poisons him, leaving herself sole Queen of Mercia. Ragnar and Ecbert read each other openly: Ragnar says Ecbert will rule Mercia through his puppets, and both admit they are corrupt. Ecbert fails to keep Lagertha or Athelstan in Wessex. In Hedeby, Kalf reveals to Einar that he has prepared for Lagertha's return by allying with Horik's son Erlendur and Jarl Borg's widow Torvi. In Kattegat, Siggy drowns saving Ragnar's sons while Aslaug is with Harbard.

vikings:S03E05.title: The Usurper
vikings:S03E05.summary: Ragnar returns to find Siggy dead and learns about Harbard. Lagertha learns Kalf has usurped Hedeby; Ragnar refuses a civil war and instead invites Kalf and his ships to join an invasion of Frankia, leaving the earldom as a matter between Kalf and Lagertha. Kalf admits his betrayal to Lagertha and claims he desired her throughout. Ragnar announces he will attack Paris and begins gathering knowledge about it. In Wessex, Ecbert sends Aethelwulf to settle disputes at the settlement; Aethelwulf massacres the settlers, and Ecbert publicly arrests the nobles involved for treason before privately congratulating his son on the ruse.

vikings:S03E06.title: Born Again
vikings:S03E06.summary: Athelstan sketches Paris on the Seine and judges it impregnable. A survivor, Stender, brings Ragnar news of the settlement massacre; Ragnar takes the blame himself and kills Stender after confirming he has told no one else. In Wessex, Judith is punished for adultery until she names Athelstan, and Ecbert halts the punishment by recasting the child as divinely chosen, naming him Alfred. Athelstan recovers his Christian faith; Kalf arrives in Kattegat with Siegfried, Erlendur and Torvi to join the raid, and the wanderer Sinric is recruited as a guide. Floki, believing the gods demand a sacrifice, murders Athelstan, and Ragnar asks forgiveness for what he is about to do.

vikings:S03E07.title: Paris
vikings:S03E07.summary: In Paris, Emperor Charles refuses to ask his brothers for help because he wants to prove himself their superior, while Count Odo prepares the defence and courts Princess Gisla. Ecbert tells Aethelwulf he intends to overthrow King Aelle of Northumbria, possibly by assassination, and sends him to force Kwenthrith, who has killed six Wessex nobles, back into vassalage. Ragnar puts Floki in command of the attack on Paris, and a quarrelsome council agrees a two-pronged assault. Aethelwulf resists Kwenthrith's seduction and her claim that her son Magnus is Ragnar's, and forces her to sign Mercia's submission. Floki confesses to Helga that he killed Athelstan.

vikings:S03E08.title: To the Gates!
vikings:S03E08.summary: The Northmen assault Paris by land and river. Count Odo forces a bishop to bless the Oriflamme and orders no quarter, and the defenders hold the gates and cut down the scaling ladders and towers. Bjorn is badly wounded; Kalf saves Lagertha, who agrees to be with him while promising she will one day kill him. The Emperor is hailed for the victory. Floki blames himself for the disaster, and Ragnar tells Athelstan's spirit that Floki's command was a trap set by a patient man.

vikings:S03E09.title: Breaking Point
vikings:S03E09.summary: A second assault almost breaks through but fails, and the Emperor refuses to show himself to his soldiers. Paris is starving and diseased, and Odo advises coming to terms while Gisla begs her father to refuse. Ecbert extracts his reward for protecting Judith and Alfred, and deflects Aethelwulf's suspicion that he was ready to sacrifice him in Mercia. Ragnar reads the Frankish peace offer as a sign of weakness, overrules his fractious council, rejects the first sum and demands baptism at the parley.

vikings:S03E10.title: The Dead
vikings:S03E10.summary: The Franks pay the tribute and Ragnar, apparently dying, lingers. Bjorn tells the Franks his father's last wish is a Christian burial in the cathedral; the coffin is carried in by unarmed men, Ragnar rises, seizes Princess Gisla and forces the gates, and the Northmen sack the city. Only Bjorn knew the plan. Ragnar leaves Rollo to winter at the camp. Emperor Charles, abandoned by his brothers, orders Gisla to marry Rollo and offers Rollo land and a dukedom in return for defending Paris against Ragnar. Ragnar confronts Floki: 'You killed Athelstan.'

vikings:S04E01.title: A Good Treason
vikings:S04E01.summary: Ragnar lies near death after Paris while Bjorn, speaking to Kattegat in his name, publicly orders Floki's arrest for Athelstan's murder; Ragnar recovers and rebukes Bjorn for forcing his hand in public. In Hedeby, Kalf announces that he and Lagertha will share the earldom, and when Einar's family threatens to unmake him, Kalf invites everyone who wants Lagertha banished to carve a mark on a post, then has his archers kill them. In Frankia, Rollo is now a Christian duke married to Princess Gisla, and when his Viking warriors grow restless he ambushes and slaughters his own camp. Bjorn announces he will go alone into the wilderness to test himself.

vikings:S04E02.title: Kill the Queen
vikings:S04E02.summary: Floki escapes, is recaptured by Ragnar's sons, and is chained in a cave under a punishment Ragnar borrows from the myth of Loki. In Wessex, Mercian rebels have overthrown Kwenthrith, and Ecbert sends Aethelwulf to rescue her and her son Magnus, warning him that the informant known only as "W" is probably using them as bait. Ecbert woos Judith by asking what she really wants and hiring a teacher so she can learn illumination, overruling church objections. In Paris, Count Odo sounds out Rollo about the weak Emperor, while Roland has his sister Therese sleep with Odo to collect material that will discredit him.

vikings:S04E03.title: Mercy
vikings:S04E03.summary: Kalf declares his love to Lagertha and hopes for a child, while he and Erlendur send a berserker to kill Bjorn, giving the assassin King Horik's ring as a pass. Gisla demands a divorce from Rollo, and Odo, desperate to keep the Duke from leaving, buys time by promising him a language teacher. Ecbert gathers intelligence on the Paris siege from the Frankish priest Prudentius, and Judith agrees to become his mistress only after he swears to respect her as an equal. Aethelwulf brings Kwenthrith and Magnus back to Wessex, and Floki is freed by Helga after their daughter dies.

vikings:S04E04.title: Yol
vikings:S04E04.summary: Ecbert and King Aelle agree to invade Mercia to restore Kwenthrith, with Aelle openly hostile to Ragnar's son Magnus. Rollo, now able to speak Frankish, begs Gisla not to annul their marriage and wins her over. Aslaug takes Ivar to Floki and asks him to raise the boy in the old faith, while Ragnar grows close to the slave Yidu, who gives him a Chinese drug for his pain. Bjorn kills the berserker, then takes Torvi away from Erlendur; Lagertha keeps Torvi's son. Harald Finehair arrives in Kattegat and, over a game of hnefatafl with Ragnar's sons, tells Aslaug he intends to become King of all Norway.

vikings:S04E05.title: Promised
vikings:S04E05.summary: Kalf and Erlendur decide to use Torvi as their eyes in Ragnar's household by threatening her child. Harald and his brother Halfdan bring ships and men to join the new attack on Paris, and Halfdan befriends the estranged Floki. Kwenthrith identifies "W" as Wigstan and pushes the kings toward invasion, and Ecbert prays that he would sup with the Devil to gain his earthly kingdom. In Paris, Gisla suggests Rollo arrange Odo's death, and Roland takes Therese's pillow-talk evidence of Odo's imperial ambition to the Emperor. Lagertha agrees to marry Kalf and kills him at their wedding, and Hedeby acclaims her Earl.

vikings:S04E06.title: What Might Have Been
vikings:S04E06.summary: Lagertha explains that she killed Kalf to keep a promise to reclaim her earldom. Ecbert sends Alfred on pilgrimage to Rome and orders Aethelwulf to go with him, then announces he will lead the Mercian campaign himself. Yidu uses her control of Ragnar's drug to secure a place on the voyage to Paris, and Erlendur makes clear to Torvi that he owns her through her son. The Vikings sail with Harald and Halfdan, and Floki chooses his new friends over Ragnar. The Emperor begs Rollo not to change sides, while Odo tells Therese he will save Paris himself and then stage a coup. At the close, the wanderer Harbard arrives in Kattegat.

vikings:S04E07.title: The Profit and the Loss
vikings:S04E07.summary: Ragnar attacks up the Seine with boats while a land party distracts the archers in the forts, but Rollo, who designed the defences, closes the river and routs the fleet, leaving Ragnar dependent on Yidu's drug and briefly ordering a retreat. Bjorn confronts Erlendur with his father's ring and Erlendur denies it. Harbard, the wanderer who arrived at the end of the previous episode, wins Aslaug's trust. In Mercia, Ecbert meets Wigstan in the royal mausoleum, where Wigstan offers to join forces against the Ruling Council and then renounce the throne and hand Ecbert the crown of Mercia.

vikings:S04E08.title: Portage
vikings:S04E08.summary: Odo urges the Emperor to arrest Rollo, but the Emperor, already warned of Odo's ambitions, has Roland kill him during one of Odo's whipping sessions with Therese and gives Rollo full command of the realm. Ecbert returns victorious from Mercia and shows Kwenthrith sealed documents in which the dead council and Wigstan transferred her throne to him; when she tries to flee with Magnus he confines her. Ragnar camps instead of retreating and has the fleet hauled up a cliff to carry it overland past the forts. Yidu threatens to reveal Ragnar's secret about the slaughter of the Wessex settlers, and he drowns her. Kwenthrith tries to kill Ecbert and dies at Judith's hand.

vikings:S04E09.title: Death All 'Round
vikings:S04E09.summary: The Vikings drag their ships across the mountains while the Emperor rewards Roland with the title of Count and Defender of Paris and asks for Therese as his mistress; Gisla warns Rollo that proximity to her father is the real source of power. Ecbert is crowned King of Wessex and Mercia and tells Aelle that they are no longer equals. Lagertha miscarries, and Bjorn's young daughter Siggy is found drowned while Aslaug is absorbed with Harbard. Erlendur forces Torvi to swear to kill Bjorn with a crossbow, but she turns on Erlendur instead, and Ragnar, weakened by the drug, says he has come for Rollo.

vikings:S04E10.title: The Last Ship
vikings:S04E10.summary: The Viking fleet reaches Paris from upstream, and Rollo, refusing advice to break off, rallies his men to attack again and again until he defeats Ragnar in battle. At dinner the Emperor reveals that he has seen through Roland and Therese and has them killed. Years later, Bjorn returns to Kattegat with Floki and Helga planning a Mediterranean voyage, and a visitor reveals that the Wessex settlement was destroyed and that Ragnar concealed it, which turns his sons against his memory. Ragnar returns after years away and challenges anyone to kill him and take the crown; no one does.

vikings:S04E11.title: The Outsider
vikings:S04E11.summary: Years after vanishing from Kattegat, a broken Ragnar returns and offers his sword to his sons, daring any of them to kill him and take the crown; none will. He announces he is going back to England to avenge the destroyed settlement, but Bjorn has already signed up Floki, Hvitserk and King Harald for his own voyage to the Mediterranean, and Ubbe and Sigurd refuse to go. Ragnar tries to repair old bonds, confessing failure to Lagertha and saying farewell to Floki, while Ivar nearly kills the slave Margrethe to hide his impotence until she talks him down. The episode ends with Ivar forcing his father to ask him properly, and agreeing to sail to England.

vikings:S04E12.title: The Vision
vikings:S04E12.summary: Ragnar tries to recruit warriors in the market and is publicly shamed for having hidden the settlement's fate; with no one willing to follow him, he digs up his burial hoard and pays men to sail. Bjorn plans his route along the Frankish coast and decides to approach Rollo for safe passage, sending messengers to test where Rollo stands. Lagertha arrives in Kattegat for the departure feast and clashes with Aslaug, while Harald flatters Bjorn over his own designs on Norway. Margrethe confides Ivar's secret to Sigurd, and on the eve of sailing Ragnar thanks Aslaug for never turning their sons against him. Both fleets leave, and Ivar tells his brothers he is sailing to England with his father, defying Aslaug's vision that they will drown.

vikings:S04E13.title: Two Journeys
vikings:S04E13.summary: A storm wrecks Ragnar's fleet off England, leaving a handful of survivors who blame him for the disaster. Ragnar decides that only he and Ivar will go on, telling Ivar he did not come here to go back, and leads him inland toward Ecbert's villa while teaching him that his legs are a source of strength. In Frankia, Rollo detains Bjorn's party, then brings a librarian and a Roman map to show the route before offering safe passage only if he can come too. In Kattegat, with Ragnar, Bjorn, Hvitserk and Ivar gone, Lagertha moves to retake the town, using Margrethe to lure Ubbe and Sigurd away and lock them up. Ragnar arrives at Ecbert's gates and tells Ivar to act like a cripple so the Saxons will not feel threatened.

vikings:S04E14.title: In the Uncertain Hour Before the Morning
vikings:S04E14.summary: Lagertha confronts Aslaug, who gives up Kattegat in exchange for safe passage and a promise that her sons will not seek revenge; Lagertha kills her anyway and spares Ubbe and Sigurd. In Wessex, Ragnar talks his way into Ecbert's villa by claiming friendship with the king, refuses food until his son is fed, and hears Ecbert admit he ordered the massacre of the settlement as part of a larger strategy to unite England. Ragnar publicly disowns Magnus, whom Ecbert has raised as Ragnar's son, and Ecbert sends the boy away. Over wine and theology, Ragnar insists that Ecbert must kill him, then proposes a bargain: Ecbert sends Ivar home safely and hands Ragnar to King Aelle, and Ragnar will make sure his sons blame Aelle alone.

vikings:S04E15.title: All His Angels
vikings:S04E15.summary: Ragnar says goodbye to Ivar and secretly tells him to take his revenge on Ecbert, not Aelle, and to use the fact that everyone underestimates him. Ecbert agonises and then hands Ragnar over to Aelle, a Pontius Pilate move that lets another king do the killing. On the road Ragnar tells the Seer that he chose his own fate, and at Aelle's court he is tortured and thrown into a pit of snakes. Before he dies Ragnar makes a public speech about welcoming Valhalla and says the little piggies will grunt when they hear how the old boar suffered, a message aimed at his sons. Ivar reaches Kattegat, learns his mother is dead and that Lagertha now rules.

vikings:S04E16.title: Crossings
vikings:S04E16.summary: Ecbert and Aethelwulf argue over the risk of releasing Ivar, and Ecbert puts his son in charge of raising Wessex's defences. In Kattegat, Ubbe and Sigurd agree to bide their time rather than move against Lagertha, who rallies the town behind building fortifications against envious rivals. Ivar demands justice and challenges Lagertha to single combat; she refuses and he vows to kill her one day. At sea, King Harald privately muses about overthrowing the Lothbroks, and in Spain Bjorn's raid stalls when Floki refuses to let them kill worshippers in a mosque while Helga adopts an orphan girl. The episode ends with Ragnar's sons, at home and in the Mediterranean, sensing his death.

vikings:S04E17.title: The Great Army
vikings:S04E17.summary: The sons of Ragnar decide to raise the largest army ever gathered, calling in favours and promising whatever it takes to the kings and earls of the north, and Ivar declares war on the whole world. Bjorn's fleet stops in Frankia, where Rollo offers land to any northern settler and is rejected by Floki and Hvitserk. Judith travels to Northumbria to warn her father Aelle, who dismisses her and refuses an alliance with Ecbert; Ecbert teaches Alfred about kingship over wine he secretly does not drink. King Harald recruits the ambitious bastard Egil, and when Ivar tries to attack Lagertha on Bjorn's return, Bjorn stands in the way and puts the father's revenge first.

vikings:S04E18.title: Revenge
vikings:S04E18.summary: As the Great Army gathers in Kattegat, Ivar claims Ragnar chose him to lead the revenge, but the brothers back Bjorn, who announces he will command alone and refuses to share power with Harald and Halfdan. Harald confronts his old love Ellisif, now married, while Egil scouts Kattegat's defences under Harald's patronage. In Wessex, Aethelwulf confronts Ecbert over a lifetime of manipulation, and Ecbert urges Judith to return to her husband for Alfred's sake. King Aelle dismisses the Northmen's reputation as propaganda and marches out, only to be routed; the sons of Ragnar kill him with the blood eagle on the spot where their father died.

vikings:S04E19.title: On the Eve
vikings:S04E19.summary: Egil's fleet attacks Kattegat after scouting it disguised as traders, but Lagertha's defenders hold, capture Egil, and use his wife to make him confess that King Harald paid for the raid. Ecbert sends Aethelwulf to meet the heathen army and asks his son's forgiveness, while Ivar and Bjorn clash over leadership and tactics. Ivar argues for abandoning the traditional shield wall and stretching the battle across the landscape to surprise the Saxons. When the Saxons are harried on the march, Aethelwulf turns toward Repton to destroy the Viking ships, exactly as Ivar predicted, and runs into the trap.

vikings:S04E20.title: The Reckoning
vikings:S04E20.summary: The Saxons are routed and Aethelwulf flees to Ecbert, who abdicates in his son's favour, sends his family away, and stays behind with Bishop Edmund to face the army. Captured, Ecbert offers the sons of Ragnar a legal grant to East Anglia in exchange for choosing the manner of his own death, and Bjorn accepts; Ecbert takes his own life. In Kattegat, Helga dies at the hands of the girl she adopted and Floki gives himself to the gods. At the victory feast the army splits: Bjorn plans to return to the Mediterranean, Ivar calls on warriors to follow him in further raids, and when Sigurd mocks him in front of everyone, Ivar kills him with an axe.

vikings:S05E01.title: The Departed Part One
vikings:S05E01.summary: After Ivar kills Sigurd, the Great Army splinters: Bjorn sails for the Mediterranean, Floki sets off alone in a small boat, and Ivar persuades Ubbe and Hvitserk to seize York instead of settling the land Ecbert granted them. The brothers time the assault for a Christian feast day and take the town. In Wessex, a monk who witnessed the treaty tells Bishop Heahmund that Ecbert had already abdicated to Aethelwulf, so the land grant to the Northmen is worthless. Heahmund rallies the Saxons with a call for a holy war. King Harald arrives in Kattegat bearing news of the army's victory, and Lagertha immediately asks what he really came for.

vikings:S05E02.title: The Departed Part Two
vikings:S05E02.summary: Harald, now Lagertha's prisoner, explains away his earlier betrayal as love and offers alliance and marriage by listing how exposed Kattegat is; Lagertha scorns him. His men free him and he escapes, kidnapping Astrid, whom he begins to court with appeals to ambition and fate. In York, Ubbe and Hvitserk confront Ivar over his personal bodyguard and his refusal to consult them, and Ivar disarms them with talk of his disability. Aethelwulf joins Heahmund outside York, and the Saxon scouts report that the old Roman walls are crumbling and unguarded. Margrethe starts telling Ubbe that Lagertha's grip on power is slipping.

vikings:S05E03.title: Homeland
vikings:S05E03.summary: Harald brings Astrid home to his town while Ivar prepares York for the Saxon attack. The Saxons enter through the unguarded Roman walls and walk into a prepared defence; they retreat after heavy losses, and Ivar claims the victory as his strategy. Ubbe and Hvitserk go to the Saxons to negotiate a peace and land settlement; Alfred supports it but Aethelwulf rejects it on the grounds that Ecbert had no right to grant the land. Ivar uses their failure to claim leadership of the Great Army, and when Ubbe threatens to leave, the warriors and Hvitserk stay with Ivar.
